```ts
// Smoke test for web sign-in's guards (plan 6b, Task 3; spec docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-02-web-sign-in-design.md
// §3 and §5): the same-origin check on sign-in and Settings POSTs, the client address the limits count by, the
// famcal_signin flow (one use, bound to the browser, 10 minutes), the email address's one normal form (the Kelvin sign
// and other non-ASCII refused, an IDN as punycode), every email limit, and (Task 3b) Sign out / Sign out on all devices.
// (Tries per code, counted before the compare, are the code's own: smoke-signin-email.ts.)
//
// same-origin, client-address, flow, email-address, limits, the two sign-out routes, session-auth, api-auth,
// user-service and app-keys run for real. Faked at the boundaries: Prisma (in memory), Redis (in memory, with expiry
// on a clock this smoke moves, and the limits' two Lua scripts done as Redis would), the admin notifier (records),
// the rate limiter (allows), Telegram and messaging (record), error capture (records), and fetch (blocked).
// No network, no DB.
//
// Checks named [guard] pass before Task 3 and must keep passing. The others fail until it lands.
//
// Run with the fake env (scripts/ci-smokes.sh):
//   npx tsx scripts/smoke-signin-guards.ts

import path from 'path';
import crypto from 'crypto';
import { createRequire } from 'module';
import { fileURLToPath } from 'url';

// eslint-disable-next-line @typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any
type Row = Record<string, any>;

const ROOT = path.resolve(__dirname, '..');
const nodeRequire = createRequire(__filename);

// Test values, used only when the fake env left them unset. The app's origin is famcal.bot's.
process.env.TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN ||= 'test';
process.env.SESSION_SECRET ||= 'test-session-secret';
process.env.CRON_SECRET ||= 'test-cron';
process.env.ENCRYPTION_KEY ||= '0'.repeat(64);
process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL = 'https://famcal.bot';

type Result = { name: string; ok: boolean; reason?: string };
const results: Result[] = [];

async function check(name: string, fn: () => void | Promise<void>) {
  try {
    await fn();
    results.push({ name, ok: true });
  } catch (err) {
    results.push({ name, ok: false, reason: err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err) });
  }
}

function assert(cond: unknown, message: string): asserts cond {
  if (!cond) throw new Error(message);
}

const show = (value: unknown) => JSON.stringify(value, (_k, v) => (typeof v === 'bigint' ? `${v}n` : v instanceof Set ? [...v] : v));

// ---- The clock: Date.now() moves forward when a check says so (new Date() is left alone) ----

const realNow = Date.now.bind(Date);
let offsetMs = 0;
Date.now = () => realNow() + offsetMs;
const advance = (seconds: number) => { offsetMs += seconds * 1000; };
/** Sets the clock to an instant (epoch ms). */
const setClock = (ms: number) => { offsetMs = ms - realNow(); };

// ---- Fake Prisma: the user table, any other model empty ----

const DB: Record<string, Row[]> = {};
const prismaCalls: string[] = [];
function same(a: unknown, b: unknown): boolean {
  if (a instanceof Date || b instanceof Date) return a instanceof Date && b instanceof Date && a.getTime() === b.getTime();
  if (typeof a === 'bigint' || typeof b === 'bigint') return a != null && b != null && String(a) === String(b);
  return a === b;
}
const matches = (row: Row, where: Row = {}) => Object.entries(where).every(([k, v]) => v === undefined || same(row[k] ?? null, v));
function model(name: string): Row {
  const t = () => (DB[name] ??= []);
  const impl: Row = {
    findUnique: async (a: Row = {}) => t().find((r) => matches(r, a.where)) ?? null,
    findFirst: async (a: Row = {}) => t().find((r) => matches(r, a.where)) ?? null,
    findMany: async (a: Row = {}) => t().filter((r) => matches(r, a.where)),
    count: async (a: Row = {}) => t().filter((r) => matches(r, a.where)).length,
    update: async (a: Row) => {
      const row = t().find((r) => matches(r, a.where));
      if (!row) throw Object.assign(new Error(`No ${name} record was found for an update.`), { code: 'P2025' });
      Object.assign(row, a.data);
      return row;
    },
    updateMany: async (a: Row) => {
      const rows = t().filter((r) => matches(r, a.where));
      rows.forEach((r) => Object.assign(r, a.data));
      return { count: rows.length };
    },
  };
  return new Proxy(impl, {
    get: (target, prop) => {
      if (typeof prop !== 'string' || prop === 'then') return undefined;
      return (...args: unknown[]) => {
        prismaCalls.push(`${name}.${prop}`);
        return (target[prop] ?? (async () => null))(...args);
      };
    },
  });
}
const models: Record<string, Row> = {};
const fakePrisma: Row = new Proxy({} as Row, {
  get(_t, prop) {
    if (typeof prop !== 'string' || prop === 'then') return undefined;
    if (prop === '$transaction') return async (arg: unknown) => (typeof arg === 'function' ? arg(fakePrisma) : Promise.all(arg as Promise<unknown>[]));
    if (prop.startsWith('$')) return async () => undefined;
    return (models[prop] ??= model(prop));
  },
});

// ---- Fake Redis: values and sets with an expiry on the clock above; the limits' Lua scripts done as Redis does ----

type Entry = { value: string | Set<string>; expiresAt: number | null };
const store = new Map<string, Entry>();
let redisDown = false;
const live = (k: string): Entry | undefined => {
  const e = store.get(k);
  if (e && e.expiresAt !== null && e.expiresAt <= Date.now()) {
    store.delete(k);
    return undefined;
  }
  return e;
};
const decode = (e: Entry | undefined) => {
  if (!e || typeof e.value !== 'string') return null;
  try { return JSON.parse(e.value); } catch { return e.value; }
};
const encode = (v: unknown) => (typeof v === 'string' ? v : JSON.stringify(v));
const ttlOf = (k: string) => {
  const e = live(k);
  if (!e) return -2;
  return e.expiresAt === null ? -1 : Math.ceil((e.expiresAt - Date.now()) / 1000);
};
const expire = (k: string, sec: number) => { const e = live(k); if (e) e.expiresAt = Date.now() + sec * 1000; };
const incr = (k: string) => {
  const n = Number((live(k)?.value as string) ?? 0) + 1;
  store.set(k, { value: String(n), expiresAt: live(k)?.expiresAt ?? null });
  return n;
};
const redisImpl: Row = {
  get: async (k: string) => decode(live(k)),
  mget: async (...ks: unknown[]) => ks.flat().map((k) => decode(live(String(k)))),
  set: async (k: string, v: unknown, o?: Row) => {
    if (o?.nx && live(k)) return null;
    store.set(k, { value: encode(v), expiresAt: o?.ex ? Date.now() + o.ex * 1000 : null });
    return 'OK';
  },
  getdel: async (k: string) => { const e = live(k); store.delete(k); return decode(e); },
  del: async (...ks: unknown[]) => ks.flat().reduce((n: number, k) => n + (store.delete(String(k)) ? 1 : 0), 0),
  ttl: async (k: string) => ttlOf(k),
  eval: async (script: string, keys: string[], args: string[]) => {
    const [key] = keys;
    if (script.includes("'SADD'")) {
      // ADD_MEMBER_SCRIPT
      const e = live(key);
      const set = e && e.value instanceof Set ? e.value : new Set<string>();
      const added = !set.has(args[0]);
      set.add(args[0]);
      store.set(key, { value: set, expiresAt: e?.expiresAt ?? null });
      if (ttlOf(key) < 0) expire(key, Number(args[1]));
      if (added && set.size > Number(args[2])) { set.delete(args[0]); return 0; }
      return 1;
    }
    if (script.includes("'INCR'")) {
      // COUNT_SCRIPT
      const n = incr(key);
      if (ttlOf(key) < 0 || n === Number(args[1])) expire(key, Number(args[0]));
      return n;
    }
    throw new Error(`unknown script in smoke: ${script}`);
  },
};
const fakeRedis = new Proxy(redisImpl, {
  get: (t, p) => {
    if (typeof p !== 'string' || p === 'then') return undefined;
    const fn = t[p] ?? (async () => null);
    return (...args: unknown[]) => {
      if (redisDown) return Promise.reject(new Error('smoke: Redis is down'));
      return fn(...args);
    };
  },
});

// ---- Records ----

const captured: string[] = [];
const adminWarnings: { context: string; message: string }[] = [];
const sent: Row[] = [];
const logLines: string[] = [];
for (const level of ['log', 'info', 'warn', 'error'] as const) {
  const write = console[level].bind(console);
  console[level] = (...args: unknown[]) => {
    logLines.push(args.map((a) => (a instanceof Error ? a.message : String(a))).join(' '));

}

const recorder = (platform: string): Row =>

      sent.push({ platform, via: p, chatId, text });

  });

function installStubs(messagingTypes: Row) {
  const Module = nodeRequire('module');
  const stubs: Record<string, Row> = {};
  (globalThis as Row).__smokeStubs = stubs;
  if (typeof Module.registerHooks !== 'function') throw new Error('This smoke needs Node 22.15+ (module.registerHooks)');
  Module.registerHooks({
    load(url: string, context: unknown, nextLoad: (u: string, c: unknown) => unknown) {
      const file = url.startsWith('file:') ? fileURLToPath(url.split('?')[0]) : '';
      if (!(file in stubs)) return nextLoad(url, context);
      const names = Object.keys(stubs[file]).filter((n) => n !== 'default' && /^[A-Za-z_$][\w$]*$/.test(n));
      const source = [
        `const s = globalThis.__smokeStubs[${JSON.stringify(file)}];`,
        ...names.map((n) => `export const ${n} = s[${JSON.stringify(n)}];`),
        'export default (s.__esModule ? s.default : s);',
      ].join('\n');
      return { format: 'module', source, shortCircuit: true };
    },
  });
  const stub = (rel: string, exports: Row) => {
    const filename = path.join(ROOT, rel);
    stubs[filename] = exports;
    const mod = new Module(filename);

  stub('src/utils/prisma.ts', { prisma: fakePrisma, withRetry: (fn: () => unknown) => fn() });

  stub('src/services/telegram/index.ts', telegram);

function reset() {

  store.clear();
  redisDown = false;
  offsetMs = 0;
  prismaCalls.length = 0;
  captured.length = 0;

const load = (rel: string): Promise<Row> => import(path.join(ROOT, rel)).catch((err) => {

async function main() {

    const headers: Row = { ...(o.headers ?? {}) };

      assert(res && res.status === 403, `${origin}: ${res?.status}`);

    }

      '', '   ', '@gmail.com', 'dana@', 42, null, undefined, {}, ['dana@gmail.com'],
    ];
    const passed = refused.filter((input) => normalizeEmail(input) !== null).map((input) => `${show(input)} → ${normalizeEmail(input)}`);
    assert(passed.length === 0, `accepted: ${passed.join('; ')}`);
  });

  await check('#9 emailKey is a keyed hash (32 hex, one per address, changes with SESSION_SECRET, never the address or its plain sha256); maskEmail shows d•••@gmail.com', async () => {
    const { emailKey, maskEmail } = await load('src/services/web-signin/email-address.ts');
    const a = emailKey('dana@gmail.com');
    assert(/^[0-9a-f]{32}$/.test(a), `form: ${a}`);
    assert(emailKey('dana@gmail.com') === a && emailKey('tal@gmail.com') !== a, 'not one per address');
    assert(!crypto.createHash('sha256').update('dana@gmail.com').digest('hex').startsWith(a), 'a plain sha256');
    const secret = process.env.SESSION_SECRET;
    process.env.SESSION_SECRET = 'another-secret';
    const b = emailKey('dana@gmail.com');
    process.env.SESSION_SECRET = secret;
    assert(b !== a, 'the same under another SESSION_SECRET');
    assert(maskEmail('dana@gmail.com') === 'd•••@gmail.com' && maskEmail('a@x.co') === 'a•••@x.co', `mask: ${maskEmail('dana@gmail.com')}`);
  });

  // ---- The flow ----

  const flowCookieOf = (res: Response) => (res.headers.getSetCookie?.() ?? []).find((c: string) => c.startsWith('famcal_signin='));
  const oidc = (kind = 'telegram') => ({ kind, state: 'state-1', nonce: 'nonce-1', codeVerifier: 'verifier-1', locale: 'he' });
  const startOne = async (flow: Row) => {
    const { startFlow } = await load('src/services/web-signin/flow.ts');
    const res = NextResponse.json({ ok: true });
    await startFlow(res, flow);
    const header = flowCookieOf(res) ?? '';
    return { res, header, cookie: header.split(';')[0] };
  };

  await check('#10 startFlow sets famcal_signin (httpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Lax, Path=/api/auth, 10 minutes) and keeps the flow 600 s under the cookie\'s sha256, never the cookie', async () => {
    reset();
    const { header, cookie } = await startOne(oidc());
    assert(/^famcal_signin=[A-Za-z0-9_-]{43};/.test(header), `cookie: ${header}`);
    for (const flag of ['Path=/api/auth', 'Max-Age=600', 'Secure', 'HttpOnly', 'SameSite=lax']) assert(header.toLowerCase().includes(flag.toLowerCase()), `${flag} missing: ${header}`);
    const id = cookie.split('=')[1];
    const keys = [...store.keys()];
    const want = `signin:flow:${crypto.createHash('sha256').update(id).digest('hex')}`;
    assert(keys.length === 1 && keys[0] === want, `keys ${show(keys)}, want ${want}`);
    assert(!keys[0].includes(id), 'the key holds the cookie');
    assert(ttlOf(want) === 600, `ttl ${ttlOf(want)}`);
    assert(show(decode(live(want))) === show(oidc()), `record ${show(decode(live(want)))}`);
    assert(!logLines.some((l) => l.includes(id) || l.includes('state-1') || l.includes('nonce-1') || l.includes('verifier-1')), `a secret in the log: ${show(logLines)}`);
  });

  await check('#11 takeFlow is one use and bound to the browser: its own cookie gets it once; no cookie, a foreign or unknown id gets null', async () => {
    reset();
    const { takeFlow } = await load('src/services/web-signin/flow.ts');
    const mine = await startOne(oidc());
    const theirs = await startOne({ ...oidc(), state: 'their-state' });
    const at = (cookie?: string) => req('/api/auth/telegram/callback', { method: 'GET', cookie });
    assert((await takeFlow(at(), ['telegram'])) === null, 'no cookie got a flow');
    assert((await takeFlow(at(`famcal_signin=${'A'.repeat(43)}`), ['telegram'])) === null, 'an unknown id got a flow');
    assert((await takeFlow(at('famcal_signin=not-a-flow-id'), ['telegram'])) === null, 'a malformed id got a flow');
    const first = await takeFlow(at(mine.cookie), ['telegram']);
    assert(show(first) === show(oidc()), `first take ${show(first)}`);
    assert((await takeFlow(at(mine.cookie), ['telegram'])) === null, 'a second take got the flow again');
    const other = await takeFlow(at(theirs.cookie), ['telegram']);
    assert(other?.state === 'their-state', `the other browser's flow ${show(other)}`);
  });

  await check('#12 a flow brought to the wrong step is refused and left for its own step (another tab\'s sign-in of another kind still finishes: review focus RF1); an add-google flow keeps its user id', async () => {
    reset();
    const { takeFlow } = await load('src/services/web-signin/flow.ts');
    const tg = await startOne(oidc('telegram'));
    const at = (cookie: string) => req('/api/auth/google/callback', { method: 'GET', cookie });
    assert((await takeFlow(at(tg.cookie), ['google', 'add-google'])) === null, 'a telegram flow passed the google callback');
    const own = await takeFlow(at(tg.cookie), ['telegram']);
    assert(own?.kind === 'telegram', `the refused flow was used up, so its own callback finds nothing: ${show(own)}`);
    const add = await startOne({ ...oidc('add-google'), userId: 42 });
    const got = await takeFlow(at(add.cookie), ['google', 'add-google']);
    assert(got?.kind === 'add-google' && got.userId === 42, `add-google ${show(got)}`);
  });

  await check('#13 a flow is gone after 10 minutes', async () => {
    reset();
    const { takeFlow } = await load('src/services/web-signin/flow.ts');
    const { cookie } = await startOne(oidc());
    advance(601);
    assert((await takeFlow(req('/api/auth/telegram/callback', { method: 'GET', cookie }), ['telegram'])) === null, 'an 11-minute-old flow was taken');
  });

  await check('#14 peekFlow reads the email flow without using it up, and only an email flow; takeFlow then uses it up', async () => {
    reset();
    const { peekFlow, takeFlow } = await load('src/services/web-signin/flow.ts');
    const email = { kind: 'email', emailKey: 'k'.repeat(32), locale: 'ru' };
    const { cookie } = await startOne(email);
    const at = () => req('/api/auth/email/verify', { cookie });
    assert(show(await peekFlow(at(), 'email')) === show(email), 'first peek');
    assert(show(await peekFlow(at(), 'email')) === show(email), 'second peek');
    assert(show(await takeFlow(at(), ['email'])) === show(email), 'take');
    assert((await peekFlow(at(), 'email')) === null, 'a peek after the take');
    const tg = await startOne(oidc());
    assert((await peekFlow(req('/api/auth/email/verify', { cookie: tg.cookie }), 'email')) === null, 'peek returned an OIDC flow');

  await check('#15 clearFlowCookie clears famcal_signin on its own path (empty, Max-Age=0, Path=/api/auth)', async () => {
    const { clearFlowCookie } = await load('src/services/web-signin/flow.ts');

  const limits = () => load('src/services/web-signin/limits.ts');

  await check('#16 one code a minute per email: the second within the minute is refused (email-minute), the next minute passes', async () => {

    assert((await allowCodeRequest({ emailKey, ip: '203.0.113.5' })).ok === true, 'first');
    const second = await allowCodeRequest({ emailKey, ip: '203.0.113.6' });

    reset();
    const { allowCodeRequest } = await limits();

    reset();

    const bad = keys.filter((k) => !/^signin:lim:[a-z-]+:([0-9a-f]{32}|\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2})$/.test(k));
    assert(bad.length === 0, `keys: ${show(bad)}`);
    const ttls = keys.map((k) => [k, ttlOf(k)] as const).filter(([, ttl]) => ttl < 1 || ttl > 86400);
    assert(ttls.length === 0, `ttls ${show(ttls)}`);
    assert(prismaCalls.length === 0, `database: ${show(prismaCalls)}`);
    assert(logLines.some((l) => l.includes('no x-real-ip')), 'the missing address was not logged');
    assert(!logLines.some((l) => /dana|tal@|203\.0\.113/.test(l)), `an address in the log: ${show(logLines)}`);

  await check('#24 Redis failing fails closed and logged: no code request, every check blocked, no send', async () => {
    reset();
    const { allowCodeRequest, codeChecksBlocked, recordWrongCode, takeDailySend } = await limits();
    const emailKey = await keyFor('dana@gmail.com');
    redisDown = true;
    const r = await allowCodeRequest({ emailKey, ip: '203.0.113.5' });
    assert(!r.ok && r.reason === 'store-down', `request ${show(r)}`);
    assert((await codeChecksBlocked({ emailKey, ip: '203.0.113.5' })) === true, 'check not blocked');
    await recordWrongCode({ emailKey, ip: '203.0.113.5' });
    assert((await takeDailySend()) === false, 'a send with Redis down');
    assert(captured.filter((c) => c.startsWith('signin-limits')).length === 4, `captured ${show(captured)}`);
  });

  await check('#25 countWithin counts a key of the caller\'s own in one Lua call: 1, 2, 3; the window starts at the first count and the next ones don\'t renew it; the key is free after the window; a Redis failure is thrown, not swallowed', async () => {
    reset();
    const { countWithin } = await limits();
    const key = 'signin:code-tries:probe';
    const counts = [await countWithin(key, 600), await countWithin(key, 600), await countWithin(key, 600)];
    assert(show(counts) === show([1, 2, 3]), `counts ${show(counts)}`);
    assert(ttlOf(key) === 600, `ttl after the first counts ${ttlOf(key)}`);
    advance(300);
    assert((await countWithin(key, 600)) === 4, 'the fourth count');
    assert(ttlOf(key) === 300, `the window was renewed by a later count: ttl ${ttlOf(key)}`);
    advance(301);
    assert((await countWithin(key, 600)) === 1, 'the count did not start over after the window');
    redisDown = true;
    let thrown = false;
    try { await countWithin(key, 600); } catch { thrown = true; }
    assert(thrown, 'a Redis failure was swallowed');
    assert(captured.length === 0, `countWithin captured an error itself: ${show(captured)}`);
  });

  // ---- Sign out (Task 3b adds its checks here) ----

  let failed = 0;
  for (const r of results) {
    process.stdout.write(`${r.ok ? 'OK' : 'FAIL'}  ${r.name}${r.ok ? '' : ` — ${r.reason}`}\n`);
    if (!r.ok) failed++;
  }
  process.stdout.write(`\n${results.length - failed}/${results.length} passed\n`);
  process.exit(failed ? 1 : 0);
}

main().catch((err) => {
  process.stderr.write(`${err instanceof Error ? err.stack : String(err)}\n`);
  process.exit(1);
});
```

- [ ] **Step 4: Create `src/lib/same-origin.ts`**

```ts
/**
 * The guard on every sign-in and Settings POST (web sign-in spec §3): the request must come from the app's own origin
 * and send JSON. A page on another site can still make a browser POST here with its cookies (SameSite=Lax lets a
 * top-level form through), so without this someone else's sign-in could land in your browser (login CSRF), or a
 * signed-in browser could be made to sign out. A cross-site form can't set the Origin header, and it can't send
 * `application/json` without a CORS preflight, which this app never answers.
 *
 * The origin is the app's base URL (getBaseUrl), never the request's Host header, which the client writes.
 */

import { NextRequest, NextResponse } from 'next/server';
import { getBaseUrl } from '../config/urls';

/** The media type a request says it sends, lower-cased, without parameters ("application/json; charset=utf-8" → "application/json"). */
function mediaType(request: NextRequest): string {
  return (request.headers.get('content-type') ?? '').split(';')[0].trim().toLowerCase();
}

/**
 * null when the request may go on. Otherwise the answer to return at once: 403 `{ error: 'cross_site' }` when its
 * Origin is missing or not the app's, 415 `{ error: 'json_only' }` when its body is not JSON (pass `json: false` for a
 * route that takes no JSON body). Each refusal is logged with the method, the path and the reason, never a header value.
 */
export function refuseCrossSite(request: NextRequest, opts: { json?: boolean } = {}): NextResponse | null {
  const where = `${request.method} ${request.nextUrl.pathname}`;
  const origin = request.headers.get('origin');
  if (origin === null || origin !== new URL(getBaseUrl()).origin) {
    console.warn(`[same-origin] refused ${where}: ${origin === null ? 'no Origin header' : 'another Origin'}`);
    return NextResponse.json({ error: 'cross_site' }, { status: 403 });
  }
  if (opts.json !== false && mediaType(request) !== 'application/json') {
    console.warn(`[same-origin] refused ${where}: the body is not JSON`);
    return NextResponse.json({ error: 'json_only' }, { status: 415 });
  }
  return null;
}
```

- [ ] **Step 5: Create `src/services/web-signin/client-address.ts`**

```ts
/**
 * The client's address for the sign-in limits (web sign-in spec §5). It is the `x-real-ip` header Railway's edge sets,
 * as the zmanim pages' limit reads it (proxy.ts); never X-Forwarded-For, which the client can write. Before launch one
 * real request confirms that Railway overwrites a value the client sends.
 *
 * An IPv6 address counts by its /64, the block one home or phone line gets, so changing the last 64 bits buys no new
 * count. An IPv4-mapped IPv6 address (::ffff:192.0.2.7) counts as its IPv4 address. Pure: no I/O.
 */

import { isIP } from 'net';

/** The address to count by: an IPv4 address, or an IPv6 /64 written `a:b:c:d::/64`; null when the header is missing or not an address. */
export function clientAddress(request: Request): string | null {
  const raw = request.headers.get('x-real-ip')?.trim() ?? '';
  if (raw === '') return null;
  const kind = isIP(raw);
  if (kind === 4) return raw;
  if (kind === 6) return ipv6Block(raw);
  return null;
}

/** The /64 of an IPv6 address `isIP` accepted (any compression, an embedded IPv4, a %zone), or the IPv4 address it maps. */
function ipv6Block(address: string): string | null {
  const bare = address.split('%')[0].toLowerCase();
  const halves = bare.split('::');
  if (halves.length > 2) return null;
  const groupsOf = (part: string): string[] => (part === '' ? [] : part.split(':'));
  const head = groupsOf(halves[0]);
  const tail = halves.length === 2 ? groupsOf(halves[1]) : [];
  // An embedded IPv4 address (the last 32 bits written 192.0.2.7) is two groups
  const last = halves.length === 2 ? tail : head;
  if (last.length > 0 && last[last.length - 1].includes('.')) {
    const [a, b, c, d] = last.pop()!.split('.').map(Number);
    last.push(((a << 8) | b).toString(16), ((c << 8) | d).toString(16));
  }
  const gap = 8 - head.length - tail.length;
  if (halves.length === 2 ? gap < 1 : gap !== 0) return null;
  const groups = [...head, ...new Array<string>(halves.length === 2 ? gap : 0).fill('0'), ...tail].map((g) => parseInt(g, 16));
  if (groups.some((g) => !Number.isInteger(g) || g < 0 || g > 0xffff)) return null;
  if (groups.slice(0, 5).every((g) => g === 0) && groups[5] === 0xffff) {
    return [groups[6] >> 8, groups[6] & 0xff, groups[7] >> 8, groups[7] & 0xff].join('.');
  }
  return `${groups.slice(0, 4).map((g) => g.toString(16)).join(':')}::/64`;
}
```

- [ ] **Step 6: Create `src/services/web-signin/email-address.ts`**

```ts
/**
 * Email addresses for sign-in (web sign-in spec §3, "Email"): the one form an address is stored, looked up and limited
 * in, its keyed hash for Redis keys, and the masked form the chat notices show.
 *
 * An address is accepted only as ASCII after trimming; an internationalised domain is turned into punycode first.
 * Lower-casing is done on ASCII letters only, after the ASCII check: String.prototype.toLowerCase folds the Kelvin sign
 * (U+212A) into "k", and IDNA folds it, a full-width dot and others into ASCII, so "danK@gmail.com" would otherwise
 * become someone else's "dank@gmail.com". An IDN is accepted only when its punycode converts back to exactly what was
 * typed. Anything else is null, which the routes answer with the same words as any other address.
 */

import crypto from 'crypto';
import { domainToASCII, domainToUnicode } from 'url';
import { appKey } from '../../lib/app-keys';

const MAX_ADDRESS = 254;
const MAX_LOCAL = 64;
const MAX_DOMAIN = 253;
/** Printable ASCII, no space. */
const PRINTABLE_ASCII = /^[\x21-\x7e]+$/;
/** RFC 5322's dot-atom, lower case: no quoted local parts, no leading, trailing or double dot. */
const LOCAL_PART = /^[a-z0-9!#$%&'*+/=?^_`{|}~-]+(?:\.[a-z0-9!#$%&'*+/=?^_`{|}~-]+)*$/;
/** A DNS label: letters, digits and hyphens, 1 to 63, not starting or ending with a hyphen. */
const LABEL = /^(?!-)[a-z0-9-]{1,63}(?<!-)$/;
/** The top label: letters, or punycode. */
const TOP_LABEL = /^(?:[a-z]{2,63}|xn--[a-z0-9-]{1,59})$/;

/** Upper-case ASCII letters lower-cased, and nothing else touched. */
const lowerAscii = (text: string) => text.replace(/[A-Z]/g, (c) => c.toLowerCase());

/** The domain in ASCII (punycode for an IDN), lower case, or null. */
function asciiDomain(typed: string): string | null {
  if (typed.length === 0) return null;
  const lowered = lowerAscii(typed);
  let domain = lowered;
  if (!PRINTABLE_ASCII.test(lowered)) {
    domain = domainToASCII(lowered);
    if (!domain || domainToUnicode(domain) !== lowered) return null;
  }
  if (domain.length > MAX_DOMAIN) return null;
  const labels = domain.split('.');
  if (labels.length < 2 || !labels.every((label) => LABEL.test(label)) || !TOP_LABEL.test(labels[labels.length - 1])) return null;
  return domain;
}

/** The address as FamCal stores and compares it (`local@domain`, ASCII, lower case), or null for anything else. */
export function normalizeEmail(input: unknown): string | null {
  if (typeof input !== 'string') return null;
  const text = input.trim();
  if (text.length === 0 || text.length > MAX_ADDRESS) return null;
  const at = text.indexOf('@');
  if (at <= 0 || at !== text.lastIndexOf('@')) return null;
  const typedLocal = text.slice(0, at);
  // ASCII before any case folding, so no character folds into another address
  if (!PRINTABLE_ASCII.test(typedLocal)) return null;
  const local = lowerAscii(typedLocal);
  if (local.length > MAX_LOCAL || !LOCAL_PART.test(local)) return null;
  const domain = asciiDomain(text.slice(at + 1));
  if (!domain) return null;
  const address = `${local}@${domain}`;
  return address.length <= MAX_ADDRESS ? address : null;
}

/** What a sign-in hash is of: an email address, a client address, an account, or a code bound to its address. */
export type SigninHashLabel = 'email' | 'ip' | 'account' | 'code';

/**
 * HMAC-SHA256 under the 'signin' key (from SESSION_SECRET, app-keys.ts) of `<label>:<value>`, hex, 32 characters.
 * Redis keys and stored values hold this, never the address, the IP or the code. Throws when SESSION_SECRET is unset
 * (appKey reports that once): sign-in can't run without it.
 */
export function signinHash(label: SigninHashLabel, value: string): string {
  const key = appKey('signin');
  if (!key) throw new Error('SESSION_SECRET is not set: no sign-in key');
  return crypto.createHmac('sha256', key).update(`${label}:${value}`).digest('hex').slice(0, 32);
}

/** The keyed hash of a normalised address: the id its limits, codes and flows are kept under. */
export function emailKey(normalized: string): string {
  return signinHash('email', normalized);
}

/** The address as the chat notices show it: "dana@gmail.com" → "d•••@gmail.com". */
export function maskEmail(address: string): string {
  const at = address.lastIndexOf('@');
  if (at <= 0) return '•••';
  return `${address[0]}•••${address.slice(at)}`;
}
```

- [ ] **Step 7: Create `src/services/web-signin/flow.ts`**

```ts
/**
 * A sign-in's one-time checks (web sign-in spec §3): Telegram's and Google's state, nonce and PKCE verifier, and the
 * email flow's address key. They live in Redis for 10 minutes and are bound to the browser that started the sign-in
 * by the famcal_signin cookie: a random id, whose sha256 names the record, so the Redis key never holds the cookie.
 *
 * - An OIDC callback takes its record (GETDEL): used once, whatever happens next. A callback without the cookie, or
 *   whose record is gone, gets null; the route then says to start again in the browser you began in. A record of
 *   another kind is left alone (a GET, no GETDEL) and also gets null: it is this browser's newer sign-in of another
 *   way, started in another tab, and its own step still finishes it.
 * - The email flow is read (GET) on each try, since a wrong code doesn't end it; the right code takes it.
 * - The cookie is httpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Lax (Telegram and Google return with a top-level GET), path /api/auth.
 *
 * Nothing here logs the cookie, a state, a nonce, a verifier or an address key.
 */

import crypto from 'crypto';
import type { NextRequest, NextResponse } from 'next/server';
import { redis } from '../../utils/redis';
import { REDIS_KEYS } from '../../config/redis-keys';

export const SIGNIN_COOKIE_NAME = 'famcal_signin';
const FLOW_TTL_SEC = 10 * 60;
const COOKIE_OPTIONS = { httpOnly: true, secure: true, sameSite: 'lax' as const, path: '/api/auth' };
/** A flow id: 32 random bytes, base64url. Anything else in the cookie is not ours and reaches no Redis call. */
const FLOW_ID = /^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{43}$/;

export type OidcFlow = {
  kind: 'telegram' | 'google' | 'add-google';
  state: string;
  nonce: string;
  codeVerifier: string;
  locale: string;
  /** add-google only: the account the Google sign-in way is added to. */
  userId?: number;
};
export type EmailFlow = { kind: 'email'; emailKey: string; locale: string };
export type SignInFlow = OidcFlow | EmailFlow;

const recordKey = (flowId: string) => REDIS_KEYS.signinFlow(crypto.createHash('sha256').update(flowId).digest('hex'));

/** The record as a flow, or null when it isn't one (an old or foreign shape). */
function asFlow(value: unknown): SignInFlow | null {
  if (!value || typeof value !== 'object') return null;
  const v = value as Record<string, unknown>;
  if (typeof v.locale !== 'string') return null;
  if (v.kind === 'email') {
    return typeof v.emailKey === 'string' ? { kind: 'email', emailKey: v.emailKey, locale: v.locale } : null;
  }
  if (v.kind !== 'telegram' && v.kind !== 'google' && v.kind !== 'add-google') return null;
  if (typeof v.state !== 'string' || typeof v.nonce !== 'string' || typeof v.codeVerifier !== 'string') return null;
  if (v.kind === 'add-google' && typeof v.userId !== 'number') return null;
  return {
    kind: v.kind,
    state: v.state,
    nonce: v.nonce,
    codeVerifier: v.codeVerifier,
    locale: v.locale,
    ...(typeof v.userId === 'number' ? { userId: v.userId } : {}),
  };
}

/** The flow id in the request's famcal_signin cookie, or null (logged: which browser it was is the person's question). */
function flowIdOf(request: NextRequest, step: string): string | null {
  const id = request.cookies.get(SIGNIN_COOKIE_NAME)?.value;
  if (!id || !FLOW_ID.test(id)) {
    console.warn(`[signin-flow] ${step}: no famcal_signin cookie (another browser, or over 10 minutes)`);
    return null;
  }
  return id;
}

/**
 * Stores `flow` for 10 minutes under a new random id and sets that id as this response's famcal_signin cookie. A
 * second sign-in in the same browser replaces the cookie; the first record expires unused. Throws when Redis fails
 * (the route catches it and answers that sign-in failed).
 */
export async function startFlow(response: NextResponse, flow: SignInFlow): Promise<void> {
  const flowId = crypto.randomBytes(32).toString('base64url');
  await redis.set(recordKey(flowId), flow, { ex: FLOW_TTL_SEC });
  response.cookies.set(SIGNIN_COOKIE_NAME, flowId, { ...COOKIE_OPTIONS, maxAge: FLOW_TTL_SEC });
  console.info(`[signin-flow] started a ${flow.kind} sign-in${'userId' in flow && flow.userId !== undefined ? ` for user ${flow.userId}` : ''}`);
}

/**
 * Takes this browser's flow (GETDEL: used once) when it is one of `kinds`; null without the cookie, when the record
 * is gone (used, or over 10 minutes), or when it is another kind. A flow of another kind is only read (GET), never
 * used up: the browser's latest sign-in may be another way's, started in a second tab, and it must still finish there
 * (review focus RF1). Only a flow of a matching kind is then taken, so it is still used once.
 */
export async function takeFlow(request: NextRequest, kinds: SignInFlow['kind'][]): Promise<SignInFlow | null> {
  const step = kinds.join('/');
  const flowId = flowIdOf(request, step);
  if (!flowId) return null;
  const key = recordKey(flowId);
  const seen = asFlow(await redis.get(key));
  if (seen && !kinds.includes(seen.kind)) {
    console.warn(`[signin-flow] ${step}: the cookie's sign-in is a ${seen.kind} one; refused and left for its own step`);
    return null;
  }
  const flow = seen ? asFlow(await redis.getdel(key)) : null;
  if (!flow || !kinds.includes(flow.kind)) {
    console.warn(`[signin-flow] ${step}: no sign-in under the cookie (used, or over 10 minutes)`);
    return null;
  }
  return flow;
}

/** Reads this browser's email flow without using it up (GET): a wrong code leaves it for the next try. */
export async function peekFlow(request: NextRequest, kind: 'email'): Promise<EmailFlow | null> {
  const flowId = flowIdOf(request, kind);
  if (!flowId) return null;
  const flow = asFlow(await redis.get(recordKey(flowId)));
  if (!flow || flow.kind !== kind) {
    console.warn(`[signin-flow] ${kind}: no email sign-in under the cookie (used, or over 10 minutes)`);
    return null;
  }
  return flow;
}

/** Clears the famcal_signin cookie (same path and flags, Max-Age 0), once a flow is finished or refused. */
export function clearFlowCookie(response: NextResponse): void {
  response.cookies.set(SIGNIN_COOKIE_NAME, '', { ...COOKIE_OPTIONS, maxAge: 0 });
}
```

- [ ] **Step 8: Create `src/services/web-signin/limits.ts`**

The two Lua scripts are the only place a count and its expiry are set. The smoke's fake Redis does exactly what they do: `INCR`, then `EXPIRE` when `TTL < 0` or when the count reaches the restart point; for the set, `SADD`, `EXPIRE` when `TTL < 0`, then `SREM` and refuse a new member past the cap. Review the scripts line by line against those three sentences.

```ts
/**
 * The email sign-in limits (web sign-in spec §5), all in Upstash, before any database lookup, and counted the same for
 * an address no account has, so the answers and their timing say nothing about who has an account.
 *
 * | What                               | Limit                                                       |
 * |------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------|
 * | Codes to one email                 | 1 a minute, 5 a day                                         |
 * | Code requests from one address     | 20 an hour                                                  |
 * | Add-email codes per account        | 3 addresses a day                                           |
 * | Wrong codes for one email          | 10 a day, then email sign-in for it pauses for a day        |
 * | Wrong codes from one address       | 20 an hour                                                  |
 * | All codes sent                     | 90 a UTC day (Resend allows 100), then one admin message    |
 *
 * (Tries per code, 5 then void, are counted by email-code.ts through countWithin below.)
 *
 * - Keys are `signin:lim:<what>:<keyed hash>` (signinHash: the email's key, the address's, the account's), never an
 *   address, an IP or a user id in clear, and each expires within a day. The day's budget is keyed by its UTC date and
 *   expires at the next 00:00 UTC.
 * - A count and its expiry are set in one Lua call, so no key is ever left without one. A count past its limit is
 *   still counted (an attacker's flood doesn't reset anything).
 * - Redis failing fails closed: no code is sent or checked, and the failure is logged.
 * - An address is clientAddress() (x-real-ip, IPv6 by /64). Without one, requests count under one shared key, logged
 *   once per process (a sign that Railway stopped setting the header).
 */

import { redis } from '../../utils/redis';
import { REDIS_KEYS } from '../../config/redis-keys';
import { captureError } from '../../lib/error-capture';
import { signinHash } from './email-address';

export type LimitReason =
  | 'email-minute'
  | 'email-day'
  | 'ip-hour'
  | 'account-day'
  | 'wrong-email-day'
  | 'wrong-ip-hour'
  | 'daily-budget'
  | 'store-down';

const MINUTE_SEC = 60;
const HOUR_SEC = 60 * 60;
const DAY_SEC = 24 * 60 * 60;
const DAY_MS = DAY_SEC * 1000;

const LIMIT = {
  codesPerEmailDay: 5,
  codeRequestsPerAddressHour: 20,
  addAddressesPerAccountDay: 3,
  wrongCodesPerEmailDay: 10,
  wrongCodesPerAddressHour: 20,
  codesSentPerDay: 90,
} as const;

/**
 * INCR KEYS[1] and return the count; set its expiry (ARGV[1] seconds) when it has none, and again when the count
 * reaches ARGV[2] (when > 0), so the pause after a limit is a whole window.
 */
const COUNT_SCRIPT =
  "local n = redis.call('INCR', KEYS[1]) if redis.call('TTL', KEYS[1]) < 0 or n == tonumber(ARGV[2]) then redis.call('EXPIRE', KEYS[1], ARGV[1]) end return n";
/**
 * SADD ARGV[1] to the set KEYS[1], with its expiry (ARGV[2] seconds) when it has none. A new member past ARGV[3]
 * members is taken out again and refused (0); otherwise 1. A member already in the set always passes.
 */
const ADD_MEMBER_SCRIPT =
  "local added = redis.call('SADD', KEYS[1], ARGV[1]) if redis.call('TTL', KEYS[1]) < 0 then redis.call('EXPIRE', KEYS[1], ARGV[2]) end if added == 1 and redis.call('SCARD', KEYS[1]) > tonumber(ARGV[3]) then redis.call('SREM', KEYS[1], ARGV[1]) return 0 end return 1";

/** The key every request without a client address shares. */
const NO_ADDRESS = 'none';

const limitKey = (what: string, id: string) => REDIS_KEYS.signinLimit(what, id);

/** The address's hash, the shared one without an address (said once per process, on globalThis: Next 16 bundles). */
function addressId(ip: string | null): string {
  if (ip === null) {
    const g = globalThis as { __famcalSigninNoAddressWarned?: boolean };
    if (!g.__famcalSigninNoAddressWarned) {
      g.__famcalSigninNoAddressWarned = true;
      console.warn('[signin-limits] a request came with no x-real-ip: requests without one share one count');
    }
  }
  return signinHash('ip', ip ?? NO_ADDRESS);
}

async function count(key: string, windowSec: number, restartAt = 0): Promise<number> {
  return Number(await redis.eval(COUNT_SCRIPT, [key], [String(windowSec), String(restartAt)]));
}

/**
 * Counts one more on `key` and returns the count: the first count gives the key `windowSec` seconds to live, the next
 * ones don't renew it. One Lua call, so a crash between an INCR and an EXPIRE can't leave a counter that never ends.
 * For a count that is not one of the limits above (Task 5's tries per code). A Redis failure is thrown: the caller
 * decides what a failed count means.
 */
export async function countWithin(key: string, windowSec: number): Promise<number> {
  return count(key, windowSec);
}

/** The day's budget: its key (the UTC date) and the seconds to the next 00:00 UTC. */
function budget(nowMs: number): { key: string; ttlSec: number } {
  const day = new Date(nowMs).toISOString().slice(0, 10);
  const nextMidnight = (Math.floor(nowMs / DAY_MS) + 1) * DAY_MS;
  return { key: limitKey('daily-send', day), ttlSec: Math.max(1, Math.ceil((nextMidnight - nowMs) / 1000)) };
}

function refused(step: string, reason: LimitReason, userId?: number): { ok: false; reason: LimitReason } {
  console.info(`[signin-limits] ${step} refused: ${reason}${userId !== undefined ? ` (user ${userId})` : ''}`);
  return { ok: false, reason };
}

/**
 * May a code be mailed for this address? Counts the request: the address's 20 an hour, then the email's 1 a minute
 * and 5 a day, then (Add email, `addForUserId`) the account's 3 addresses a day. Refused first, without counting, when
 * the day's 90 are sent or the email is paused for wrong codes. Runs for every request, whether or not an account has
 * the address.
 */
export async function allowCodeRequest(args: {
  emailKey: string;
  ip: string | null;
  addForUserId?: number;
}): Promise<{ ok: true } | { ok: false; reason: LimitReason }> {
  const step = args.addForUserId !== undefined ? 'add-email code request' : 'code request';
  try {
    const [sent, wrong] = await redis.mget<(number | string | null)[]>(
      budget(Date.now()).key,
      limitKey('wrong-email-day', args.emailKey),
    );
    if (Number(sent ?? 0) >= LIMIT.codesSentPerDay) return refused(step, 'daily-budget', args.addForUserId);
    if (Number(wrong ?? 0) >= LIMIT.wrongCodesPerEmailDay) return refused(step, 'wrong-email-day', args.addForUserId);
    if ((await count(limitKey('ip-hour', addressId(args.ip)), HOUR_SEC)) > LIMIT.codeRequestsPerAddressHour) {
      return refused(step, 'ip-hour', args.addForUserId);
    }
    const firstThisMinute = await redis.set(limitKey('email-minute', args.emailKey), 1, { nx: true, ex: MINUTE_SEC });
    if (firstThisMinute === null) return refused(step, 'email-minute', args.addForUserId);
    if ((await count(limitKey('email-day', args.emailKey), DAY_SEC)) > LIMIT.codesPerEmailDay) {
      return refused(step, 'email-day', args.addForUserId);
    }
    if (args.addForUserId !== undefined) {
      const accountKey = limitKey('account-day', signinHash('account', String(args.addForUserId)));
      const allowed = Number(await redis.eval(ADD_MEMBER_SCRIPT, [accountKey], [args.emailKey, String(DAY_SEC), String(LIMIT.addAddressesPerAccountDay)]));
      if (allowed !== 1) return refused(step, 'account-day', args.addForUserId);
    }
    return { ok: true };
  } catch (error) {
    captureError(error, 'signin-limits', { step, ...(args.addForUserId !== undefined ? { user_id: args.addForUserId } : {}) });
    return { ok: false, reason: 'store-down' };
  }
}

/** Is checking a code paused here: 10 wrong codes for this email today, or 20 from this address this hour? Fails closed. */
export async function codeChecksBlocked(args: { emailKey: string; ip: string | null }): Promise<boolean> {
  try {
    const [forEmail, fromAddress] = await redis.mget<(number | string | null)[]>(
      limitKey('wrong-email-day', args.emailKey),
      limitKey('wrong-ip-hour', addressId(args.ip)),
    );
    if (Number(forEmail ?? 0) >= LIMIT.wrongCodesPerEmailDay) {
      console.info('[signin-limits] code check refused: wrong-email-day');
      return true;
    }
    if (Number(fromAddress ?? 0) >= LIMIT.wrongCodesPerAddressHour) {
      console.info('[signin-limits] code check refused: wrong-ip-hour');
      return true;
    }
    return false;
  } catch (error) {
    captureError(error, 'signin-limits', { step: 'code check' });
    return true;
  }
}

/** Counts a wrong (or expired) code for this email (a day, restarted at the 10th) and from this address (an hour). */
export async function recordWrongCode(args: { emailKey: string; ip: string | null }): Promise<void> {
  try {
    await count(limitKey('wrong-email-day', args.emailKey), DAY_SEC, LIMIT.wrongCodesPerEmailDay);
    await count(limitKey('wrong-ip-hour', addressId(args.ip)), HOUR_SEC);
  } catch (error) {
    captureError(error, 'signin-limits', { step: 'wrong code' });
  }
}

/** The one admin message when the day's budget is spent. */
async function tellAdminBudgetSpent(): Promise<void> {
  try {
    const { notifyAdminWarning } = await import('../../utils/error-notifier');
    await notifyAdminWarning(
      'signin-email-budget',
      `Email sign-in sent its ${LIMIT.codesSentPerDay} codes for today (UTC), and pauses until 00:00 UTC. Resend's free plan allows 100 a day.`,
    );
  } catch (error) {
    captureError(error, 'signin-email-budget-alert', {}, 'warning');
  }
}

/**
 * Takes one send from the UTC day's 90. true: send. false: the day's codes are spent (or Redis failed), so no mail.
 * The send that spends the 90th tells the admin, once a day.
 */
export async function takeDailySend(): Promise<boolean> {
  const { key, ttlSec } = budget(Date.now());
  try {
    const sent = await count(key, ttlSec);
    if (sent === LIMIT.codesSentPerDay) await tellAdminBudgetSpent();
    if (sent > LIMIT.codesSentPerDay) {
      console.warn(`[signin-limits] the day's ${LIMIT.codesSentPerDay} sign-in emails are sent: no more until 00:00 UTC`);
      return false;
    }
    return true;
  } catch (error) {
    captureError(error, 'signin-limits', { step: 'daily send' });
    return false;
  }
}
```

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes:
  - `refuseCrossSite` (3a);
  - `readSession`, `clearSessionCookie`, `createSessionToken(userId, method, signedInAt)`, `SESSION_COOKIE_NAME` (Task 2);

- Produces:

  - `POST /api/auth/signout-all?user_id=` (body `{ initData? }`, or `{ user_id, initData? }`): Origin + JSON, then `verifyUserAuth`; sets `sessionsValidAfter = now`; answers `{ ok: true }` and clears this browser's cookie. It answers 400 `{ error: 'bad_request' }` for a body that is not JSON, 500 `{ error: 'failed' }` when the write fails, and otherwise `verifyUserAuth`'s own 400/401/403/404/429.

```ts
/** Valid Telegram initData for a Telegram user id, signed with the bot token. */
function initDataFor(tgId: number): string {
  const params: Record<string, string> = {
    auth_date: String(Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000)),
    query_id: 'AAH-smoke',
    user: JSON.stringify({ id: tgId, first_name: 'Test' }),
  };
  const checkString = Object.keys(params).sort().map((k) => `${k}=${params[k]}`).join('\n');
  const secret = crypto.createHmac('sha256', 'WebAppData').update(process.env.TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN ?? '').digest();
  const hash = crypto.createHmac('sha256', secret).update(checkString).digest('hex');
  return [...Object.entries(params), ['hash', hash]].map(([k, v]) => `${k}=${encodeURIComponent(v)}`).join('&');
}
```

- [ ] **Step 3: Create `app/api/auth/signout/route.ts`**

```ts
// POST /api/auth/signout: sign out on this device (web sign-in spec §2.4, §4). Clears this browser's session cookie.
// Origin and JSON are checked (same-origin.ts), so another site can't sign you out. No account read, no database query.

import { NextRequest, NextResponse } from 'next/server';
import { refuseCrossSite } from '@/src/lib/same-origin';
import { clearSessionCookie, readSession } from '@/src/lib/session-auth';

export async function POST(request: NextRequest) {
  const refused = refuseCrossSite(request);
  if (refused) return refused;
  const session = readSession(request);
  console.info(`[signout] ${session ? `user ${session.userId} (${session.method})` : 'a browser without a valid session'} signed out on this device`);
  const response = NextResponse.json({ ok: true });
  clearSessionCookie(response);
  return response;
}
```

- [ ] **Step 4: Create `app/api/auth/signout-all/route.ts`**

```ts
// POST /api/auth/signout-all?user_id=: sign out on all devices (web sign-in spec §2.13, §4). Sets the account's
// sessionsValidAfter to now, so every session cookie signed in before it is refused on its next request, and clears
// this browser's cookie. From the web app (the cookie) and the Mini App (initData, which this doesn't end).
// Origin and JSON are checked first (same-origin.ts). user_id comes from the query, as on every user route; the
// contract's body `user_id` is read when the query has none.

import { NextRequest, NextResponse } from 'next/server';
import { refuseCrossSite } from '@/src/lib/same-origin';
import { verifyUserAuth } from '@/src/lib/api-auth';
import { requestInitData } from '@/src/lib/request-init-data';
import { settingsRateLimiter } from '@/src/lib/rate-limit';
import { clearSessionCookie } from '@/src/lib/session-auth';
import { updateUserById } from '@/src/services/user-service';
import { captureError } from '@/src/lib/error-capture';

export async function POST(request: NextRequest) {
  const refused = refuseCrossSite(request);
  if (refused) return refused;

  let body: Record<string, unknown> = {};
  try {
    const parsed: unknown = await request.json();
    if (parsed && typeof parsed === 'object' && !Array.isArray(parsed)) body = parsed as Record<string, unknown>;
  } catch {
    // Not the error's message: V8 quotes the start of the text it couldn't parse
    console.warn('[signout-all] refused: the body is not JSON');
    return NextResponse.json({ error: 'bad_request' }, { status: 400 });
  }

  const userId = request.nextUrl.searchParams.get('user_id')
    ?? (typeof body.user_id === 'string' || typeof body.user_id === 'number' ? String(body.user_id) : null);
  const auth = await verifyUserAuth(request, userId, requestInitData(request, body), settingsRateLimiter, 'signout-all');
  if (!auth.success) return auth.response;

  try {
    await updateUserById(auth.user.id, { sessionsValidAfter: new Date() });
  } catch (error) {
    captureError(error, 'signout-all', { user_id: auth.user.id });
    return NextResponse.json({ error: 'failed' }, { status: 500 });
  }
  console.info(`[signout-all] user ${auth.user.id} ended every web session (${auth.via})`);
  const response = NextResponse.json({ ok: true });
  clearSessionCookie(response);
  return response;
}
```

```ts
    const events = envelopes.flatMap((envelope) => (envelope[1] as Row[][]).filter((item) => item[0].type === 'event').map((item) => item[1] as Row));
    const signin = events.find((event) => event.exception?.values?.[0]?.value === 'smoke: a sign-in route failed');
    assert(signin, `no sign-in error event: ${events.length} events`);
    // Without the stack frames: their context lines are this file's own source
    const text = show({ ...signin, exception: { values: (signin.exception.values as Row[]).map(({ stacktrace: _frames, ...rest }) => rest) } });
    const found = [['the email', SIGNIN.email], ['the email (encoded)', encodeURIComponent(SIGNIN.email)], ['the OAuth code', SIGNIN.code], ['the state', SIGNIN.state], ['the email code', `"code":"${SIGNIN.otp}"`]]
      .filter(([, secret]) => text.includes(secret)).map(([name]) => name);
    assert(found.length === 0, `in the event: ${found.join(', ')}: ${text.slice(0, 600)}`);
    assert(String(signin.request?.url ?? '').includes('/signin-fails?user_id=9&code=[scrubbed]'), `request.url ${signin.request?.url}`);
  });

  let failed = 0;
```

The search leaves out the event's stack frames, because Sentry's context lines quote this file's own source. In this harness the SDK does not attach the POST body to the event. So #3 pins what does reach it (the URL, the query, the Next request path), and #13 pins the body scrub directly.

```ts
function withoutInitData(body: Dict): Dict {
  const rest = { ...body };
  delete rest.initData;
  return rest;

function scrubBody(data: unknown): unknown {
  if (typeof data === 'string') {
    try {
      const parsed: unknown = JSON.parse(data);
      if (parsed && typeof parsed === 'object' && !Array.isArray(parsed)) {
        if (!('initData' in parsed)) return data;
        return JSON.stringify(withoutInitData(parsed as Dict));

  if (data && typeof data === 'object' && !Array.isArray(data) && 'initData' in data) {
```

```ts
  return Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(body).filter(([name]) => !isSecretField(name)));
```

### Open questions (for the controller, not the owner)

1. **No client address.** A request with no `x-real-ip` counts under one shared key, which fails closed: 20 code requests an hour for all such requests together, logged once per process. If Railway ever drops the header, email sign-in slows for everyone rather than going unlimited. The spec's pre-launch check (one real request) settles it.
2. **What the request route answers on a limit** (Task 5). The limits return a reason. The spec says the screen always shows the same words, so Task 5 should answer `{ ok: true }` for every reason except possibly `'daily-budget'` and `'store-down'`. Neither reveals whether an account has the address, so an "email sign-in is paused, try later" line would be honest there. That is Task 5's and Task 8's choice, and needs `site.signin.*` strings if taken.

## Part C: Task 4, Telegram and Google sign-in (OpenID Connect)

Spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-02-web-sign-in-design.md` §2.3, §3, §8 "Flows". Contract: `plan/contract.md`, section "OIDC".

Verified while drafting (outside the repo, nothing in it changed): openid-client 6.8.8 was installed in a scratch folder, and every file below plus the smoke ran in a scratch copy of the repo, with stand-ins for the Task 2 and Task 3 functions written to the contract. Results of that run: the 29 original checks passed (they are #1-#25 and #28-#31 below); `tsc` and `eslint` reported nothing for these files (the only `tsc` errors were `prisma.signInIdentity` before Task 1's client exists); the existing smokes that scan the tree (`smoke-dst`, `smoke-pause`, `smoke-alerts-gate-writers`, `smoke-console-scrub`, `smoke-fetch-retry`, `smoke-google-retry`, `smoke-fail-closed` #12) still pass. Three changes were each reverted after checking that the smoke catches them: logging the state (caught by #31), dropping `expectedNonce` (#15), and dropping `enableNonRepudiationChecks` (#17: without it, a token signed with a key the provider never published was accepted).

The fix pass after the cross-check changed four things that have not been run yet (Step 9 is their first run; Step 10 shows each guard failing without its code): the state-mismatch answer now keeps the browser's current flow (#10, new #26), the callback answers a provider's `?error=` (new #27), the smoke runner is `run-smoke.sh`, and the Google callback is written in the form Task 6 extends. The final cross-part pass changed three more, also not run: #4 expects the English landing unprefixed (`/dashboard?user_id=9`, part A's `appPageUrl`), and the callback that finds no flow of its kind leaves the cookie alone, with #13 now finishing the other tab's Google sign-in (note 11).

### Contract notes

1. **`User` means `UserConfig`.** In `finishSignIn(user: User, …)`, `findUserByIdentity(): Promise<User | null>` and `resolveGoogleSignIn(): { user: User }`, `User` is `UserConfig` from `src/types.ts`. That is what `getUserByTelegramId`, `getUserById` and `verifyUserAuth` already return. `findUserByIdentity` returns `convertPrismaUserToConfig(identity.user)`, so Task 2's `finishSignIn` must take a `UserConfig`, and `UserConfig.telegramId` is a `number` there.
2. **The nonce is required from both providers (ruling R6, kept).** The spec (§3) says "The nonce is checked when Telegram returns it", but openid-client cannot check a nonce only when one is present: with `expectedNonce` set, a token without one is refused, and without it, a token that has one is refused. Telegram's documentation (core.telegram.org/bots/telegram-login) lists `nonce` as an optional request parameter "to be included in the resulting id_token", and we always send one. If a live Telegram token has none, the sign-in is refused and the log line reads `JWT "nonce" (nonce) claim missing`, so the first live sign-in still records whether Telegram returns it. If it doesn't, Claude drops `expectedNonce` for Telegram only (one line in `oidc.ts`; state and PKCE still bind the browser). That is Claude's own post-launch check (part H, Task 11c), not an owner decision. The decision is recorded in a comment above `finishAuthorization` in `oidc.ts`.
3. **The client secret goes in the form (`client_secret_post`), not in a Basic header.** Following RFC 6749, openid-client's `ClientSecretBasic` form-encodes the id and secret before base64 (`-` becomes `%2D`). A server that doesn't decode them refuses, which is what the first draft of this smoke's token endpoint did. Both providers list `client_secret_post`.
4. **openid-client's own 30 s timeout is turned off.** Every request gets `AbortSignal.timeout(30 s)` from openid-client. `repoFetch` doesn't pass `signal` on, and `config.timeout = 0` stops the signal being made after discovery (CLAUDE.md: no timeout of our own). Smoke #28 asserts that no request reaches fetch with a signal.
5. **customFetch's signature differs from the repo's.** openid-client calls `(url: string, options: CustomFetchOptions) => Promise<Response>`, where `options` holds `body`, `headers: Record<string,string>`, `method`, `redirect: 'manual'` and `signal?`. `googleFetch` and `fetchWithRetry` take `(url: string, init: RequestInit)`, so `repoFetch` adapts between them. It casts `body` to `BodyInit` because TS 5.9's `BufferSource` doesn't accept openid-client's `Uint8Array` type. `fetchWithRetry` throws `HttpStatusError` on a 4xx, which openid-client wraps as `ClientError: something went wrong` with the error as its `cause`. `describeOidcError` unwraps it, so a refused Telegram exchange logs as `HTTP 400`.
6. **This task exports more than the contract lists:**
   - `oidc.ts`: `newOidcChecks()`, `redirectUri(provider)`, `describeOidcError(error)` and `__resetOidcForTests()`.
   - A new file, `oidc-route.ts`: `requestLocale`, `startOidcSignIn` and `handleOidcCallback`.
   - `google-signin.ts`: the type `GoogleSignInResult`.
   - What Task 6 does with them:
     - `add-start` uses `newOidcChecks()` (the only generator of state, nonce and PKCE verifier; Task 6 defines no second one) + `authorizationUrl('google', …)` + `startFlow(…, { kind: 'add-google', …, userId })`.
     - Task 6 does not write a second Google callback. It replaces the `GET` in `app/api/auth/google/callback/route.ts` with the same call to `handleOidcCallback`, whose inner callback is Step 8's, plus exactly two changes: `kinds` becomes `['google', 'add-google']`, and one line `if (flow.kind === 'add-google') return finishAddGoogle(flow, claims);` goes right after the verified-address check. Both error paths (a refused exchange, the provider's `?error=`) stay in `handleOidcCallback`, so there is one place that reports a callback failure to Sentry and it never reads the error's `cause`.
     - Task 7 replaces the one marked comment in `resolveGoogleSignIn`.
7. **Where `email_verified` is enforced.** The Google callback refuses an unverified email first, before any lookup, so the refusal covers every Google flow kind. `finishAuthorization` passes the flag through as the contract's `GoogleClaims` has it, and `emailVerified` is false whenever there is no email.
8. **A misconfigured Google client stays off.** If `GOOGLE_SIGNIN_CLIENT_ID` equals `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID`, `providerConfigured('google')` is false and the process warns once. A calendar-client token must never sign anyone in (spec §3).
9. **This task depends on the Sentry scrubber.** The callbacks call `captureError` inside a request whose URL has `code` and `state` in its query. The spec's leak work (§8 "Leaks": the scrubber drops `code`, `state`, `token`, `id_token` and `email` from URLs) has to ship in the same push. Everything ships in one push at the end, so nothing reaches prod without it.
10. **No user-facing strings in this task.** Every outcome is a `status` on `/signin`, and the UI tasks word it.
11. **A second sign-in started in the same browser (review focus RF1).** `startFlow` replaces the `famcal_signin` cookie, so when tab 1's provider answer arrives, the browser sends tab 2's cookie and `takeFlow` returns tab 2's flow (and uses it up, GETDEL, before the state can be compared). The state differs, so tab 1 lands on `/signin?status=restart` and signs nobody in. If that were all, tab 2's own answer would then find no flow. So on a state mismatch `handleOidcCallback` puts the flow it just took back with `startFlow(response, flow)` (the same state, nonce and verifier under a new flow id, and the new cookie on the restart answer), and tab 2 still signs in. The state stays one use: the kept flow is used up by its own callback. A forged or stale callback therefore cannot end a sign-in the person is in the middle of (it could before: the mismatch used the flow up). Smoke #10 (the old id is used up, the flow is kept under a new one) and #26 (two tabs, both providers). Two tabs on two different ways (Telegram in one, Google or an email code in the other) are the other half: Task 3's `takeFlow` only reads a flow of another kind (it never uses it up), and the callback leaves the cookie alone when it finds no flow of its kind, so the other tab's sign-in still finishes. Smoke #13 (a Telegram answer under a Google sign-in's cookie, then that Google sign-in finishing).
12. **A provider's `?error=` (cancelled, refused, unavailable).** After the state check (RFC 6749 has the provider echo `state` on an error answer; one that leaves it out gets `restart`, which is also right), the callback goes back to the plain `/signin` page (no status; the person chose not to continue) and logs `[signin] <provider> came back without a code (<error word>)`; the word is logged only when it is a lowercase OAuth error word (`access_denied`), else as `unrecognised`, so a crafted link puts no text in the log. It is not an error, so nothing goes to Sentry. Without this branch openid-client would throw on the `error` parameter and the person would land on "Something went wrong". Smoke #27.

### Open questions

- Settled by the controller (R13): Google gets `prompt=select_account`, so on a browser with several Google accounts signed in the person picks one instead of Google taking the last used (#3 pins it).
- The four new variables (`TELEGRAM_LOGIN_CLIENT_ID`, `TELEGRAM_LOGIN_CLIENT_SECRET`, `GOOGLE_SIGNIN_CLIENT_ID`, `GOOGLE_SIGNIN_CLIENT_SECRET`) also go in the startup checks (warn only) and the README table (spec §6.4). That isn't in this task, so another part has to own it. Both secret names match the console scrubber's `SECRET` pattern.
- Live check: openid-client compares `iss` exactly with the discovered issuer, `https://accounts.google.com`. Google's docs allow `accounts.google.com` without `https://`. Code-flow tokens carry the `https` form, but the first live Google sign-in confirms it.

```ts
type Result = { name: string; ok: boolean; reason?: string };

async function check(name: string, fn: () => void | Promise<void>) {

// ---- Fake Prisma: in-memory tables, compound unique keys, `include` of a `<name>Id` relation ----

const DB: Record<string, Row[]> = {};
const num = (x: unknown) => (x instanceof Date ? x.getTime() : Number(x));
function same(a: unknown, b: unknown): boolean {
  if (a instanceof Date || b instanceof Date) return a instanceof Date && b instanceof Date && a.getTime() === b.getTime();
  if (typeof a === 'bigint' || typeof b === 'bigint') return a != null && b != null && String(a) === String(b);
  return a === b;
}
const isPlain = (v: unknown): v is Row => v !== null && typeof v === 'object' && !(v instanceof Date) && !Array.isArray(v);

function matches(row: Row, where?: Row): boolean {
  if (!where) return true;
  return Object.entries(where).every(([k, cond]) => {
    if (cond === undefined) return true;
    if (k === 'AND') return ([] as Row[]).concat(cond).every(c => matches(row, c));
    if (k === 'OR') return (cond as Row[]).some(c => matches(row, c));
    if (k === 'NOT') return !([] as Row[]).concat(cond).some(c => matches(row, c));
    // A compound unique key (kind_subject: { kind, subject }) names no column of its own.
    if (isPlain(cond) && !(k in row) && k.includes('_')) return matches(row, cond);
    const v = row[k];
    if (isPlain(cond)) {
      if ('equals' in cond && !same(v ?? null, cond.equals)) return false;
      if ('in' in cond && !(cond.in as unknown[]).some(x => same(v, x))) return false;
      if ('not' in cond && same(v ?? null, cond.not)) return false;
      if ('lt' in cond && !(v != null && num(v) < num(cond.lt))) return false;
      if ('gt' in cond && !(v != null && num(v) > num(cond.gt))) return false;
      return true;
    }
    return same(v ?? null, cond);
  });
}

function shape(name: string, row: Row | undefined, a: Row = {}): Row | null {
  if (!row) return null;
  const out: Row = a.select ? Object.fromEntries(Object.keys(a.select).filter(k => a.select[k]).map(k => [k, row[k]])) : { ...row };
  for (const [rel, on] of Object.entries(a.include ?? {})) {
    if (on) out[rel] = { ...(DB[rel] ?? []).find(r => same(r.id, row[`${rel}Id`])) };
  }
  return out;
}

const prismaCalls: string[] = [];
function model(name: string): Row {
  const t = () => (DB[name] ??= []);
  const impl: Row = {
    findUnique: async (a: Row = {}) => shape(name, t().find(r => matches(r, a.where)), a),
    findFirst: async (a: Row = {}) => shape(name, t().find(r => matches(r, a.where)), a),
    findMany: async (a: Row = {}) => t().filter(r => matches(r, a.where)).map(r => shape(name, r, a)),
    count: async (a: Row = {}) => t().filter(r => matches(r, a.where)).length,
    update: async (a: Row) => {
      const row = t().find(r => matches(r, a.where));
      if (!row) throw Object.assign(new Error(`No ${name} record was found for an update.`), { code: 'P2025' });
      Object.assign(row, a.data);
      return shape(name, row, a);
    },
    updateMany: async (a: Row) => {
      const rows = t().filter(r => matches(r, a.where));
      rows.forEach(r => Object.assign(r, a.data));
      return { count: rows.length };
    },
  };
  return Object.fromEntries(
    Object.entries(impl).map(([k, fn]) => [k, (...args: unknown[]) => { prismaCalls.push(`${name}.${k}`); return fn(...args); }]),
  );
}
const models: Record<string, Row> = {};
const fakePrisma: Row = new Proxy({} as Row, {
  get(_t, prop) {
    if (typeof prop !== 'string' || prop === 'then') return undefined;
    if (prop === '$transaction') return async (arg: unknown) => (typeof arg === 'function' ? arg(fakePrisma) : Promise.all(arg as Promise<unknown>[]));
    if (prop.startsWith('$')) return async () => undefined;
    return (models[prop] ??= model(prop));
  },
});

// ---- Fake Redis (Upstash parses JSON on read), with expiry on a clock the smoke can move ----

let redisSkewMs = 0;
const redisNow = () => Date.now() + redisSkewMs;
const redisStore = new Map<string, { raw: string; expiresAt: number | null }>();
const live = (k: string) => {
  const e = redisStore.get(k);
  if (e && e.expiresAt !== null && e.expiresAt <= redisNow()) redisStore.delete(k);
  return redisStore.get(k);
};
const decode = (raw: string | undefined) => {
  if (raw === undefined) return null;
  try { return JSON.parse(raw); } catch { return raw; }
};
const encode = (v: unknown) => (typeof v === 'string' ? v : JSON.stringify(v));
const expiry = (o?: Row) => (o?.ex ? redisNow() + o.ex * 1000 : o?.px ? redisNow() + o.px : null);
const redisImpl: Row = {
  get: async (k: string) => decode(live(k)?.raw),
  set: async (k: string, v: unknown, o?: Row) => {
    if (o?.nx && live(k)) return null;
    redisStore.set(k, { raw: encode(v), expiresAt: expiry(o) });
    return 'OK';
  },
  setex: async (k: string, sec: number, v: unknown) => { redisStore.set(k, { raw: encode(v), expiresAt: redisNow() + sec * 1000 }); return 'OK'; },
  // Reads and deletes in one tick, as GETDEL does.
  getdel: async (k: string) => { const e = live(k); redisStore.delete(k); return decode(e?.raw); },
  del: async (...ks: unknown[]) => ks.flat().reduce((n: number, k) => n + (redisStore.delete(String(k)) ? 1 : 0), 0),
  incr: async (k: string) => { const n = Number(live(k)?.raw ?? 0) + 1; redisStore.set(k, { raw: String(n), expiresAt: live(k)?.expiresAt ?? null }); return n; },
  expire: async (k: string, sec: number) => { const e = live(k); if (!e) return 0; e.expiresAt = redisNow() + sec * 1000; return 1; },
  exists: async (...ks: string[]) => ks.filter(k => live(k)).length,
};
const fakeRedis = new Proxy(redisImpl, {
  get: (t, p) => (typeof p !== 'string' || p === 'then' ? undefined : t[p] ?? (async () => null)),
});

const captured: { context: string; message: string; extra: string; severity?: string }[] = [];
```
