// ---- The two providers, played by fetch ----

type P = 'telegram' | 'google';
const RSA = crypto.generateKeyPairSync('rsa', { modulusLength: 2048 });
const FOREIGN_RSA = crypto.generateKeyPairSync('rsa', { modulusLength: 2048 });
const EC = crypto.generateKeyPairSync('ec', { namedCurve: 'P-256' });
const SERVERS = {
  telegram: {
    issuer: 'https://oauth.telegram.org',
    discovery: 'https://oauth.telegram.org/.well-known/openid-configuration',
    auth: 'https://oauth.telegram.org/auth',
    token: 'https://oauth.telegram.org/token',
    jwks: 'https://oauth.telegram.org/.well-known/jwks.json',
    kid: 'oidc-1',
    algs: ['RS256', 'ES256', 'EdDSA', 'ES256K'],
    clientId: () => SIGNIN_ENV.TELEGRAM_LOGIN_CLIENT_ID,
    secret: () => SIGNIN_ENV.TELEGRAM_LOGIN_CLIENT_SECRET,
  },
  google: {
    issuer: 'https://accounts.google.com',
    discovery: 'https://accounts.google.com/.well-known/openid-configuration',
    auth: 'https://accounts.google.com/o/oauth2/v2/auth',
    token: 'https://oauth2.googleapis.com/token',
    jwks: 'https://www.googleapis.com/oauth2/v3/certs',
    kid: 'g-1',
    algs: ['RS256'],
    clientId: () => SIGNIN_ENV.GOOGLE_SIGNIN_CLIENT_ID,
    secret: () => SIGNIN_ENV.GOOGLE_SIGNIN_CLIENT_SECRET,
  },
};

const b64 = (v: unknown) => Buffer.from(typeof v === 'string' ? v : JSON.stringify(v)).toString('base64url');
function signJwt(claims: Row, kid: string, o: { alg?: 'RS256' | 'ES256'; key?: crypto.KeyObject } = {}): string {
  const alg = o.alg ?? 'RS256';
  const input = `${b64({ alg, kid, typ: 'JWT' })}.${b64(claims)}`;
  const sig = alg === 'RS256'
    ? crypto.sign('sha256', Buffer.from(input), o.key ?? RSA.privateKey)
    : crypto.sign('sha256', Buffer.from(input), { key: o.key ?? EC.privateKey, dsaEncoding: 'ieee-p1363' });
  return `${input}.${sig.toString('base64url')}`;
}

/** Every value a log line must never hold: codes, states, nonces, verifiers, tokens, secrets, the email. */
const secrets = new Set<string>([SIGNIN_ENV.TELEGRAM_LOGIN_CLIENT_SECRET, SIGNIN_ENV.GOOGLE_SIGNIN_CLIENT_SECRET, 'dana@gmail.com']);
const codes = new Map<string, { p: P; challenge: string; redirectUri: string; idToken: string; used: boolean }>();
const fetches: { url: string; method: string; signal: boolean }[] = [];
const tokenCalls: { p: P; status: number }[] = [];
const failOnce = new Set<string>();
const json = (body: unknown, status = 200) => new Response(JSON.stringify(body), { status, headers: { 'content-type': 'application/json' } });

function providerFetch(url: string, init: RequestInit): Response {
  const method = (init.method ?? 'GET').toUpperCase();
  for (const p of ['telegram', 'google'] as P[]) {
    const s = SERVERS[p];
    if (url === s.discovery) {
      return json({
        issuer: s.issuer, authorization_endpoint: s.auth, token_endpoint: s.token, jwks_uri: s.jwks,
        response_types_supported: ['code'], subject_types_supported: ['public'],
        token_endpoint_auth_methods_supported: ['client_secret_basic', 'client_secret_post'],
        id_token_signing_alg_values_supported: s.algs, code_challenge_methods_supported: ['plain', 'S256'],
      });
    }
    if (url === s.jwks) {
      return json({ keys: [
        { ...RSA.publicKey.export({ format: 'jwk' }), kid: s.kid, alg: 'RS256', use: 'sig' },
        { ...EC.publicKey.export({ format: 'jwk' }), kid: `${s.kid}-es`, alg: 'ES256', use: 'sig' },
      ] });
    }
    if (url === s.token && method === 'POST') {
      const form = new URLSearchParams(String(init.body));
      const entry = codes.get(form.get('code') ?? '');
      const challenge = crypto.createHash('sha256').update(form.get('code_verifier') ?? '').digest('base64url');
      const refuse = (status: number, error: string) => { tokenCalls.push({ p, status }); return json({ error }, status); };
      if (form.get('client_id') !== s.clientId() || form.get('client_secret') !== s.secret()) return refuse(401, 'invalid_client');
      if (!entry || entry.used || entry.p !== p || form.get('grant_type') !== 'authorization_code') return refuse(400, 'invalid_grant');
      if (form.get('redirect_uri') !== entry.redirectUri || challenge !== entry.challenge) return refuse(400, 'invalid_grant');
      entry.used = true;
      const accessToken = `at-${crypto.randomUUID()}`;
      secrets.add(accessToken);
      tokenCalls.push({ p, status: 200 });
      return json({ access_token: accessToken, token_type: 'Bearer', expires_in: 30, id_token: entry.idToken });
    }
  }
  throw new Error(`network blocked in smoke: ${method} ${url}`);
}

interface Approval { alg?: 'RS256' | 'ES256'; key?: crypto.KeyObject; nonce?: string | null; aud?: unknown; expIn?: number }

/** The provider's side of an approval: an id_token for this authorization request, and the URL the browser comes back to. */
function approve(p: P, authUrl: URL, claims: Row, o: Approval = {}): URL {
  const q = authUrl.searchParams;
  const now = Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000);
  const nonce = o.nonce === undefined ? q.get('nonce') : o.nonce;
  const body: Row = { iss: SERVERS[p].issuer, aud: o.aud ?? q.get('client_id'), iat: now, exp: now + (o.expIn ?? 30), ...(nonce === null ? {} : { nonce }), ...claims };
  const code = crypto.randomBytes(16).toString('hex');
  const idToken = signJwt(body, o.alg === 'ES256' ? `${SERVERS[p].kid}-es` : SERVERS[p].kid, o);
  codes.set(code, { p, challenge: q.get('code_challenge') ?? '', redirectUri: q.get('redirect_uri') ?? '', idToken, used: false });
  for (const v of [code, idToken, q.get('state'), q.get('nonce')]) if (v) secrets.add(v);
  const back = new URL(q.get('redirect_uri') ?? '');
  back.searchParams.set('code', code);
  back.searchParams.set('state', q.get('state') ?? '');
  return back;
}

// ---- Fixtures ----

const DAY = 86_400_000;
function baseUser(o: Row): Row {
  return {
    name: 'x', englishName: '', gender: 'male', language: 'en', location: 'Tel Aviv', culture: 'default',
    messagingPlatform: 'telegram', googleRefreshToken: '', calendarAssignments: null, calendarSource: 'NATIVE',
    pairingId: null, remindersEnabled: false, suspendedAt: null, unreachableSince: null, whatsappPhone: null,
    whatsappBsuid: null, telegramId: null, isAdmin: false, globalRules: [], defaultReminderMinutes: null,
    sessionsValidAfter: null, googleAccountKey: null, googleCalendarSignIn: true,
    createdAt: new Date(Date.now() - 30 * DAY), updatedAt: new Date(Date.now() - DAY),
    ...o,
  };
}

/**
 * 9 = Telegram user 111111111 (en). 1 = Telegram user 5550001 (he) with a Google sign-in way (sub g-sub-1).
 * 7 = Telegram user 777, whose id is the `sub` the Telegram tokens below carry. 3 = WhatsApp-only, with an email
 * sign-in way for dana@gmail.com, the address the Google tokens carry.
 */
function seed() {
  for (const k of Object.keys(DB)) delete DB[k];
  redisStore.clear();
  redisSkewMs = 0;
  codes.clear();
  tokenCalls.length = 0;
  captured.length = 0;
  failOnce.clear();
  DB.user = [
    baseUser({ id: 9, name: 'Tal', telegramId: BigInt(111111111) }),
    baseUser({ id: 1, name: 'Dana', telegramId: BigInt(5550001), language: 'he' }),
    baseUser({ id: 7, name: 'Sub-Twin', telegramId: BigInt(777) }),
    baseUser({ id: 3, name: 'WA', messagingPlatform: 'whatsapp', whatsappPhone: '972500000003' }),
  ];
  DB.signInIdentity = [
    { id: 1, userId: 1, kind: 'google', subject: 'g-sub-1', address: 'dana@gmail.com', createdAt: new Date(Date.now() - DAY), lastUsedAt: null },
    { id: 2, userId: 3, kind: 'email', subject: 'dana@gmail.com', address: 'dana@gmail.com', createdAt: new Date(Date.now() - DAY), lastUsedAt: null },
  ];
}

const load = (rel: string): Promise<Row> => import(path.join(ROOT, rel));

async function main() {
  installStubs(await load('src/services/messaging/types.ts'));
  globalThis.fetch = (async (input: unknown, init: RequestInit = {}) => {
    const url = String(input);
    fetches.push({ url, method: (init.method ?? 'GET').toUpperCase(), signal: init.signal != null });
    if (failOnce.delete(url)) return json({ error: 'backend_error' }, 503);
    return providerFetch(url, init);
  }) as typeof fetch;

  const { NextRequest } = nodeRequire('next/server');
  const { __useRetryForTests } = await load('src/utils/fetch-retry.ts');
  const { __useGoogleRetryForTests } = await load('src/services/google-retry.ts');
  __useRetryForTests({ sleep: async () => undefined });
  __useGoogleRetryForTests({ sleep: async () => undefined });
  const { SESSION_COOKIE_NAME, validateSessionToken } = await load('src/lib/session-auth.ts');
  const { signInPageUrl } = await load('src/lib/web-session.ts');
  const { SIGNIN_COOKIE_NAME } = await load('src/services/web-signin/flow.ts');
  const { __resetOidcForTests } = await load('src/services/web-signin/oidc.ts');
  const routes = {
    telegram: { start: await load('app/api/auth/telegram/start/route.ts'), callback: await load('app/api/auth/telegram/callback/route.ts') },
    google: { start: await load('app/api/auth/google/start/route.ts'), callback: await load('app/api/auth/google/callback/route.ts') },
  };
  recordConsole();

  const req = (url: string, cookie?: string) =>
    new NextRequest(url, { headers: { 'accept-language': 'en', ...(cookie ? { cookie } : {}) } });
  const setCookies = (res: Response): string[] => res.headers.getSetCookie();
  const cookieOf = (res: Response, name: string) => setCookies(res).find(c => c.startsWith(`${name}=`));
  const valueOf = (res: Response, name: string) => cookieOf(res, name)?.split(';')[0].slice(name.length + 1) ?? '';
  const location = (res: Response) => res.headers.get('location') ?? '';
  const sessionOf = (res: Response) => {
    const value = valueOf(res, SESSION_COOKIE_NAME);
    return value ? validateSessionToken(decodeURIComponent(value)) : null;
  };

  /** /api/auth/<p>/start: the provider's URL and this browser's famcal_signin cookie. */
  async function start(p: P, locale = 'en') {
    const res: Response = await routes[p].start.GET(req(`https://famcal.bot/api/auth/${p}/start?locale=${locale}`));
    const flowCookie = `${SIGNIN_COOKIE_NAME}=${valueOf(res, SIGNIN_COOKIE_NAME)}`;
    return { res, url: new URL(location(res)), flowCookie };
  }
  /** The browser back on /api/auth/<p>/callback with what the provider gave it. */
  const callback = (p: P, back: URL, cookie?: string): Promise<Response> => routes[p].callback.GET(req(back.href, cookie));
  /** A whole sign-in: start, the provider's approval with these claims, the callback. */
  async function signIn(p: P, claims: Row, o: Approval = {}, locale = 'en') {
    const s = await start(p, locale);
    const back = approve(p, s.url, claims, o);
    return { ...s, back, res: await callback(p, back, s.flowCookie) };
  }
  const isSignInPage = (res: Response, locale: string, status: string) => location(res) === signInPageUrl(locale, status);
  const flowCleared = (res: Response) => {
    const c = cookieOf(res, SIGNIN_COOKIE_NAME) ?? '';
    return /^famcal_signin=;/.test(c) && /Path=\/api\/auth/i.test(c) && /(Max-Age=0|Expires=Thu, 01 Jan 1970)/i.test(c);
  };
  const lastCapture = () => captured[captured.length - 1];

  // ---- Not set up ----

  await check('#1 a way whose client id or secret is unset stays off: its start goes to /signin?status=unavailable, with no flow and no request', async () => {
    seed();
    const before = fetches.length;
    delete process.env.TELEGRAM_LOGIN_CLIENT_SECRET;
    process.env.GOOGLE_SIGNIN_CLIENT_ID = process.env.GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID;
    try {
      const tg = await routes.telegram.start.GET(req('https://famcal.bot/api/auth/telegram/start?locale=ru'));
      assert(isSignInPage(tg, 'ru', 'unavailable'), `telegram: ${tg.status} ${location(tg)}`);
      const g = await routes.google.start.GET(req('https://famcal.bot/api/auth/google/start?locale=en'));
      assert(isSignInPage(g, 'en', 'unavailable'), `google on the calendar client: ${g.status} ${location(g)}`);
      assert(!cookieOf(tg, SIGNIN_COOKIE_NAME) && !cookieOf(g, SIGNIN_COOKIE_NAME), `a flow cookie was set: ${show([setCookies(tg), setCookies(g)])}`);
      assert(redisStore.size === 0, `flows kept: ${show([...redisStore.keys()])}`);
      assert(fetches.length === before, `requests: ${show(fetches.slice(before))}`);
    } finally {
      Object.assign(process.env, SIGNIN_ENV);
      __resetOidcForTests();
    }
  });

  // ---- The start ----

  await check('#2 Telegram start: Telegram\'s /auth with our client, redirect URI from the base URL, openid profile, S256, state, nonce and origin; famcal_signin is HttpOnly, Secure, Lax, Path=/api/auth', async () => {
    seed();
    const { res, url } = await start('telegram');
    const q = url.searchParams;
    assert(res.status >= 300 && res.status < 400, `status ${res.status}`);
    assert(`${url.origin}${url.pathname}` === SERVERS.telegram.auth, `to ${url.origin}${url.pathname}`);
    assert(q.get('client_id') === SIGNIN_ENV.TELEGRAM_LOGIN_CLIENT_ID && q.get('response_type') === 'code', `client ${show([...q])}`);
    assert(q.get('redirect_uri') === 'https://famcal.bot/api/auth/telegram/callback', `redirect_uri ${q.get('redirect_uri')}`);
    assert(q.get('scope') === 'openid profile', `scope ${q.get('scope')}`);
    assert(q.get('code_challenge_method') === 'S256' && (q.get('code_challenge') ?? '').length === 43, `pkce ${q.get('code_challenge_method')} ${q.get('code_challenge')}`);
    assert((q.get('state') ?? '').length >= 22 && (q.get('nonce') ?? '').length >= 22 && q.get('state') !== q.get('nonce'), 'state and nonce');
    assert(q.get('origin') === 'https://famcal.bot', `origin ${q.get('origin')}`);
    assert(!url.href.includes(SIGNIN_ENV.TELEGRAM_LOGIN_CLIENT_SECRET), 'the client secret is in the URL');
    const c = cookieOf(res, SIGNIN_COOKIE_NAME) ?? '';
    assert(/HttpOnly/i.test(c) && /Secure/i.test(c) && /SameSite=Lax/i.test(c) && /Path=\/api\/auth/i.test(c), `flow cookie ${c}`);
  });

  await check('#3 Google start: Google\'s endpoint, openid email only, S256, state and nonce, the account chooser; never include_granted_scopes, access_type or origin', async () => {
    seed();
    const { url } = await start('google');
    const q = url.searchParams;
    assert(`${url.origin}${url.pathname}` === SERVERS.google.auth, `to ${url.origin}${url.pathname}`);
    assert(q.get('client_id') === SIGNIN_ENV.GOOGLE_SIGNIN_CLIENT_ID, `client_id ${q.get('client_id')}`);
    assert(q.get('redirect_uri') === 'https://famcal.bot/api/auth/google/callback', `redirect_uri ${q.get('redirect_uri')}`);
    assert(q.get('scope') === 'openid email', `scope ${q.get('scope')}`);
    assert(q.get('code_challenge_method') === 'S256' && q.get('state') && q.get('nonce'), `checks ${show([...q.keys()])}`);
    assert(q.get('prompt') === 'select_account', `prompt ${q.get('prompt')}`);
    for (const k of ['include_granted_scopes', 'access_type', 'origin']) assert(!q.has(k), `${k}=${q.get(k)}`);
  });

  // ---- Telegram: who it is ----

  await check('#4 Telegram, `id` as a number: user 9 is signed in (method tg) and lands on /dashboard?user_id=9 (English has no prefix); the code went with the secret and the PKCE verifier; famcal_signin is cleared', async () => {
    seed();
    const { res } = await signIn('telegram', { sub: '777', id: 111111111 });
    const to = new URL(location(res));
    assert(to.pathname === '/dashboard' && to.searchParams.get('user_id') === '9', `to ${location(res)}; ${show(captured)}`);
    const session = sessionOf(res);
    assert(session?.userId === 9 && session.method === 'tg', `session ${show(session)}`);
    assert(show(tokenCalls) === show([{ p: 'telegram', status: 200 }]), `token calls ${show(tokenCalls)}`);
    assert(flowCleared(res), `flow cookie ${show(setCookies(res))}`);
  });

  await check('#5 Telegram, `id` as a string of digits: user 1 is signed in, in their own language (/he/dashboard)', async () => {
    seed();
    const { res } = await signIn('telegram', { sub: '777', id: '5550001' });
    const to = new URL(location(res));
    assert(to.pathname === '/he/dashboard' && to.searchParams.get('user_id') === '1', `to ${location(res)}`);
    assert(sessionOf(res)?.userId === 1, `session ${show(sessionOf(res))}`);
  });

  await check('#6 Telegram never by `sub`: a token whose sub is user 7\'s Telegram id and whose id is user 9\'s signs in 9; one with that sub and no id signs in nobody (status=failed)', async () => {
    seed();
    const both = await signIn('telegram', { sub: '777', id: 111111111 });
    assert(sessionOf(both.res)?.userId === 9, `with id: ${show(sessionOf(both.res))}`);
    const subOnly = await signIn('telegram', { sub: '777' });
    assert(isSignInPage(subOnly.res, 'en', 'failed'), `sub only: ${location(subOnly.res)}`);
    assert(!sessionOf(subOnly.res), `sub only signed in ${show(sessionOf(subOnly.res))}`);
    assert(/no Telegram user id/.test(lastCapture()?.message ?? ''), `capture ${show(lastCapture())}`);
  });

  await check('#7 an unknown Telegram id gets the no-account page in the language the sign-in began in, with no session', async () => {
    seed();
    const { res } = await signIn('telegram', { sub: '1', id: 222222222 }, {}, 'ru');
    assert(isSignInPage(res, 'ru', 'no-account'), `to ${location(res)}`);
    assert(!sessionOf(res) && flowCleared(res), `cookies ${show(setCookies(res))}`);
  });

  await check('#8 a suspended account goes to finishSignIn\'s suspended page, with no session', async () => {
    seed();
    DB.user.find(u => u.id === 9)!.suspendedAt = new Date(Date.now() - DAY);
    const { res } = await signIn('telegram', { sub: '1', id: 111111111 });
    assert(isSignInPage(res, 'en', 'suspended') && !sessionOf(res), `to ${location(res)} ${show(setCookies(res))}`);
  });

  // ---- The one-time checks ----

  await check('#9 a reused state: the same callback a second time is status=restart and makes no second exchange', async () => {
    seed();
    const first = await signIn('telegram', { sub: '1', id: 111111111 });
    assert(sessionOf(first.res)?.userId === 9, `first ${location(first.res)}`);
    const again = await callback('telegram', first.back, first.flowCookie);
    assert(isSignInPage(again, 'en', 'restart') && !sessionOf(again), `again ${location(again)}`);
    assert(tokenCalls.length === 1, `token calls ${show(tokenCalls)}`);
  });

  await check('#10 a wrong state is status=restart with no exchange: the cookie it came with is used up (the right state under it is refused too), and this browser\'s flow is kept under a new id, which still signs in', async () => {
    seed();
    const s = await start('telegram');
    const back = approve('telegram', s.url, { sub: '1', id: 111111111 });
    const forged = new URL(back.href);
    forged.searchParams.set('state', 'not-the-state');
    const wrong = await callback('telegram', forged, s.flowCookie);
    assert(isSignInPage(wrong, 'en', 'restart') && !sessionOf(wrong), `wrong ${location(wrong)}`);
    const kept = valueOf(wrong, SIGNIN_COOKIE_NAME);
    assert(kept !== '' && kept !== s.flowCookie.slice(SIGNIN_COOKIE_NAME.length + 1) && !flowCleared(wrong), `the flow was not kept under a new id: ${show(setCookies(wrong))}`);
    const old = await callback('telegram', back, s.flowCookie);
    assert(isSignInPage(old, 'en', 'restart') && !sessionOf(old), `right state under the used-up cookie ${location(old)}`);
    assert(tokenCalls.length === 0, `token calls ${show(tokenCalls)}`);
    const right = await callback('telegram', back, `${SIGNIN_COOKIE_NAME}=${kept}`);
    assert(sessionOf(right)?.userId === 9, `right state under the kept flow ${location(right)}`);
  });

  await check('#11 a late callback (over 10 minutes after the start) is status=restart with no exchange', async () => {
    seed();
    const s = await start('telegram');
    const back = approve('telegram', s.url, { sub: '1', id: 111111111 });
    redisSkewMs = 601_000;
    const res = await callback('telegram', back, s.flowCookie);
    assert(isSignInPage(res, 'en', 'restart') && !sessionOf(res), `to ${location(res)}`);
    assert(tokenCalls.length === 0, `token calls ${show(tokenCalls)}`);
  });

  await check('#12 a callback without this browser\'s famcal_signin is status=restart with no exchange', async () => {
    seed();
    const s = await start('telegram');
    const res = await callback('telegram', approve('telegram', s.url, { sub: '1', id: 111111111 }));
    assert(isSignInPage(res, 'en', 'restart') && !sessionOf(res), `to ${location(res)}`);
    assert(tokenCalls.length === 0, `token calls ${show(tokenCalls)}`);
  });

  await check('#13 a Google flow\'s cookie on the Telegram callback is status=restart with no exchange, and that Google sign-in (another tab\'s) still finishes', async () => {
    seed();
    const g = await start('google');
    const t = await start('telegram');
    const res = await callback('telegram', approve('telegram', t.url, { sub: '1', id: 111111111 }), g.flowCookie);
    assert(isSignInPage(res, 'en', 'restart') && !sessionOf(res), `to ${location(res)}`);
    assert(tokenCalls.length === 0, `token calls ${show(tokenCalls)}`);
    // Two tabs, two ways (review focus RF1): the Telegram answer neither used up nor cleared the Google sign-in this
    // browser started last, which still finishes
    assert(!flowCleared(res) && valueOf(res, SIGNIN_COOKIE_NAME) === '', `the Google sign-in's cookie was touched: ${show(setCookies(res))}`);
    const google = await callback('google', approve('google', g.url, { sub: 'g-sub-1', email: 'dana@gmail.com', email_verified: true }), g.flowCookie);
    assert(sessionOf(google)?.userId === 1, `the Google sign-in no longer finishes: ${location(google)}`);
  });

  // ---- The id_token's checks (status=failed, a Sentry warning that names the check) ----

  const refusedWith = async (name: string, p: P, claims: Row, o: Approval, expect: RegExp) => {
    seed();
    const { res } = await signIn(p, claims, o);
    assert(isSignInPage(res, 'en', 'failed'), `${name}: to ${location(res)}`);
    assert(!sessionOf(res) && flowCleared(res), `${name}: cookies ${show(setCookies(res))}`);
    const c = lastCapture();
    assert(c && c.context === 'signin-oidc' && c.severity === 'warning' && expect.test(c.message), `${name}: capture ${show(c)}`);
  };
  const tgClaims = { sub: '1', id: 111111111 };
  const gClaims = { sub: 'g-sub-1', email: 'dana@gmail.com', email_verified: true };

  await check('#14 a wrong nonce is refused', () => refusedWith('wrong nonce', 'telegram', tgClaims, { nonce: 'someone-elses-nonce' }, /claim nonce/));
  await check('#15 an id_token with no nonce is refused (the log names it, for the first live sign-in)', () => refusedWith('no nonce', 'telegram', tgClaims, { nonce: null }, /"nonce" \(nonce\) claim missing/));
  await check('#16 a Telegram token for another audience is refused', () => refusedWith('audience', 'telegram', tgClaims, { aud: 'another-bot' }, /claim aud/));
  await check('#17 a token signed by a key Telegram didn\'t publish is refused', () => refusedWith('foreign key', 'telegram', tgClaims, { key: FOREIGN_RSA.privateKey }, /signature verification failed/));
  await check('#18 an ES256 token is refused (RS256 only), though its key is published', () => refusedWith('ES256', 'telegram', tgClaims, { alg: 'ES256' }, /"alg"/));
  await check('#19 a token expired 2 minutes ago is refused', () => refusedWith('expired', 'telegram', tgClaims, { expIn: -120 }, /claim exp/));

  await check('#20 a token that expired 10 s ago is within the clock tolerance and signs in', async () => {
    seed();
    const { res } = await signIn('telegram', tgClaims, { expIn: -10 });
    assert(sessionOf(res)?.userId === 9, `to ${location(res)}; ${show(lastCapture())}`);
  });

  // ---- Google ----

  await check('#21 Google: the sign-in way with this sub signs in user 1 (method google, /he/dashboard) and its last use is set', async () => {
    seed();
    const { res } = await signIn('google', gClaims);
    const to = new URL(location(res));
    assert(to.pathname === '/he/dashboard' && to.searchParams.get('user_id') === '1', `to ${location(res)}; ${show(captured)}`);
    const session = sessionOf(res);
    assert(session?.userId === 1 && session.method === 'google', `session ${show(session)}`);
    assert(DB.signInIdentity[0].lastUsedAt instanceof Date, `lastUsedAt ${show(DB.signInIdentity[0])}`);
    assert(flowCleared(res), `flow cookie ${show(setCookies(res))}`);
  });

  await check('#22 Google: email_verified as the string "true" counts as verified', async () => {
    seed();
    const { res } = await signIn('google', { ...gClaims, email_verified: 'true' });
    assert(sessionOf(res)?.userId === 1, `to ${location(res)}`);
  });

  await check('#23 Google: email_verified false, "false" or missing, or no email, signs in nobody (status=failed)', async () => {
    for (const claims of [{ ...gClaims, email_verified: false }, { ...gClaims, email_verified: 'false' }, { sub: 'g-sub-1', email: 'dana@gmail.com' }, { sub: 'g-sub-1', email_verified: true }]) {
      seed();
      const { res } = await signIn('google', claims);
      assert(isSignInPage(res, 'en', 'failed') && !sessionOf(res), `${show(claims)}: to ${location(res)}`);
      assert(DB.signInIdentity[0].lastUsedAt === null, `${show(claims)}: the way was looked up`);
    }
  });

  await check('#24 Google: a token for the calendar client, or for both clients with no azp, is refused', async () => {
    await refusedWith('calendar audience', 'google', gClaims, { aud: process.env.GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID }, /claim aud/);
    await refusedWith('two audiences', 'google', gClaims, { aud: [SIGNIN_ENV.GOOGLE_SIGNIN_CLIENT_ID, process.env.GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID] }, /untrusted audiences/);
  });

  await check('#25 Google never by email: an unknown sub whose verified email is user 3\'s email way gets the no-account page', async () => {
    seed();
    const { res } = await signIn('google', { ...gClaims, sub: 'g-sub-unknown' });
    assert(isSignInPage(res, 'en', 'no-account') && !sessionOf(res), `to ${location(res)}`);
    assert(DB.signInIdentity[1].lastUsedAt === null, 'the email way was touched');
  });

  // ---- Two sign-ins in one browser, and a provider that comes back without a code ----

  await check('#26 two sign-ins started in one browser (two tabs): the first one\'s callback, whose state no longer matches the cookie the second start set, is status=restart and signs nobody in; the second one still signs in; neither can be played again', async () => {
    for (const [p, claims, userId, method] of [['telegram', tgClaims, 9, 'tg'], ['google', gClaims, 1, 'google']] as [P, Row, number, string][]) {
      seed();
      const tab1 = await start(p);
      const tab2 = await start(p);
      assert(tab1.flowCookie !== tab2.flowCookie, `${p}: both starts set the same cookie`);
      const back1 = approve(p, tab1.url, claims);
      const back2 = approve(p, tab2.url, claims);
      // The browser holds the cookie the last start set (tab 2's).
      const first = await callback(p, back1, tab2.flowCookie);
      assert(isSignInPage(first, 'en', 'restart') && !sessionOf(first), `${p}: tab 1 ${location(first)}`);
      assert(tokenCalls.length === 0, `${p}: tab 1 reached the token endpoint ${show(tokenCalls)}`);
      const kept = valueOf(first, SIGNIN_COOKIE_NAME);
      assert(kept !== '' && !flowCleared(first), `${p}: tab 2's flow was not kept: ${show(setCookies(first))}`);
      const second = await callback(p, back2, `${SIGNIN_COOKIE_NAME}=${kept}`);
      const session = sessionOf(second);
      assert(session?.userId === userId && session.method === method, `${p}: tab 2 ${location(second)} ${show(session)}`);
      assert(show(tokenCalls) === show([{ p, status: 200 }]), `${p}: token calls ${show(tokenCalls)}`);
      for (const [name, back, cookie] of [['tab 2 again', back2, `${SIGNIN_COOKIE_NAME}=${kept}`], ['tab 1 again', back1, tab2.flowCookie]] as [string, URL, string][]) {
        const replay = await callback(p, back, cookie);
        assert(isSignInPage(replay, 'en', 'restart') && !sessionOf(replay), `${p}: ${name} ${location(replay)}`);
      }
      assert(tokenCalls.length === 1, `${p}: token calls after the replays ${show(tokenCalls)}`);
    }
  });

  await check('#27 a provider\'s ?error= (the person cancelled): with this browser\'s state it goes back to the plain /signin page with no exchange, no Sentry report, the flow cookie cleared and the error word logged; a word that is not a lowercase OAuth word is logged as unrecognised; with a wrong state it is status=restart', async () => {
    for (const p of ['telegram', 'google'] as P[]) {
      seed();
      const answer = async (error: string, state?: string) => {
        const s = await start(p);
        const back = new URL(s.url.searchParams.get('redirect_uri') ?? '');
        back.searchParams.set('error', error);
        back.searchParams.set('state', state ?? s.url.searchParams.get('state') ?? '');
        const mark = logged.length;
        const res = await callback(p, back, s.flowCookie);
        return { res, lines: logged.slice(mark) };
      };
      const denied = await answer('access_denied');
      assert(location(denied.res) === signInPageUrl('en'), `${p}: to ${location(denied.res)}`);
      assert(!sessionOf(denied.res) && flowCleared(denied.res), `${p}: cookies ${show(setCookies(denied.res))}`);
      assert(tokenCalls.length === 0 && captured.length === 0, `${p}: token calls ${show(tokenCalls)}, reports ${show(captured)}`);
      assert(denied.lines.includes(`[signin] ${p} came back without a code (access_denied)`), `${p}: log ${show(denied.lines)}`);
      const odd = await answer('Bad value; drop table');
      assert(location(odd.res) === signInPageUrl('en'), `${p}: odd word to ${location(odd.res)}`);
      assert(odd.lines.includes(`[signin] ${p} came back without a code (unrecognised)`) && !odd.lines.some(l => l.includes('drop table')), `${p}: odd log ${show(odd.lines)}`);
      const forged = await answer('access_denied', 'not-the-state');
      assert(isSignInPage(forged.res, 'en', 'restart'), `${p}: wrong state to ${location(forged.res)}`);
    }
  });

  // ---- The retry layers, the cache, the logs ----

  await check('#28 a 503 from either token endpoint is retried by that provider\'s layer, and no request carries a timeout signal', async () => {
    seed();
    failOnce.add(SERVERS.telegram.token);
    const tg = await signIn('telegram', tgClaims);
    assert(sessionOf(tg.res)?.userId === 9, `telegram after a 503: ${location(tg.res)}; ${show(lastCapture())}`);
    failOnce.add(SERVERS.google.token);
    const g = await signIn('google', gClaims);
    assert(sessionOf(g.res)?.userId === 1, `google after a 503: ${location(g.res)}; ${show(lastCapture())}`);
    assert(logged.some(l => l.startsWith('[signin-telegram] HTTP 503; retry 1 of 3')), `no fetchWithRetry line: ${show(logged.slice(-5))}`);
    assert(logged.some(l => l.startsWith('[google-retry] POST oauth2.googleapis.com/token answered 503; retry 1 of 3')), `no googleFetch line: ${show(logged.slice(-5))}`);
    const signalled = fetches.filter(f => f.signal);
    assert(signalled.length === 0, `requests with a signal: ${show(signalled)}`);
  });

  await check('#29 discovery and the keys are fetched once per provider for the whole run', () => {
    for (const p of ['telegram', 'google'] as P[]) {
      const discoveries = fetches.filter(f => f.url === SERVERS[p].discovery).length;
      const keys = fetches.filter(f => f.url === SERVERS[p].jwks).length;
      assert(discoveries === 1 && keys === 1, `${p}: ${discoveries} discoveries, ${keys} key fetches`);
    }
  });

  await check('#30 a failed discovery is not kept: that start goes to status=failed, and the next one discovers again and works', async () => {
    seed();
    __resetOidcForTests();
    const discovery = (u: string) => u === SERVERS.telegram.discovery;
    const before = fetches.filter(f => discovery(f.url)).length;
    const realFetch = globalThis.fetch;
    globalThis.fetch = (async (input: unknown, init?: RequestInit) => (discovery(String(input)) ? json({ error: 'gone' }, 404) : realFetch(input as string, init))) as typeof fetch;
    let first: Response;
    try {
      first = await routes.telegram.start.GET(req('https://famcal.bot/api/auth/telegram/start?locale=en'));
    } finally {
      globalThis.fetch = realFetch;
    }
    assert(isSignInPage(first, 'en', 'failed') && !cookieOf(first, SIGNIN_COOKIE_NAME), `first ${location(first)}`);
    assert(/could not start: .*HTTP 404/.test(lastCapture()?.message ?? ''), `capture ${show(lastCapture())}`);
    const { res } = await signIn('telegram', tgClaims);
    assert(sessionOf(res)?.userId === 9, `after ${location(res)}`);
    assert(fetches.filter(f => discovery(f.url)).length === before + 1, 'the second start did not discover again');
  });

  await check('#31 no log line or Sentry report holds the email, a code, a state, a nonce, an id_token, an access token or a client secret', () => {
    const texts = [...logged, ...captured.map(c => `${c.message} ${c.extra}`)];
    const leaks = texts.filter(t => [...secrets].some(s => t.includes(s)));
    assert(secrets.size > 20, `only ${secrets.size} values were tracked`);
    assert(leaks.length === 0, `leaked: ${show(leaks.slice(0, 3))}`);
  });

  Object.assign(console, realConsole);
  let failed = 0;
  for (const r of results) {
    console.log(`${r.ok ? 'OK' : 'FAIL'}  ${r.name}${r.ok ? '' : ` — ${r.reason}`}`);
    if (!r.ok) failed++;
  }
  console.log(`\n${results.length - failed}/${results.length} passed`);
  process.exit(failed ? 1 : 0);
}

main().catch(err => {
  Object.assign(console, realConsole);
  console.error(err);
  process.exit(1);
});

- [ ] **Step 4: Create `src/services/web-signin/oidc.ts`**

```ts
/**
 * Signing in on famcal.bot with Telegram or Google (OpenID Connect): the authorization URL, and the callback's checks.
 * Spec docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-02-web-sign-in-design.md §2.3 and §3.
 *
 * openid-client 6 (pinned exactly) does the protocol: discovery, PKCE (S256), state, nonce, and the id_token's
 * signature against the provider's published keys (enableNonRepudiationChecks), its issuer, its audience (our own
 * sign-in client id only), its expiry, and RS256 as the one algorithm accepted.
 *
 * Every request it makes goes through the repo's retry layer for that provider: Google's through googleFetch, Telegram's
 * through fetchWithRetry (CLAUDE.md). openid-client puts a 30 s timeout signal of its own on each request; repoFetch
 * drops it and the configuration's timeout is 0, so a call runs to the provider's ceiling (CLAUDE.md: no timeout of our own).
 *
 * Who the person is:
 * - Telegram: the `id` claim, the Telegram user id (sent only with the `profile` scope). Never `sub`: Telegram's sub
 *   is a different number for each bot.
 * - Google: `sub`, Google's account id. The email is a mutable attribute, verified only when Google says so.
 *
 * The configurations (discovered metadata, the cached signing keys) live on globalThis, so the route bundles share one
 * per process (Next 16 gives each bundle its own module instance). A failed discovery is not kept: the next sign-in tries again.
 *
 * Server only. No log line or Sentry field holds a claim, a token, a code, a state or a nonce: describeOidcError names
 * an error by its class, code and fixed message, and the claim it was about, never a value.
 */

import * as client from 'openid-client';
import { buildUrl, getBaseUrl } from '../../config/urls';
import { fetchWithRetry, HttpStatusError } from '../../utils/fetch-retry';
import { googleFetch } from '../google-retry';
import type { OidcFlow } from './flow';

export type OidcProvider = 'telegram' | 'google';

/** What a Telegram sign-in proves: the Telegram user id (User.telegramId). */
export interface TelegramClaims {
  telegramId: bigint;
}

/** What a Google sign-in proves: Google's account id, and its email with whether Google verified it. */
export interface GoogleClaims {
  sub: string;
  email: string | null;
  emailVerified: boolean;
}

const ISSUER: Record<OidcProvider, string> = {
  telegram: 'https://oauth.telegram.org',
  google: 'https://accounts.google.com',
};

/** The least each provider can give: Telegram's `profile` carries the `id` claim; Google's `email` its address. */
const SCOPE: Record<OidcProvider, string> = {
  telegram: 'openid profile',
  google: 'openid email',
};

/**
 * Seconds of clock difference allowed on exp and iat. Telegram's tokens are reported to live 30 s, so this stays
 * small; it is openid-client's default, set here so it can't drift.
 */
const CLOCK_TOLERANCE_SEC = 30;

/** A refusal of our own (not openid-client's): its reason is a fixed word, safe to log. */
class OidcRefusal extends Error {
  constructor(readonly reason: string) {
    super(`refused: ${reason}`);
    this.name = 'OidcRefusal';
  }
}

const warned = globalThis as { __famcalSigninSameClientWarned?: boolean };

/** The client id and secret, or null while the owner hasn't set them (the way then stays hidden). */
function credentials(provider: OidcProvider): { clientId: string; clientSecret: string } | null {
  const [clientId, clientSecret] =
    provider === 'telegram'
      ? [process.env.TELEGRAM_LOGIN_CLIENT_ID, process.env.TELEGRAM_LOGIN_CLIENT_SECRET]
      : [process.env.GOOGLE_SIGNIN_CLIENT_ID, process.env.GOOGLE_SIGNIN_CLIENT_SECRET];
  if (!clientId || !clientSecret) return null;
  // Sign-in has its own Google client: a token for the calendar client must never sign anyone in (spec §3).
  if (provider === 'google' && clientId === process.env.GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID) {
    if (!warned.__famcalSigninSameClientWarned) {
      warned.__famcalSigninSameClientWarned = true;
      console.warn('[signin] GOOGLE_SIGNIN_CLIENT_ID is the calendar client GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID; Google sign-in stays off until it has its own client');
    }
    return null;
  }
  return { clientId, clientSecret };
}

/** Whether this way of signing in is set up (its client id and secret are in the environment). */
export function providerConfigured(provider: OidcProvider): boolean {
  return credentials(provider) !== null;
}

/** The callback the provider sends the browser back to: from the app's base URL, never from the request's Host. */
export function redirectUri(provider: OidcProvider): string {
  return buildUrl(`/api/auth/${provider}/callback`);
}

/** A fresh state, nonce and PKCE verifier for one sign-in; the caller keeps them in the flow (startFlow). */
export function newOidcChecks(): Pick<OidcFlow, 'state' | 'nonce' | 'codeVerifier'> {
  return { state: client.randomState(), nonce: client.randomNonce(), codeVerifier: client.randomPKCECodeVerifier() };
}

/** A request's method, host and path for a log line, never its query. */
function requestOf(method: string | undefined, url: string): string {
  const parts = /^https?:\/\/([^/?#]+)([^?#]*)/.exec(url);
  return `${(method ?? 'GET').toUpperCase()} ${parts ? `${parts[1]}${parts[2]}` : '(not a URL)'}`;
}

/** Telegram is a third party with no policy of its own: the shared loop, which logs its give-up here. */
function telegramFetch(url: string, init: RequestInit): Promise<Response> {
  return fetchWithRetry(url, init, {
    label: '[signin-telegram]',
    onGiveUp: (error, info) => console.warn(`[signin-telegram] ${requestOf(init.method, url)} failed: ${describeOidcError(error)} (${info.why})`),
  });
}

/** openid-client's request, sent through the provider's retry layer, without openid-client's timeout signal. */
function repoFetch(provider: OidcProvider): client.CustomFetch {
  const send = provider === 'google' ? googleFetch : telegramFetch;
  // `signal` is left out on purpose (see the header). `body` is a form or nothing for every request made here.
  return (url, options) => send(url, { method: options.method, headers: options.headers, body: options.body as BodyInit | null | undefined, redirect: options.redirect });
}

const cache = globalThis as { __famcalOidcConfigs?: Partial<Record<OidcProvider, Promise<client.Configuration>>> };

async function discover(provider: OidcProvider, clientId: string, clientSecret: string): Promise<client.Configuration> {
  const config = await client.discovery(
    new URL(ISSUER[provider]),
    clientId,
    { client_secret: clientSecret, id_token_signed_response_alg: 'RS256', [client.clockTolerance]: CLOCK_TOLERANCE_SEC },
    client.ClientSecretPost(),
    { [client.customFetch]: repoFetch(provider) },
  );
  config.timeout = 0;
  client.enableNonRepudiationChecks(config);
  return config;
}

/** The provider's configuration: discovered once per process, and again after a failed discovery. */
function configFor(provider: OidcProvider): Promise<client.Configuration> {
  const creds = credentials(provider);
  if (!creds) return Promise.reject(new OidcRefusal('not configured'));
  const configs = (cache.__famcalOidcConfigs ??= {});
  const known = configs[provider];
  if (known) return known;
  const pending = discover(provider, creds.clientId, creds.clientSecret).catch((error: unknown) => {
    if (configs[provider] === pending) delete configs[provider];
    throw error;
  });
  configs[provider] = pending;
  return pending;
}

/** Tests only: forget the discovered configurations, as a fresh process would. */
export function __resetOidcForTests(): void {
  delete cache.__famcalOidcConfigs;
  delete warned.__famcalSigninSameClientWarned;
}

/**
 * The provider's authorization URL for one sign-in: PKCE S256, the flow's state and nonce, the least scope. Telegram
 * also gets the site's origin, which it checks against the bot's allowed URLs ("origin required" without it). Google
 * gets no include_granted_scopes and no access_type, so sign-in never carries the calendar's grant, and
 * prompt=select_account, so the person picks the account.
 */
export async function authorizationUrl(provider: OidcProvider, flow: Pick<OidcFlow, 'state' | 'nonce' | 'codeVerifier'>): Promise<URL> {
  const config = await configFor(provider);
  const params: Record<string, string> = {
    redirect_uri: redirectUri(provider),
    scope: SCOPE[provider],
    state: flow.state,
    nonce: flow.nonce,
    code_challenge: await client.calculatePKCECodeChallenge(flow.codeVerifier),
    code_challenge_method: 'S256',
  };
  if (provider === 'telegram') params.origin = new URL(getBaseUrl()).origin;
  // A family computer often has several Google accounts signed in: Google asks which one instead of taking the last used.
  if (provider === 'google') params.prompt = 'select_account';
  return client.buildAuthorizationUrl(config, params);
}

/** Telegram's user id from the `id` claim: a positive whole number, sent as a JSON number or a string of digits. */
function telegramClaims(claims: client.IDToken): TelegramClaims {
  const id = claims.id;
  if (typeof id === 'number' && Number.isSafeInteger(id) && id > 0) return { telegramId: BigInt(id) };
  if (typeof id === 'string' && /^[1-9]\d{0,19}$/.test(id)) return { telegramId: BigInt(id) };
  throw new OidcRefusal('the id_token has no Telegram user id');
}

/** Google's account id, and its email; `email_verified` counts only as true or Google's sample's string "true". */
function googleClaims(claims: client.IDToken): GoogleClaims {
  const email = typeof claims.email === 'string' && claims.email !== '' ? claims.email : null;
  const verified = claims.email_verified === true || claims.email_verified === 'true';
  return { sub: claims.sub, email, emailVerified: email !== null && verified };
}

/**
 * The callback's checks and the code exchange: the state (again; the route compares it first), the PKCE verifier,
 * the nonce, and the id_token (signature, issuer, audience, expiry, RS256). `callbackUrl` is our redirect URI with the
 * callback's query. Throws on any refusal; describe the error with describeOidcError.
 *
 * The nonce is required in the id_token for both providers (ruling R6 of the 6b plan, kept on purpose): openid-client
 * can't check a nonce only when one is there. Telegram's documentation (core.telegram.org/bots/telegram-login) lists
 * `nonce` as an optional request parameter "to be included in the resulting id_token", and we always send one. A token
 * without one is refused, and the log reads `JWT "nonce" (nonce) claim missing`. If the first live Telegram sign-in
 * shows that, drop the `expectedNonce` option for Telegram only (one line); state and PKCE still bind the browser.
 */
export async function finishAuthorization(provider: 'telegram', callbackUrl: URL, flow: OidcFlow): Promise<TelegramClaims>;
export async function finishAuthorization(provider: 'google', callbackUrl: URL, flow: OidcFlow): Promise<GoogleClaims>;
export async function finishAuthorization(provider: OidcProvider, callbackUrl: URL, flow: OidcFlow): Promise<TelegramClaims | GoogleClaims>;
export async function finishAuthorization(provider: OidcProvider, callbackUrl: URL, flow: OidcFlow): Promise<TelegramClaims | GoogleClaims> {
  const config = await configFor(provider);
  const tokens = await client.authorizationCodeGrant(config, callbackUrl, {
    pkceCodeVerifier: flow.codeVerifier,
    expectedState: flow.state,
    expectedNonce: flow.nonce,
    idTokenExpected: true,
  });
  const claims = tokens.claims();
  if (!claims) throw new OidcRefusal('no id_token');
  return provider === 'telegram' ? telegramClaims(claims) : googleClaims(claims);
}

/**
 * An error from this module, for a log line or Sentry: its class, code and fixed message, the OAuth error word and the
 * claim it was about. openid-client's messages name claims, never their values; its `cause` (which holds the claims,
 * the email among them) is never read past the claim's name.
 */
export function describeOidcError(error: unknown): string {
  if (error instanceof OidcRefusal) return error.message;
  if (error instanceof HttpStatusError) return `HTTP ${error.status}`;
  if (!(error instanceof Error)) return typeof error;
  const { code, error: word, cause } = error as { code?: unknown; error?: unknown; cause?: unknown };
  // openid-client wraps a failed request ("something went wrong"): the answer's status is the useful part.
  if (cause instanceof HttpStatusError) return `${error.name} | HTTP ${cause.status}`;
  // openid-client also wraps oauth4webapi's error, whose fixed message names the claim; that error's own cause holds
  // the claims and is read for the claim's name only.
  const inner = cause instanceof Error ? cause : error;
  const facts = (inner as { cause?: unknown }).cause;
  const claim = facts && typeof facts === 'object' ? (facts as { claim?: unknown }).claim : undefined;
  return [
    error.name,
    typeof code === 'string' ? code : null,
    typeof word === 'string' && /^[a-z_]{1,40}$/.test(word) ? word : null,
    typeof claim === 'string' && /^[a-z_]{1,20}$/.test(claim) ? `claim ${claim}` : null,
    inner.message.slice(0, 160),
  ]
    .filter(Boolean)
    .join(' | ');
}

- [ ] **Step 5: Create `src/services/web-signin/identities.ts`** (only the lookup; Task 6 adds `listSignInMethods`, `addIdentity` and `removeSignInMethod` below it)

```ts
/**
 * The sign-in ways kept in SignInIdentity (spec §2.12): a Google account, keyed by Google's account id (`sub`), or an
 * email address. A person is never found by an address they typed, a name or a phone number.
 *
 * This file starts with the lookup the Google callback needs. Task 5 adds the email lookups (findEmailSignIn,
 * emailSignInAccount, touchEmailSignIn) below it, and Task 6 the add, list and remove functions (Task 6 rewrites the
 * file whole and keeps this lookup's signature and behaviour).
 */

import { prisma } from '../../utils/prisma';
import { convertPrismaUserToConfig, type UserConfig } from '../../types';

/** The account a sign-in way belongs to, with its last use set to now; null when no account has it. */
export async function findUserByIdentity(kind: 'google' | 'email', subject: string): Promise<UserConfig | null> {
  const identity = await prisma.signInIdentity.findUnique({
    where: { kind_subject: { kind, subject } },
    include: { user: true },
  });
  if (!identity) return null;
  await prisma.signInIdentity.update({ where: { id: identity.id }, data: { lastUsedAt: new Date() } });
  return convertPrismaUserToConfig(identity.user);
}
```

- [ ] **Step 6: Create `src/services/web-signin/google-signin.ts`** (Task 7 puts its `matchCalendarAccount(claims)` call at the marked comment, in place of the plain no-account answer)

```ts
/**
 * Which FamCal account a Google sign-in opens (spec §3): the Google sign-in way with this Google account id (`sub`).
 * Never the email: Google's address can change hands, its account id never does.
 */

import type { UserConfig } from '../../types';
import { findUserByIdentity } from './identities';
import type { GoogleClaims } from './oidc';

export type GoogleSignInResult = { user: UserConfig } | { status: 'no-account' | 'several' };

export async function resolveGoogleSignIn(claims: GoogleClaims): Promise<GoogleSignInResult> {
  const user = await findUserByIdentity('google', claims.sub);
  if (user) return { user };
  // The match by the Google Calendar connection's account (spec §2.17) joins here, as the one other way in.
  return { status: 'no-account' };
}

- [ ] **Step 7: Create `src/services/web-signin/oidc-route.ts`**

```ts
/**
 * The shared steps of the Telegram and Google sign-in routes (spec §3): the start (a redirect to the provider, with the
 * one-time checks kept for this browser) and the callback (the checks, then the route's own lookup of the account).
 *
 * The callback clears the famcal_signin cookie on every answer but two (no flow of its kind under the cookie, and a state
 * that differs: both leave this browser's current sign-in to finish, see handleOidcCallback), and never lets an error out of the route: Next would report it with the
 * callback URL, whose query holds the code and the state. Every refusal logs why, never a value.
 */

import { NextRequest, NextResponse } from 'next/server';
import { captureError } from '../../lib/error-capture';
import { matchesSecret } from '../../lib/secret-compare';
import { signInPageUrl, type SignInStatus } from '../../lib/web-session';
import { VALID_LOCALES, localeFromAcceptLanguage, type Locale } from '../../utils/locale';
import { clearFlowCookie, startFlow, takeFlow, type OidcFlow } from './flow';
import {
  authorizationUrl,
  describeOidcError,
  finishAuthorization,
  newOidcChecks,
  providerConfigured,
  redirectUri,
  type GoogleClaims,
  type OidcProvider,
  type TelegramClaims,
} from './oidc';

type ClaimsOf<P extends OidcProvider> = P extends 'telegram' ? TelegramClaims : GoogleClaims;

/** The page's language when it is one of ours, else the browser's. */
export function requestLocale(request: NextRequest, given?: string | null): Locale {
  return given && (VALID_LOCALES as readonly string[]).includes(given) ? (given as Locale) : localeFromAcceptLanguage(request.headers.get('accept-language'));
}

const toSignIn = (locale: string, status?: SignInStatus) => NextResponse.redirect(signInPageUrl(locale, status));

/** A provider's OAuth error word (`access_denied`) for a log line; anything else is not echoed (the link is anyone's to craft). */
const loggable = (word: string) => (/^[a-z_]{1,40}$/.test(word) ? word : 'unrecognised');

/**
 * GET /api/auth/<provider>/start?locale=: a fresh state, nonce and PKCE verifier, kept for this browser for 10 minutes
 * (startFlow), then the provider's page. A way that isn't set up yet, or a provider that can't be reached, goes back to
 * /signin with its status.
 */
export async function startOidcSignIn(provider: OidcProvider, request: NextRequest): Promise<NextResponse> {
  const locale = requestLocale(request, request.nextUrl.searchParams.get('locale'));
  if (!providerConfigured(provider)) {
    console.warn(`[signin] ${provider} sign-in was started but is not set up`);
    return toSignIn(locale, 'unavailable');
  }
  try {
    const checks = newOidcChecks();
    const response = NextResponse.redirect(await authorizationUrl(provider, checks));
    await startFlow(response, { kind: provider, ...checks, locale });
    return response;
  } catch (error) {
    captureError(new Error(`${provider} sign-in could not start: ${describeOidcError(error)}`), 'signin-oidc', { service: 'web-signin', provider });
    return toSignIn(locale, 'failed');
  }
}

/**
 * GET /api/auth/<provider>/callback: the flow this browser started (one use: takeFlow), its state, then the code
 * exchange and the id_token's checks (finishAuthorization). `onClaims` turns the proved identity into the response;
 * its result gets the flow cookie cleared like every other answer here.
 *
 * - no flow for this browser (no cookie, used, older than 10 minutes, or another kind): status=restart, with no request
 *   to the provider, and the cookie left alone (a flow of another kind is another tab's sign-in, which still finishes);
 * - a state that differs from the flow this browser holds (the answer of an older sign-in: a second one was started here
 *   since, say in another tab): status=restart, no request to the provider, and the flow just taken is put back under a
 *   new id with the new cookie on the answer, so the newer sign-in still finishes;
 * - the provider came back with `error` (the person cancelled, or refused): the plain /signin page, logged by the error
 *   word, not reported (it is not a failure of ours);
 * - a refused exchange or id_token: status=failed, reported to Sentry as a warning by error class and claim name.
 *
 * `kinds` is the list of flow kinds this callback accepts (takeFlow leaves a flow of another kind alone).
 */
export async function handleOidcCallback<P extends OidcProvider>(
  provider: P,
  request: NextRequest,
  kinds: OidcFlow['kind'][],
  onClaims: (claims: ClaimsOf<P>, flow: OidcFlow) => Promise<NextResponse>,
): Promise<NextResponse> {
  let locale: string = requestLocale(request);
  const done = (response: NextResponse) => {
    clearFlowCookie(response);
    return response;
  };
  try {
    const flow = await takeFlow(request, kinds);
    if (!flow || flow.kind === 'email') {
      console.warn(`[signin] ${provider} callback with no sign-in started in this browser; asked to start again`);
      // The cookie is left as it is: it may name this browser's newer sign-in of another way (another tab's Google,
      // Telegram or email sign-in, which takeFlow left alone), and a dead one ends by itself in 10 minutes.
      return toSignIn(locale, 'restart');
    }
    locale = flow.locale;
    if (!matchesSecret(request.nextUrl.searchParams.get('state'), flow.state)) {
      console.warn(`[signin] ${provider} callback state differs from this browser's current sign-in; asked to start again`);
      // takeFlow used the flow up (GETDEL), but it is this browser's current one and the answer is an older sign-in's:
      // keep it, under a new id, so the sign-in the person is in the middle of can still finish.
      const restart = toSignIn(locale, 'restart');
      await startFlow(restart, flow);
      return restart;
    }
    if (request.nextUrl.searchParams.has('error')) {
      console.warn(`[signin] ${provider} came back without a code (${loggable(request.nextUrl.searchParams.get('error') ?? '')})`);
      return done(toSignIn(locale));
    }
    const callbackUrl = new URL(redirectUri(provider));
    callbackUrl.search = request.nextUrl.search;
    let claims: ClaimsOf<P>;
    try {
      claims = (await finishAuthorization(provider, callbackUrl, flow)) as ClaimsOf<P>;
    } catch (error) {
      captureError(new Error(`${provider} sign-in refused: ${describeOidcError(error)}`), 'signin-oidc', { service: 'web-signin', provider }, 'warning');
      return done(toSignIn(locale, 'failed'));
    }
    return done(await onClaims(claims, flow));
  } catch (error) {
    captureError(new Error(`${provider} sign-in callback failed: ${describeOidcError(error)}`), 'signin-oidc', { service: 'web-signin', provider });
    return done(toSignIn(locale, 'failed'));
  }
}
```

import { NextRequest, NextResponse } from 'next/server';
import { handleOidcCallback } from '@/src/services/web-signin/oidc-route';
import { finishSignIn, signInPageUrl } from '@/src/lib/web-session';
import { getUserByTelegramId } from '@/src/services/user-service';

/**
 * GET /api/auth/telegram/callback: Telegram sends the browser back here. The account is the one with the token's
 * Telegram user id (the `id` claim, never `sub`); none is the no-account page.
 */
export async function GET(request: NextRequest) {
  return handleOidcCallback('telegram', request, ['telegram'], async (claims, flow) => {
    const user = await getUserByTelegramId(claims.telegramId);
    if (!user) {
      console.info('[signin] telegram sign-in matched no account');
      return NextResponse.redirect(signInPageUrl(flow.locale, 'no-account'));
    }
    return finishSignIn(user, 'tg');
  });
}

`app/api/auth/google/callback/route.ts`. It adds no callback of its own: the provider's `?error=`, a refused exchange and every Sentry report stay in `handleOidcCallback`, which never reads an openid-client error's `cause`.

```ts
import { NextRequest, NextResponse } from 'next/server';
import { handleOidcCallback } from '@/src/services/web-signin/oidc-route';
import { resolveGoogleSignIn } from '@/src/services/web-signin/google-signin';
import { finishSignIn, signInPageUrl } from '@/src/lib/web-session';

/**
 * GET /api/auth/google/callback: Google sends the browser back here. Google must have verified the account's address
 * (for every kind of Google flow, so this check stays first); the account is resolveGoogleSignIn's.
 */
export async function GET(request: NextRequest) {
  return handleOidcCallback('google', request, ['google'], async (claims, flow) => {
    if (!claims.emailVerified || !claims.email) {
      console.warn(`[signin] google: the account's address is not verified (${flow.kind} flow)`);
      return NextResponse.redirect(signInPageUrl(flow.locale, 'failed'));
    }
    const found = await resolveGoogleSignIn(claims);
    if ('status' in found) return NextResponse.redirect(signInPageUrl(flow.locale, found.status));
    return finishSignIn(found.user, 'google');
  });
}
```

## Part D: email codes

### Contract notes (corrections against the real code, and additions; names stay consistent)

1. **`finishSignIn`'s `user` is `UserConfig`** (`src/types.ts:23`), the type `verifyUserAuth` (`src/lib/api-auth.ts:24`), `getUserById` and `getUserByTelegramId` (`src/services/user-service.ts:19,31`) carry. The contract writes `User`; a Prisma `User` would need `convertPrismaUserToConfig` at every caller. This part passes a `UserConfig`.
2. **`sendCodeEmail` takes `userId: number` as well**: `sendCodeEmail(args: { to: string; code: string; locale: string; purpose: 'signin' | 'add'; userId: number })`. Without it the one success line ("sent … for user N, Resend id …") and the give-up line can't name whose code it was, and the rule is to log the user id.
3. **`issueCode` asks `takeDailySend()` before it stores the code**, not after: a spent day must not replace a code that still works with one that is never mailed.
4. **`/api/auth/email/verify` answers** `{ ok: true, redirect }` (finishSignIn's own json response, with the flow cookie cleared) or `{ ok: false, error: 'wrong' | 'restart' | 'limited' | 'suspended' | 'blocked' | 'failed' }`. Two errors are added: `'limited'` (wrong codes paused, `codeChecksBlocked`: telling the person "wrong code" while they type the right one would mislead) and `'failed'` (HTTP 500, an unexpected failure). finishSignIn's `{ ok: false, status }` is mapped to `error: status` so the client reads one field.
5. **`/api/auth/email/request` answers** `{ ok: true }` for every address, held back by a limit or not, and also for text that is no usable address (with a flow under a random key, so the screen moves on the same way). It answers otherwise only when no address can matter: `403`/`415` from `refuseCrossSite`, `503 { ok: false, error: 'unavailable' }` while `RESEND_API_KEY` or `SESSION_SECRET` is unset, `400 { ok: false, error: 'bad_request' }` for a body that is not JSON, `500 { ok: false, error: 'failed' }`.
6. **Task 3's `normalizeEmail` order is wrong in the contract** ("trim, lowercase, IDN → punycode, then ASCII only"): `'K'.toLowerCase() === 'k'` (Kelvin sign), so lowercasing first turns `Kim@example.com` written with U+212A into an ASCII `kim@example.com` and passes. The local part must be checked for ASCII on the trimmed input **before** lowercasing (the domain may be non-ASCII and goes through `domainToASCII`, then is checked). Check #2 of this part's smoke pins it.
7. **New in this part** (not in the contract): `src/services/web-signin/safe-error.ts` (`SafeSignInError`, `safeErrorSummary`, `captureSignInFailure`); `CODE_TTL_SEC`, `CODE_MAX_TRIES` in `email-code.ts`; `codeEmail`, `CodePurpose`, `RESEND_EMAILS_URL`, `SIGNIN_FROM`, `SIGNIN_REPLY_TO` in `email-send.ts`; `REDIS_KEYS.signinCode` / `REDIS_KEYS.signinCodeTries`; and three account lookups by address, `findEmailSignIn`, `emailSignInAccount` and `touchEmailSignIn`. Those three live in `src/services/web-signin/identities.ts` (Task 4 created the file; `identities.ts` is the one file that reads `SignInIdentity`), not in `email-code.ts`: Task 6's `findUserByIdentity` touches `lastUsedAt` and returns no address, and the request must not touch it (only a finished sign-in does), so the email way needs its own lookups, but not its own file. Task 6's final `identities.ts` keeps all three verbatim.
8. **The code record** at `signin:code:<purpose>:<emailKey>` is `{ hash, userId, address }` (the contract's `checkCode` returns the address). The code itself is only ever stored as `hash` = HMAC-SHA256(`appKey('signin')`, `code:<purpose>:<emailKey>:<code>`).
9. **`scripts/smoke-pause.ts`'s `SEND_CALL` is widened** with `\b(sendCodeEmail|issueCode)\(` and `api\.resend\.com\/emails` (the old pattern matches only Telegram and WhatsApp sends). So **Task 6 must add its `app/api/signin-methods/email/add/route.ts` (it calls `issueCode`) to `NOT_PAUSED`** in the same commit, or smoke-pause fails there.
10. **This smoke fakes `src/services/web-signin/limits.ts`** (scripted answers, every call recorded). It pins that the routes ask the limits in the right order, for unknown addresses too, and act on the answers; Task 3's own smoke pins the counting. The fake's `countWithin` does what the real one does (INCR, then the expiry when the key has none) on the smoke's own Redis, without tracing it as a Redis call, so the smoke can tell that `email-code.ts` counts a try only through `countWithin`.
11. **`checkCode` counts a try with `countWithin(key, windowSec)` from Task 3's `limits.ts`** (one Lua call: INCR, and EXPIRE when the key has none), not an `INCR` followed by a separate `EXPIRE`: a process that dies between the two would leave a counter that never expires. `countWithin` uses the key as given and returns the count as a number.
12. **Two code requests in one browser (review focus RF1, email variant).** Each request replaces the `famcal_signin` cookie with a new flow (`startFlow`), and a flow holds the address key it was made for. A verify reads the flow the cookie names (`peekFlow`, no consuming) and checks the code against that address only, so a code from tab 1 sent under tab 2's cookie is the generic `wrong` (counted as a wrong code for tab 2's address and the IP) and can never sign in the other flow's account; tab 2's own code still works, and a wrong try leaves the cookie alone. Asking twice for the same address leaves only the newer code working (the code record is keyed by purpose and address, not by flow). Smoke #16. Two tabs on two ways (an email code in one, Telegram or Google started in the other): the verify finds no email flow under the cookie, answers `restart` and leaves the cookie alone, so the other tab's sign-in still finishes (smoke #11; Task 3's `takeFlow` and Task 4's callback do the same the other way round).
