- [ ] **Step 1: Write the shared smoke world `scripts/lib/signin-world.ts`**

```ts
// The world the web sign-in smokes run in (smoke-signin-methods.ts, smoke-signin-calendar-match.ts): the real modules,
// with fakes at the boundaries only. Prisma and Upstash in memory (Prisma with the signInIdentity -> user relation the
// email lookups select; Upstash with the two Lua scripts the limits and countWithin run), Next's after() (queued, run by
// drainAfter()), the rate limiter (records nothing, allows), error capture (recorded), Telegram and WhatsApp (every
// send recorded, or refused on demand), the OIDC exchange (oidc.ts: scripted claims, the state checked as openid-client
// checks it), the calendar's Google account (google-sync/client.ts: scripted per refresh token), the admin notifier,
// and fetch (Resend answered and recorded; anything else blocked).
// Every console line is kept, so a smoke can check that no address, code or token reached one. No network, no DB.
// scripts/lib/ is not a smoke (ci-smokes.sh runs scripts/smoke-*.ts only).

import path from 'path';
import crypto from 'crypto';
import { createRequire } from 'module';
import { fileURLToPath } from 'url';

// eslint-disable-next-line @typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any
export type Row = Record<string, any>;

export const ROOT = path.resolve(__dirname, '..', '..');
const nodeRequire = createRequire(__filename);
export const BASE = 'https://famcal.bot';
export const DAY = 86_400_000;

// Test values only (the fake env of ci-smokes.sh leaves these unset)
process.env.SESSION_SECRET ||= 'test-session-secret';
process.env.TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN ||= '000000:fake';
process.env.ENCRYPTION_KEY ||= '0'.repeat(64);
process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL = BASE;
process.env.RESEND_API_KEY = 're_smoke_only';

// ---- Checks ----

export type Result = { name: string; ok: boolean; reason?: string };
export const results: Result[] = [];

export async function check(name: string, fn: () => void | Promise<void>): Promise<void> {
  try {
    await fn();
    results.push({ name, ok: true });
  } catch (err) {
    results.push({ name, ok: false, reason: err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err) });
  }
}

export function assert(cond: unknown, message: string): asserts cond {
  if (!cond) throw new Error(message);
}

/** JSON that can show a BigInt and survives a cycle. */
export function show(value: unknown): string {
  try {
    return JSON.stringify(value, (_k, v) => (typeof v === 'bigint' ? `${v}n` : v));
  } catch {
    return String(value);
  }
}

// ---- Console: every line is kept (this check's in `logs`, the whole run's in `everyLog`) ----

export const logs: string[] = [];
export const everyLog: string[] = [];
const realLog = console.log;
const lineOf = (args: unknown[]) => args.map(a => (typeof a === 'string' ? a : a instanceof Error ? `${a.name}: ${a.message}` : show(a))).join(' ');
for (const level of ['log', 'info', 'warn', 'error'] as const) {
  console[level] = (...args: unknown[]) => {
    const line = lineOf(args);
    logs.push(line);
    everyLog.push(line);
  };
}

export function report(): never {
  let failed = 0;
  for (const r of results) {
    realLog(`${r.ok ? 'OK' : 'FAIL'}  ${r.name}${r.ok ? '' : ` — ${r.reason}`}`);
    if (!r.ok) failed++;
  }
  if (failed) realLog(`\nlog lines of the run:\n${everyLog.map(l => `  ${l}`).join('\n')}`);
  realLog(`\n${results.length - failed}/${results.length} passed`);
  process.exit(failed ? 1 : 0);
}

// ---- Fake Prisma: in-memory tables, any model ----

export const DB: Record<string, Row[]> = {};
export const prismaCalls: string[] = [];

const num = (x: unknown) => (x instanceof Date ? x.getTime() : Number(x));
function same(a: unknown, b: unknown): boolean {
  if (a instanceof Date || b instanceof Date) return a instanceof Date && b instanceof Date && a.getTime() === b.getTime();
  if (typeof a === 'bigint' || typeof b === 'bigint') return a != null && b != null && String(a) === String(b);
  return a === b;
}
const isPlain = (v: unknown): v is Row => v !== null && typeof v === 'object' && !(v instanceof Date) && !Array.isArray(v);

function matches(row: Row, where?: Row): boolean {
  if (!where) return true;
  return Object.entries(where).every(([k, cond]) => {
    if (cond === undefined) return true;
    if (k === 'AND') return ([] as Row[]).concat(cond).every(c => matches(row, c));
    if (k === 'OR') return (cond as Row[]).some(c => matches(row, c));
    if (k === 'NOT') return !([] as Row[]).concat(cond).some(c => matches(row, c));
    // A compound unique key (kind_subject, userId_kind): its fields, all of them
    if (isPlain(cond) && k.includes('_') && !(k in row)) return matches(row, cond);
    const v = row[k];
    if (isPlain(cond)) {
      if ('equals' in cond && !same(v ?? null, cond.equals)) return false;
      if ('in' in cond && !(cond.in as unknown[]).some(x => same(v, x))) return false;
      if ('notIn' in cond && (cond.notIn as unknown[]).some(x => same(v, x))) return false;
      if ('not' in cond && (isPlain(cond.not) ? matches(row, { [k]: cond.not }) : same(v ?? null, cond.not))) return false;
      if ('startsWith' in cond && !(typeof v === 'string' && v.startsWith(String(cond.startsWith)))) return false;
      if ('gt' in cond && !(v != null && num(v) > num(cond.gt))) return false;
      if ('gte' in cond && !(v != null && num(v) >= num(cond.gte))) return false;
      if ('lt' in cond && !(v != null && num(v) < num(cond.lt))) return false;
      if ('lte' in cond && !(v != null && num(v) <= num(cond.lte))) return false;
      return true;
    }
    return same(v ?? null, cond);
  });
}

function pick(row: Row | undefined, select?: Row): Row | null {
  if (!row) return null;
  if (!select) return { ...row };
  return Object.fromEntries(Object.keys(select).filter(k => select[k]).map(k => [k, row[k]]));
}

/** The relations the code under test reads through select/include (many-to-one, by the foreign key). */
const RELATIONS: Record<string, Record<string, { table: string; fk: string }>> = {
  signInIdentity: { user: { table: 'user', fk: 'userId' } },
};

/** A row as findUnique/findFirst/findMany answer it: `select` picks columns and relations, `include` adds relations. */
function shape(name: string, row: Row | undefined, args: Row): Row | null {
  if (!row) return null;
  const relations = RELATIONS[name] ?? {};
  const related = (key: string, arg: unknown): Row | null => {
    const { table, fk } = relations[key];
    const target = (DB[table] ?? []).find(r => same(r.id, row[fk]));
    if (!target) return null;
    return isPlain(arg) && isPlain(arg.select) ? pick(target, arg.select) : { ...target };
  };
  if (args.select) {
    const columns = Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(args.select).filter(([k]) => !(k in relations)));
    const out = pick(row, columns) as Row;
    for (const key of Object.keys(relations)) if (args.select[key]) out[key] = related(key, args.select[key]);
    return out;
  }
  const out = { ...row };
  for (const key of Object.keys(relations)) if (args.include?.[key]) out[key] = related(key, args.include[key]);
  return out;
}

function sorted(rows: Row[], orderBy?: Row | Row[]): Row[] {
  const keys = ([] as Row[]).concat(orderBy ?? []).flatMap(o => Object.entries(o));
  return [...rows].sort((a, b) => {
    for (const [k, dir] of keys) {
      const d = num(a[k]) - num(b[k]);
      if (d) return dir === 'desc' ? -d : d;
    }
    return 0;
  });
}

function applyData(row: Row, data: Row) {
  for (const [k, v] of Object.entries(data)) {
    if (v === undefined) continue;
    if (isPlain(v) && 'increment' in v) row[k] = (row[k] ?? 0) + v.increment;
    else if (isPlain(v) && 'set' in v) row[k] = v.set;
    else if (isPlain(v) && ('connect' in v || 'create' in v || 'disconnect' in v)) continue;
    else row[k] = v;
  }
}

/** The unique constraints Postgres would enforce, per model (a null column never collides). */
const UNIQUE: Record<string, string[][]> = {
  signInIdentity: [['kind', 'subject'], ['userId', 'kind']],
  user: [['telegramId'], ['whatsappPhone'], ['whatsappBsuid']],
};
function assertUnique(name: string, row: Row, all: Row[]) {
  for (const cols of UNIQUE[name] ?? []) {
    if (cols.some(c => row[c] == null)) continue;
    if (all.some(o => o !== row && cols.every(c => same(o[c], row[c])))) {
      throw Object.assign(new Error(`Unique constraint failed on the fields: (${cols.join(',')})`), { code: 'P2002' });
    }
  }
}

const DEFAULTS: Record<string, () => Row> = {
  signInIdentity: () => ({ lastUsedAt: null }),
};

function model(name: string): Row {
  const t = () => (DB[name] ??= []);
  const create = (data: Row): Row => {
    const now = new Date();
    const row: Row = { id: Math.max(0, ...t().map(r => Number(r.id) || 0)) + 1, createdAt: now, updatedAt: now, ...(DEFAULTS[name]?.() ?? {}) };
    applyData(row, data);
    assertUnique(name, row, t());
    t().push(row);
    return row;
  };
  const writeOne = (row: Row, data: Row) => {
    const next = { ...row };
    applyData(next, data);
    assertUnique(name, next, t().filter(r => r !== row));
    Object.assign(row, next);
    if ('updatedAt' in row) row.updatedAt = new Date();
  };
  const impl: Row = {
    findUnique: async (a: Row = {}) => shape(name, t().find(r => matches(r, a.where)), a),
    findFirst: async (a: Row = {}) => shape(name, sorted(t().filter(r => matches(r, a.where)), a.orderBy)[0], a),
    findMany: async (a: Row = {}) =>
      sorted(t().filter(r => matches(r, a.where)), a.orderBy).slice(0, a.take ?? undefined).map(r => shape(name, r, a)),
    count: async (a: Row = {}) => t().filter(r => matches(r, a.where)).length,
    create: async (a: Row) => pick(create(a.data), a.select),
    update: async (a: Row) => {
      const row = t().find(r => matches(r, a.where));
      if (!row) throw Object.assign(new Error(`No ${name} record was found for an update.`), { code: 'P2025' });
      writeOne(row, a.data);
      return pick(row, a.select);
    },
    // Checks and sets in one tick, as a single UPDATE ... WHERE does.
    updateMany: async (a: Row) => {
      const rows = t().filter(r => matches(r, a.where));
      rows.forEach(r => writeOne(r, a.data));
      return { count: rows.length };
    },
    upsert: async (a: Row) => {
      const row = t().find(r => matches(r, a.where));
      if (row) {
        writeOne(row, a.update);
        return pick(row, a.select);
      }
      return pick(create({ ...a.where, ...a.create }), a.select);
    },
    delete: async (a: Row) => {
      const i = t().findIndex(r => matches(r, a.where));
      if (i < 0) throw Object.assign(new Error(`No ${name} record to delete`), { code: 'P2025' });
      return t().splice(i, 1)[0];
    },
    deleteMany: async (a: Row = {}) => {
      const keep = t().filter(r => !matches(r, a.where));
      const count = t().length - keep.length;
      DB[name] = keep;
      return { count };
    },
  };
  return Object.fromEntries(
    Object.entries(impl).map(([k, fn]) => [k, (...args: unknown[]) => { prismaCalls.push(`${name}.${k}`); return fn(...args); }]),
  );
}

const models: Record<string, Row> = {};
export const fakePrisma: Row = new Proxy({} as Row, {
  get(_t, prop) {
    if (typeof prop !== 'string' || prop === 'then') return undefined;
    if (prop === '$transaction') {
      return async (arg: unknown) => {
        prismaCalls.push('$transaction');
        return typeof arg === 'function' ? arg(fakePrisma) : Promise.all(arg as Promise<unknown>[]);
      };
    }
    if (prop.startsWith('$')) return async () => undefined;
    return (models[prop] ??= model(prop));
  },
});

// ---- Fake Upstash Redis (it parses JSON on read). An unknown command throws, so a smoke shows what it needs. ----

export const redisStore = new Map<string, string>();
/** The sets the capped-set Lua script (Task 3's Add email account limit) keeps; a set is no string, so it lives apart. */
const redisSets = new Map<string, Set<string>>();
const decode = (raw: string | undefined) => {
  if (raw === undefined) return null;
  try { return JSON.parse(raw); } catch { return raw; }
};
const encode = (v: unknown) => (typeof v === 'string' ? v : JSON.stringify(v));
const glob = (pattern: string) => new RegExp(`^${pattern.replace(/[.+^${}()|[\]\\]/g, '\\$&').replace(/\*/g, '.*').replace(/\?/g, '.')}$`);
const incrBy = (k: string, n: number) => {
  const next = Number(redisStore.get(k) ?? 0) + n;
  redisStore.set(k, String(next));
  return next;
};
const redisImpl: Row = {
  get: async (k: string) => decode(redisStore.get(k)),
  set: async (k: string, v: unknown, o?: Row) => {
    if (o?.nx && redisStore.has(k)) return null;
    redisStore.set(k, encode(v));
    return 'OK';
  },
  del: async (...ks: unknown[]) => ks.flat().reduce((n: number, k) => n + (redisStore.delete(String(k)) ? 1 : 0), 0),
  // Reads and deletes in one tick, as GETDEL does.
  getdel: async (k: string) => { const raw = redisStore.get(k); redisStore.delete(k); return decode(raw); },
  incr: async (k: string) => incrBy(k, 1),
  incrby: async (k: string, n: number) => incrBy(k, Number(n)),
  decr: async (k: string) => incrBy(k, -1),
  expire: async (k: string) => (redisStore.has(k) ? 1 : 0),
  pexpire: async (k: string) => (redisStore.has(k) ? 1 : 0),
  expireat: async (k: string) => (redisStore.has(k) ? 1 : 0),
  ttl: async (k: string) => (redisStore.has(k) ? 600 : -2),
  pttl: async (k: string) => (redisStore.has(k) ? 600_000 : -2),
  exists: async (...ks: unknown[]) => ks.flat().filter(k => redisStore.has(String(k))).length,
  mget: async (...ks: unknown[]) => ks.flat().map(k => decode(redisStore.get(String(k)))),
  scan: async (_cursor: unknown, o?: Row) => [0, [...redisStore.keys()].filter(k => !o?.match || glob(String(o.match)).test(k))],
  keys: async (pattern: string) => [...redisStore.keys()].filter(k => glob(pattern).test(k)),
  // The two Lua scripts the code under test runs (Task 3's limits, Task 5's countWithin): a counter, and a set with a
  // cap. The fake has no clock, so an expiry is not modelled; any other script throws, so a smoke shows what it needs.
  eval: async (script: string, keys: string[], args: string[]) => {
    const [key] = keys;
    if (script.includes("'SADD'")) {
      const set = redisSets.get(key) ?? new Set<string>();
      const added = !set.has(args[0]);
      set.add(args[0]);
      redisSets.set(key, set);
      if (added && set.size > Number(args[2])) {
        set.delete(args[0]);
        return 0;
      }
      return 1;
    }
    if (script.includes("'INCR'")) return incrBy(key, 1);
    throw new Error(`the fake Redis does not know this script: ${script.slice(0, 60)}`);
  },
};
const batch = () => {
  const ops: [string, unknown[]][] = [];
  const chain: Row = new Proxy({} as Row, {
    get: (_t, name) => {
      if (name === 'then' || typeof name !== 'string') return undefined;
      if (name === 'exec') {
        return async () => {
          const out: unknown[] = [];
          for (const [op, args] of ops) out.push(await fakeRedis[op](...args));
          return out;
        };
      }
      return (...args: unknown[]) => { ops.push([name, args]); return chain; };
    },
  });
  return chain;
};
redisImpl.pipeline = batch;
redisImpl.multi = batch;
export const fakeRedis: Row = new Proxy(redisImpl, {
  get: (t, p) => (typeof p !== 'string' || p === 'then' ? undefined : t[p] ?? (() => { throw new Error(`the fake Redis has no ${p}()`); })),
});

// ---- What the world saw ----

/** Next's after(): its task is queued while the request runs, and run by drainAfter() (the sign-in request mails after its answer). */
const afterQueue: (() => unknown)[] = [];
export async function drainAfter(): Promise<void> {
  while (afterQueue.length) await afterQueue.shift()!();
}

export const sent: { platform: 'telegram' | 'whatsapp'; chatId: string; text: string }[] = [];
export const captured: { context: string; message: string; extra: Row }[] = [];
export const everyCapture: { context: string; message: string; extra: Row }[] = [];
export const mails: { to: string[]; body: Row; idempotencyKey: string | null }[] = [];
export const everyMail: { to: string[]; body: Row; idempotencyKey: string | null }[] = [];

/** The scripted boundaries. A check sets what it needs after resetWorld(). */
export const world = {
  telegramFails: false,
  whatsappFails: false,
  oidc: { telegram: true, google: true } as Record<string, boolean>,
  /** What Google's token says (finishAuthorization's answer) */
  claims: null as Row | null,
  /** The calendar account per refresh token: an address, an Error to throw, or a function run at the ask */
  accounts: {} as Record<string, string | Error | (() => string)>,
  /** The refresh tokens Google was asked about, in order */
  googleAsks: [] as string[],
};

export function resetWorld(): void {
  for (const k of Object.keys(DB)) delete DB[k];
  redisStore.clear();
  redisSets.clear();
  afterQueue.length = 0;
  prismaCalls.length = 0;
  sent.length = 0;
  captured.length = 0;
  mails.length = 0;
  logs.length = 0;
  Object.assign(world, { telegramFails: false, whatsappFails: false, oidc: { telegram: true, google: true }, claims: null, accounts: {}, googleAsks: [] });
}

function chatService(platform: 'telegram' | 'whatsapp'): Row {
  const service: Row = {
    sendMessage: async (chatId: unknown, text: string) => {
      if (platform === 'telegram' ? world.telegramFails : world.whatsappFails) throw new Error(`${platform} refused the send (smoke)`);
      sent.push({ platform, chatId: String(chatId), text });
      return platform === 'telegram' ? 1 : 'wamid.smoke';
    },
  };
  return new Proxy(service, {
    get: (t, p) => (typeof p !== 'string' || p === 'then' ? undefined : t[p] ?? (() => { throw new Error(`the fake ${platform} service has no ${p}()`); })),
  });
}

let identitySeq = 1000;

export function baseUser(o: Row): Row {
  return {
    name: 'x', englishName: '', gender: 'male', language: 'en', location: 'Tel Aviv', culture: 'default',
    messagingPlatform: 'telegram', googleRefreshToken: '', googleScopes: [], calendarAssignments: null, calendarSource: 'NATIVE',
    pairingId: null, remindersEnabled: false, suspendedAt: null, unreachableSince: null, whatsappPhone: null, whatsappBsuid: null,
    telegramId: null, isAdmin: false, globalRules: [], voiceInputEnabled: true, textSummaryEnabled: true, voiceSummaryEnabled: false,
    weatherEnabled: true, sessionsValidAfter: null, googleAccountKey: null, googleCalendarSignIn: true,
    createdAt: new Date(Date.now() - 30 * DAY), updatedAt: new Date(Date.now() - DAY),
    ...o,
  };
}

export function identityRow(o: Row): Row {
  return { id: ++identitySeq, createdAt: new Date(Date.now() - DAY), lastUsedAt: null, ...o };
}

/** Valid Telegram initData for a Telegram user id, signed with the bot token. */
export function initDataFor(tgId: number): string {
  const params: Record<string, string> = {
    auth_date: String(Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000)),
    query_id: 'AAH-smoke',
    user: JSON.stringify({ id: tgId, first_name: 'Test' }),
  };
  const checkString = Object.keys(params).sort().map(k => `${k}=${params[k]}`).join('\n');
  const secret = crypto.createHmac('sha256', 'WebAppData').update(process.env.TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN ?? '').digest();
  const hash = crypto.createHmac('sha256', secret).update(checkString).digest('hex');
  return [...Object.entries(params), ['hash', hash]].map(([k, v]) => `${k}=${encodeURIComponent(v)}`).join('&');
}

export const load = (rel: string): Promise<Row> => import(path.join(ROOT, rel));

/** A request to famcal.bot: JSON, from famcal.bot (origin: null sends none, or another one), with the client address set. */
export function request(url: string, o: { method?: string; body?: unknown; cookie?: string; initData?: string; origin?: string | null } = {}): Row {
  const { NextRequest } = nodeRequire('next/server');
  const headers: Record<string, string> = { 'content-type': 'application/json', 'x-real-ip': '203.0.113.9', 'accept-language': 'en' };
  if (o.origin !== null) headers.origin = o.origin ?? BASE;
  if (o.cookie) headers.cookie = o.cookie;
  if (o.initData) headers['x-telegram-init-data'] = o.initData;
  return new NextRequest(`${BASE}${url}`, {
    method: o.method ?? (o.body === undefined ? 'GET' : 'POST'),
    headers,
    body: o.body === undefined ? undefined : JSON.stringify(o.body),
  });
}

/** The session cookie header for a person, as the finishing step sets it. */
export async function sessionCookie(userId: number, method: string, signedInAt = Date.now() - 60_000): Promise<string> {
  const { createSessionToken, SESSION_COOKIE_NAME } = await load('src/lib/session-auth.ts');
  return `${SESSION_COOKIE_NAME}=${createSessionToken(userId, method, signedInAt)}`;
}

/** The flow cookie header for a one-time sign-in flow, as a start route sets it. */
export async function flowCookie(flow: Row): Promise<string> {
  const { NextResponse } = nodeRequire('next/server');
  const { startFlow, SIGNIN_COOKIE_NAME } = await load('src/services/web-signin/flow.ts');
  const res = NextResponse.json({});
  await startFlow(res, flow);
  const value = res.cookies.get(SIGNIN_COOKIE_NAME)?.value;
  if (!value) throw new Error('startFlow set no cookie');
  return `${SIGNIN_COOKIE_NAME}=${value}`;
}

export async function body(res: Response): Promise<Row> {
  try { return await res.clone().json(); } catch { return { nonJson: true }; }
}

export async function installSigninWorld(): Promise<void> {
  const types = await load('src/services/messaging/types.ts');
  // A stub goes into require's cache (static imports) and is served to import() by a load hook.
  const Module = nodeRequire('module');
  const stubs: Record<string, Row> = {};
  (globalThis as Row).__signinStubs = stubs;
  if (typeof Module.registerHooks !== 'function') throw new Error('This smoke needs Node 22.15+ (module.registerHooks)');
  Module.registerHooks({
    load(url: string, context: unknown, nextLoad: (u: string, c: unknown) => unknown) {
      const file = url.startsWith('file:') ? fileURLToPath(url.split('?')[0]) : '';
      if (!(file in stubs)) return nextLoad(url, context);
      const names = Object.keys(stubs[file]).filter(n => n !== 'default' && /^[A-Za-z_$][\w$]*$/.test(n));
      const source = [
        `const s = globalThis.__signinStubs[${JSON.stringify(file)}];`,
        ...names.map(n => `export const ${n} = s[${JSON.stringify(n)}];`),
        'export default (s.__esModule ? s.default : s);',
      ].join('\n');
      return { format: 'module', source, shortCircuit: true };
    },
  });
  const stub = (rel: string, exports: Row) => {
    const filename = path.join(ROOT, rel);
    stubs[filename] = exports;
    const mod = new Module(filename);
    Object.assign(mod, { filename, loaded: true, exports });
    Module._cache[filename] = mod;
  };

  stub('src/utils/prisma.ts', { prisma: fakePrisma, withRetry: (fn: () => unknown) => fn() });
  stub('src/utils/redis.ts', { redis: fakeRedis });
  const limiter = (name: string) => ({ name });
  stub('src/lib/rate-limit.ts', {
    commandRateLimiter: limiter('command'), settingsRateLimiter: limiter('settings'), generalRateLimiter: limiter('general'),
    tokenPollRateLimiter: limiter('token-poll'), calendarRateLimiter: limiter('calendar'), reminderActionRateLimiter: limiter('reminder-action'),
    calendarWriteRateLimiter: limiter('calendar-write'),
    checkRateLimit: async () => ({ success: true, limit: 99, remaining: 99, reset: 0 }),
    getRateLimitHeaders: () => ({}),
  });
  const capture = (e: unknown, context: string, extra: Row = {}) => {
    const entry = { context, message: e instanceof Error ? e.message : String(e), extra };
    captured.push(entry);
    everyCapture.push(entry);
  };
  stub('src/lib/error-capture.ts', {
    captureError: capture,
    captureWarning: (message: string, context: string, extra?: Row) => capture(new Error(message), context, extra),
    captureInfo: () => undefined,
  });
  stub('src/utils/error-notifier.ts', {
    getAdminUserIds: async () => [], notifyAdminError: async () => undefined, notifyAdminWarning: async () => undefined, notifyAdminFeedback: async () => undefined,
  });
  const telegram = { getBot: () => ({}), initBot: () => ({}), getMessagingService: () => chatService('telegram'), setUserMenuButton: async () => undefined };
  stub('src/services/telegram/bot.ts', telegram);
  stub('src/services/telegram/index.ts', telegram);
  const messaging = {
    ...types,
    getWhatsAppService: () => chatService('whatsapp'),
    getTelegramService: () => chatService('telegram'),
    getMessagingService: (platform: unknown) => chatService(platform === 'whatsapp' ? 'whatsapp' : 'telegram'),
    detectPlatform: () => 'telegram',
  };
  stub('src/services/messaging/index.ts', messaging);
  stub('src/services/messaging/factory.ts', messaging);
  // The OIDC exchange: openid-client and the network never load. The state is checked as authorizationCodeGrant does.
  const random = () => crypto.randomBytes(32).toString('base64url');

    providerConfigured: (provider: string) => world.oidc[provider] === true,
    newOidcChecks: () => ({ state: random(), nonce: random(), codeVerifier: random() }),
    redirectUri: (provider: string) => `${BASE}/api/auth/${provider}/callback`,
    describeOidcError: (error: unknown) => (error instanceof Error ? error.name : 'unknown'),
    authorizationUrl: async (provider: string, flow: Row) =>
      new URL(provider === 'google'
        ? `https://accounts.google.com/o/oauth2/v2/auth?state=${flow.state}&nonce=${flow.nonce}`
        : `https://oauth.telegram.org/auth?state=${flow.state}`),
    finishAuthorization: async (_provider: string, callbackUrl: URL, flow: Row) => {

      }

      },
    }),
    CALLS_PER_RUN: 100,
    counted: async (_budget: unknown, call: () => Promise<unknown>) => call(),
    BudgetSpent: class BudgetSpent extends Error {},
    __useSyncGoogleForTests: () => undefined,
  });

  // after() works only inside a request: queue its task for drainAfter()
  nodeRequire('next/server').after = (task: unknown) => {
    afterQueue.push(typeof task === 'function' ? (task as () => unknown) : () => task);
  };

  // fetch: Resend is answered and its request recorded; everything else is blocked.
  globalThis.fetch = (async (input: unknown, init?: RequestInit) => {
    const url = input instanceof Request ? input.url : String(input);
    if (url === 'https://api.resend.com/emails') {
      const raw = input instanceof Request ? await input.text() : String(init?.body ?? '');
      const parsed: Row = JSON.parse(raw || '{}');
      const headers = new Headers(input instanceof Request ? input.headers : init?.headers);
      const mail = { to: ([] as string[]).concat(parsed.to ?? []), body: parsed, idempotencyKey: headers.get('idempotency-key') };
      mails.push(mail);
      everyMail.push(mail);
      return new Response(JSON.stringify({ id: `re_smoke_${everyMail.length}` }), { status: 200, headers: { 'content-type': 'application/json' } });
    }
    throw new Error(`network blocked in smoke: ${url}`);
  }) as typeof fetch;
}
```

```ts
    assert(/^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{32}$/.test(token), `token ${token}`);
    const stored = [...redisStore.entries()].map(([k, v]) => `${k}=${v}`).join('\n');
    assert(!stored.includes(token) && [...redisStore.keys()].some(k => k.startsWith('signin:add-google:')), `Redis:\n${stored}`);
    const n = await addLink(NOA_TG, noa);
    assert(n.status === 409 && (await body(n)).error === 'has-one', `Noa ${n.status} ${show(await body(n))}`);
    world.oidc.google = false;
    const off = await addLink(TAL_TG, tal);
    assert(off.status === 409 && (await body(off)).error === 'unavailable', `off ${off.status} ${show(await body(off))}`);
  });

  await check('#18 only Continue uses the link up: looking at it (the page) twice keeps it; add-start answers Google\'s URL with the flow cookie; a second Continue is expired', async () => {
    seed();
    const token = tokenOf((await body(await addLink(TAL_TG, tal))).url);
    assert(show(await addGoogle.peekAddGoogleToken(token)) === show({ userId: TAL }), 'first look');
    assert(show(await addGoogle.peekAddGoogleToken(token)) === show({ userId: TAL }), 'second look');
    const start = await addStart(token);
    const sb = await body(start);
    assert(start.status === 200 && new URL(sb.url).host === 'accounts.google.com', `add-start ${start.status} ${show(sb)}`);
    assert(start.cookies.get(SIGNIN_COOKIE_NAME)?.value, 'no flow cookie');
    const again = await addStart(token);
    assert(again.status === 410 && (await body(again)).error === 'expired', `again ${again.status} ${show(await body(again))}`);
    assert(await addGoogle.peekAddGoogleToken(token) === null && await addGoogle.peekAddGoogleToken('not-a-token') === null, 'a used link still reads');
  });

  await check('#19 [guard] a Continue from another site is refused and leaves the link usable', async () => {
    seed();
    const token = tokenOf((await body(await addLink(TAL_TG, tal))).url);
    const evil = await addStart(token, { origin: 'https://evil.example' });
    assert(evil.status === 403, `evil ${evil.status}`);
    assert((await addStart(token)).status === 200, 'the link was used up by the refused request');
  });

  await check('#20 Google\'s answer to Add Google attaches the account (sub, the verified address, used now), sends the masked notice, signs this browser in as that account, and clears the flow cookie', async () => {
    seed();
    const { state, cookie } = await continueAddGoogle(TAL_TG, tal);
    world.claims = { sub: 'g-tal', email: 'tal@gmail.com', emailVerified: true };
    const res = await callback(state, cookie);
    assert(pathOf(res) === '/dashboard?user_id=9', `location ${location(res)}; captured ${show(captured)}`);
    const session = validateSessionToken(res.cookies.get(SESSION_COOKIE_NAME)?.value ?? '');
    assert(session?.userId === TAL && session.method === 'google', `session ${show(session)}`);
    const [way] = identitiesOf(TAL);
    assert(way?.kind === 'google' && way.subject === 'g-tal' && way.address === 'tal@gmail.com' && way.lastUsedAt instanceof Date, `way ${show(way)}`);
    assert(sent.length === 1 && sent[0].chatId === String(TAL_TG) && sent[0].text.includes('t•••@gmail.com') && !sent[0].text.includes('tal@gmail.com'), `sent ${show(sent)}`);
    assert(!res.cookies.get(SIGNIN_COOKIE_NAME)?.value, `flow cookie ${show(res.cookies.get(SIGNIN_COOKIE_NAME))}`);
  });

  await check('#21 a Google account another FamCal account signs in with is refused (status=taken): nothing attached, no notice, no session', async () => {
    seed();
    const { state, cookie } = await continueAddGoogle(TAL_TG, tal);
    world.claims = { sub: 'g-noa', email: 'noa@gmail.com', emailVerified: true };
    const res = await callback(state, cookie);
    assert(location(res).includes('status=taken'), `location ${location(res)}`);
    assert(identitiesOf(TAL).length === 0 && sent.length === 0 && !res.cookies.get(SESSION_COOKIE_NAME)?.value, `ways ${show(identitiesOf(TAL))} sent ${show(sent)}`);
  });

  await check('#22 an address Google has not verified is refused (status=failed), nothing attached', async () => {
    seed();
    const { state, cookie } = await continueAddGoogle(TAL_TG, tal);
    world.claims = { sub: 'g-tal', email: 'tal@gmail.com', emailVerified: false };
    const res = await callback(state, cookie);
    assert(location(res).includes('status=failed') && identitiesOf(TAL).length === 0 && sent.length === 0, `location ${location(res)}`);
  });

  await check('#23 [guard] a callback without this browser\'s flow says start again (restart); a state that is not the flow\'s says restart too (Task 4\'s handleOidcCallback), and the flow is then used up', async () => {
    seed();
    world.claims = { sub: 'g-tal', email: 'tal@gmail.com', emailVerified: true };
    assert(location(await callback('anything')).includes('status=restart'), 'no flow cookie');
    const { state, cookie } = await continueAddGoogle(TAL_TG, tal);
    assert(location(await callback(`${state}x`, cookie)).includes('status=restart'), 'a wrong state');
    assert(location(await callback(state, cookie)).includes('status=restart'), 'the flow worked twice');
    assert(identitiesOf(TAL).length === 0, `ways ${show(identitiesOf(TAL))}`);
  });

  await check('#24 a later "Continue with Google" with the added account signs in and moves its last-used date, with no notice; a Google account nobody added gets no-account', async () => {
    seed();
    DB.signInIdentity.push(identityRow({ userId: TAL, kind: 'google', subject: 'g-tal', address: 'tal@gmail.com' }));
    world.claims = { sub: 'g-tal', email: 'tal@gmail.com', emailVerified: true };
    const res = await callback('st-1', await flowCookie({ kind: 'google', state: 'st-1', nonce: 'n-1', codeVerifier: 'v'.repeat(43), locale: 'en' }));
    assert(pathOf(res) === '/dashboard?user_id=9', `location ${location(res)}; captured ${show(captured)}`);
    assert(identitiesOf(TAL)[0].lastUsedAt instanceof Date && sent.length === 0, `way ${show(identitiesOf(TAL))} sent ${show(sent)}`);
    world.claims = { sub: 'g-nobody', email: 'nobody@gmail.com', emailVerified: true };
    const none = await callback('st-2', await flowCookie({ kind: 'google', state: 'st-2', nonce: 'n-2', codeVerifier: 'w'.repeat(43), locale: 'en' }));
    assert(location(none).includes('status=no-account'), `location ${location(none)}`);
  });

  // ---- Remove keeps a WhatsApp link's expiry (ruling R4) ----

  await check('#25 [R4] a WhatsApp link session that removes a way gets a fresh cookie that keeps the link\'s own expiry and only the seconds left (never renewed); a web session\'s fresh cookie gets a full new life', async () => {
    seed();
    DB.signInIdentity.push(identityRow({ userId: DANA, kind: 'email', subject: 'dana@example.com', address: 'dana@example.com' }));
    const exp = Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000) + 3600;
    const old = `${SESSION_COOKIE_NAME}=${createSessionToken(DANA, 'wa', Date.now() - 60_000, { exp })}`;
    const res = await remove(DANA, 'email', { cookie: old });
    assert(res.status === 200 && (await body(res)).ok === true, `remove ${res.status} ${show(await body(res))}`);
    const cookie = res.cookies.get(SESSION_COOKIE_NAME);
    const session = validateSessionToken(cookie?.value ?? '');
    assert(session?.method === 'wa' && session.exp === exp, `exp ${session?.exp}, wanted ${exp}`);
    assert(typeof cookie?.maxAge === 'number' && cookie.maxAge > 3500 && cookie.maxAge <= 3600, `maxAge ${cookie?.maxAge}`);
    const again = await list(DANA, { cookie: `${SESSION_COOKIE_NAME}=${cookie?.value}` });
    assert(again.status === 200, `the cookie it got is refused: ${again.status}`);
    seed();
    DB.signInIdentity.push(identityRow({ userId: TAL, kind: 'email', subject: 'tal@example.com', address: 'tal@example.com' }));
    const web = await remove(TAL, 'email', { cookie: await sessionCookie(TAL, 'google') });
    const fresh = validateSessionToken(web.cookies.get(SESSION_COOKIE_NAME)?.value ?? '');
    assert(fresh?.method === 'google' && fresh.exp - fresh.iat === SESSION_TTL_SEC.web, `web session ${show(fresh)}`);
  });

  // ---- addIdentity's answers (ruling R10) and a refused account (ruling R5) ----

  await check('#26 [R10] Add Google with the Google account this same account already holds signs it in with no second notice and adds no row (kept)', async () => {
    seed();
    DB.signInIdentity.push(identityRow({ userId: TAL, kind: 'google', subject: 'g-tal', address: 'tal@gmail.com' }));
    world.claims = { sub: 'g-tal', email: 'tal@gmail.com', emailVerified: true };
    const cookie = await flowCookie({ kind: 'add-google', state: 'st-k', nonce: 'n-k', codeVerifier: 'k'.repeat(43), locale: 'en', userId: TAL });
    const res = await callback('st-k', cookie);
    assert(pathOf(res) === '/dashboard?user_id=9', `location ${location(res)}; captured ${show(captured)}`);
    assert(sent.length === 0 && identitiesOf(TAL).length === 1, `sent ${show(sent)} ways ${show(identitiesOf(TAL))}`);
    assert(validateSessionToken(res.cookies.get(SESSION_COOKIE_NAME)?.value ?? '')?.userId === TAL, 'no session');
  });

  await check('#27 an account that got a Google way between the link and the callback is refused there (status=has-one): the second Google account is not attached, no notice, no session', async () => {
    seed();
    const { state, cookie } = await continueAddGoogle(TAL_TG, tal);
    DB.signInIdentity.push(identityRow({ userId: TAL, kind: 'google', subject: 'g-old', address: 'old@gmail.com' }));
    world.claims = { sub: 'g-new', email: 'tal@gmail.com', emailVerified: true };
    const res = await callback(state, cookie);
    assert(location(res).includes('status=has-one'), `location ${location(res)}`);
    assert(identitiesOf(TAL).length === 1 && sent.length === 0 && !res.cookies.get(SESSION_COOKIE_NAME)?.value, `ways ${show(identitiesOf(TAL))} sent ${show(sent)}`);
  });

  await check('#28 [R5] a banned account (its Telegram id is on the block list) or a suspended one gets no Google way and no notice from Add Google: the callback lands on its page (status=blocked / suspended), with no session', async () => {
    for (const refusal of ['blocked', 'suspended']) {
      seed();
      const { state, cookie } = await continueAddGoogle(TAL_TG, tal);
      if (refusal === 'blocked') DB.blockedIdentifier = [{ id: 1, telegramId: BigInt(TAL_TG), whatsappPhone: null, createdAt: new Date() }];
      else userRow(TAL).suspendedAt = new Date();
      world.claims = { sub: 'g-tal', email: 'tal@gmail.com', emailVerified: true };
      const res = await callback(state, cookie);
      assert(location(res).includes(`status=${refusal}`), `${refusal}: location ${location(res)}`);
      assert(identitiesOf(TAL).length === 0 && sent.length === 0 && !res.cookies.get(SESSION_COOKIE_NAME)?.value, `${refusal}: ways ${show(identitiesOf(TAL))} sent ${show(sent)}`);
    }
  });

  // ---- The same address typed two ways (Review Focus RF3), through Task 5's real request and verify routes ----

  await check('#29 [RF3] Add typed "  Dana@Example.COM " and Sign in typed "dana@example.com" are one emailKey: the sign-in code goes to the stored address, and the right code signs that account in (in its own language)', async () => {
    seed();
    const dana: Auth = { cookie: await sessionCookie(DANA, 'wa') };
    const code = await startAdd(DANA, '  Dana@Example.COM ', dana);
    const added = pendingKey(DANA);
    assert(added === emailKey('dana@example.com'), 'the pending Add email is under another key than the normalised address');
    assert((await confirm(DANA, code, dana)).status === 200, 'Add email did not finish');
    assert(identitiesOf(DANA)[0]?.subject === 'dana@example.com', `way ${show(identitiesOf(DANA))}`);
    aMinutePasses();
    const asked = await askForCode('dana@example.com');
    assert(asked.res.status === 200 && (await body(asked.res)).ok === true, `request ${asked.res.status}`);
    assert(asked.mail && show(asked.mail.to) === show(['dana@example.com']), `mailed ${show(asked.mail?.to)}`);
    assert(show(flowKeys()) === show([added]), `flow keys ${show(flowKeys())}, Add email's ${added}`);
    const verify = await verifyRoute.POST(request('/api/auth/email/verify', {
      body: { code: codeIn(asked.mail) },
      cookie: `${SIGNIN_COOKIE_NAME}=${asked.res.cookies.get(SIGNIN_COOKIE_NAME)?.value}`,
    }));
    const vb = await body(verify);
    assert(verify.status === 200 && vb.ok === true && String(vb.redirect).includes('/he/dashboard?user_id=42'), `verify ${verify.status} ${show(vb)}`);
    const session = validateSessionToken(verify.cookies.get(SESSION_COOKIE_NAME)?.value ?? '');
    assert(session?.userId === DANA && session.method === 'email', `session ${show(session)}`);
  });

  await check('#30 [RF3] the reverse: Add typed "tal@example.com" and Sign in typed "  TAL@Example.com " are one emailKey, and the code goes to the stored address', async () => {
    seed();
    const code = await startAdd(TAL_TG, 'tal@example.com', tal);
    const added = pendingKey(TAL);
    assert((await confirm(TAL_TG, code, tal)).status === 200, 'Add email did not finish');
    assert(added === emailKey(normalizeEmail('  TAL@Example.com ')), 'the two spellings have two keys');
    aMinutePasses();
    const asked = await askForCode('  TAL@Example.com ');
    assert(asked.mail && show(asked.mail.to) === show(['tal@example.com']), `mailed ${show(asked.mail?.to)}`);
    assert(show(flowKeys()) === show([added]), `flow keys ${show(flowKeys())}, Add email's ${added}`);
  });

  await check('#31 [RF3] a Kelvin-sign look-alike (ta + U+212A + l@example.com) is refused in both: Add answers invalid with no mail, and Sign in mails nothing to the ASCII address it lowercases to (takl@example.com) while the real address still gets its code', async () => {
    seed();
    DB.user.push(baseUser({ id: 50, name: 'Kay', telegramId: BigInt(555555555) }));
    DB.signInIdentity.push(identityRow({ userId: 50, kind: 'email', subject: 'takl@example.com', address: 'takl@example.com' }));
    const kelvin = 'taKl@example.com';
    const add = await addEmail(TAL_TG, kelvin, tal);
    assert(add.status === 400 && (await body(add)).error === 'invalid' && mails.length === 0, `add ${add.status} ${show(await body(add))}, mails ${mails.length}`);
    const asked = await askForCode(kelvin);
    assert(asked.res.status === 200 && (await body(asked.res)).ok === true && asked.mail === null && mails.length === 0, `sign in ${asked.res.status}, mails ${show(mails.map(m => m.to))}`);
    assert(!flowKeys().includes(emailKey('takl@example.com')), "the Kelvin address got the ASCII look-alike's key");
    const control = await askForCode('takl@example.com');
    assert(control.mail && show(control.mail.to) === show(['takl@example.com']), `the real address: ${show(control.mail?.to)}`);
  });

  // ---- Words and logs ----

  await check('#32 the notice names Settings\' path in the words of the Settings screen, in all three catalogues: "Sign in on the web" / "Remove", "כניסה מהדפדפן" / "הסרה", «Вход через браузер» / «Убрать»', async () => {
    const read = (lang: string): Row => JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(path.join(ROOT, 'messages', `${lang}.json`), 'utf8')).signinNotice;
    const want: Record<string, string[]> = {
      en: ['Settings → Sign in on the web → Remove'],
      he: ['הגדרות ← כניסה מהדפדפן ← הסרה'],
      ru: ['«Настройки» → «Вход через браузер» → «Убрать»'],
    };
    for (const lang of ['en', 'he', 'ru']) {
      const notice = read(lang);
      for (const key of ['addedGoogle', 'addedEmail', 'calendarGoogle']) {
        assert(want[lang].every(w => String(notice[key]).includes(w)), `${lang}.${key}: ${notice[key]}`);
      }
    }
  });

  await check('#33 a body that is not JSON is logged as a fact (never the parse message) and read as no body: Add email answers invalid and mails nothing', async () => {
    seed();
    const res = await addRoute.POST(request(`/api/signin-methods/email/add?user_id=${TAL_TG}`, { method: 'POST', ...tal }));
    assert(res.status === 400 && (await body(res)).error === 'invalid' && mails.length === 0, `status ${res.status} ${show(await body(res))}`);
    assert(logs.some(l => l.includes('[signin-methods] the body is not JSON')) && !logs.some(l => /unexpected end of json|json input/i.test(l)), `logs ${show(logs)}`);
  });

  await check('#34 no console line and no capture holds an email address, a sign-in code or an Add Google token', () => {
    const text = [...everyLog, ...everyCapture.map(c => `${c.context} ${c.message} ${show(c.extra)}`)].join('\n').toLowerCase();
    const addresses = ['tal@example.com', 'noa@example.com', 'dana@example.com', 'takl@example.com', 'tal@gmail.com', 'noa@gmail.com', 'old@gmail.com', 'nobody@gmail.com', 'noa2@example.com'];
    const found = addresses.filter(a => text.includes(a));
    const codes = everyMail.map(codeIn).filter(code => new RegExp(`\\b${code}\\b`).test(text));
    const tokens = addTokens.filter(t => t && text.includes(t.toLowerCase()));
    assert(found.length === 0 && codes.length === 0 && tokens.length === 0, `leaked: ${show({ found, codes, tokens })}`);
  });

  report();
}

// The harness captures console.*, so a crash is written straight to stdout.
main().catch(err => {
  process.stdout.write(`${err instanceof Error ? err.stack : String(err)}\n`);
  process.exit(1);
});
```

- [ ] **Step 5: Write the full `src/services/web-signin/identities.ts`** (replaces Task 4's file with Task 5's three email lookups in it; those three stay exactly as Task 5 wrote them)

```ts
/**
 * The ways a FamCal account signs in on the web besides Telegram (web sign-in spec §2.12, §4): one Google account and
 * one email per person, each on one account only (SignInIdentity, unique on (kind, subject) and on (userId, kind)).
 * Google is keyed on its account id (sub), never on the address; an email on its normalised form
 * (normalizeEmail). A way is added only from a proved account (Settings' Add email and Add Google) or by the calendar
 * match (calendar-account.ts), never by matching an address someone typed.
 *
 * This file is the one home of SignInIdentity access (besides the account merge in account-linking.ts), email lookups
 * by address included: the sign-in request looks an address up without touching lastUsedAt (only a finished sign-in
 * does), so those three lookups are separate from findUserByIdentity.
 *
 * No log line here holds a subject or an address: the user id and the kind only.
 */

import { prisma } from '../../utils/prisma';
import { captureError } from '../../lib/error-capture';
import { getUserById } from '../user-service';
import { convertPrismaUserToConfig, type UserConfig } from '../../types';
import { providerConfigured } from './oidc';
import { emailConfigured } from './email-send';

export type IdentityKind = 'google' | 'email';
/** What Settings can remove: a Google way, the email way, or the calendar's Google account before its first use. */
export type RemovableWay = 'google' | 'email' | 'calendar-google';

/** Settings → Sign in on the web, as GET /api/signin-methods answers it (plus the session's method). */
export interface SignInMethodsView {
  /** On for a Telegram account; nothing to add or remove */
  telegram: boolean;
  google: { address: string } | null;
  /** No Google way yet, but the Google account the calendar is connected from would sign in (spec §2.17) */
  googleFromCalendar: boolean;
  email: { address: string } | null;
  /** Which ways this server has set up (their env vars), so Settings offers only those */
  providers: { telegram: boolean; google: boolean; email: boolean };
}

/** The P2002 Prisma answers when a unique constraint holds (read by its code, as the fakes throw it). */
const isUniqueViolation = (error: unknown) => (error as { code?: unknown } | null)?.code === 'P2002';

/**
 * The account a sign-in way belongs to, or null. A found way gets its last-used date (a failure there is logged and the
 * sign-in still goes ahead: the date is only shown in Settings).
 */
export async function findUserByIdentity(kind: IdentityKind, subject: string): Promise<UserConfig | null> {
  const identity = await prisma.signInIdentity.findUnique({
    where: { kind_subject: { kind, subject } },
    select: { id: true, userId: true },
  });
  if (!identity) return null;
  const user = await getUserById(identity.userId);
  if (!user) return null;
  try {
    await prisma.signInIdentity.update({ where: { id: identity.id }, data: { lastUsedAt: new Date() } });
  } catch (error) {
    console.error(`[signin] user ${user.id}: recording when the ${kind} way was last used failed`);
    captureError(error, 'signin-identity-touch', { user_id: user.id, kind }, 'warning');
  }
  return user;
}

/** The account that signs in with this (normalised) address: its user, the address as stored, the person's language. */
export async function findEmailSignIn(normalized: string): Promise<{ userId: number; address: string; language: string } | null> {
  const row = await prisma.signInIdentity.findUnique({
    where: { kind_subject: { kind: 'email', subject: normalized } },
    select: { userId: true, address: true, user: { select: { language: true } } },
  });
  return row ? { userId: row.userId, address: row.address, language: row.user.language } : null;
}

/** The account a right code signs in, while it still has that email way (it may have been removed since the code). */
export async function emailSignInAccount(userId: number, address: string): Promise<{ identityId: number; user: UserConfig } | null> {
  const row = await prisma.signInIdentity.findFirst({
    where: { kind: 'email', userId, address },
    select: { id: true, user: true },
  });
  return row ? { identityId: row.id, user: convertPrismaUserToConfig(row.user) } : null;
}

/** Marks the email way used now (Settings shows it). */
export async function touchEmailSignIn(identityId: number): Promise<void> {
  await prisma.signInIdentity.update({ where: { id: identityId }, data: { lastUsedAt: new Date() } });
}

/** Whether the account has a way of this kind. */
export async function hasIdentity(userId: number, kind: IdentityKind): Promise<boolean> {
  const row = await prisma.signInIdentity.findUnique({ where: { userId_kind: { userId, kind } }, select: { id: true } });
  return row !== null;
}

/** The account's ways, for Settings. One query (the ways); the rest is on the row already read. */
export async function listSignInMethods(user: UserConfig): Promise<SignInMethodsView> {
  const rows = await prisma.signInIdentity.findMany({ where: { userId: user.id }, select: { kind: true, address: true } });
  const google = rows.find(r => r.kind === 'google');
  const email = rows.find(r => r.kind === 'email');
  return {
    telegram: user.telegramId !== null,
    google: google ? { address: google.address } : null,
    googleFromCalendar: !google && user.googleCalendarSignIn && Boolean(user.googleRefreshToken) && Boolean(user.googleAccountKey),
    email: email ? { address: email.address } : null,
    providers: { telegram: providerConfigured('telegram'), google: providerConfigured('google'), email: emailConfigured() },
  };
}

/**
 * Add a way to an account. 'added': a row was made (the caller sends the notice). 'kept': this same account already
 * holds this subject, nothing changed (no notice: it went out when the way was made). 'taken': another account holds
 * this subject. 'has-one': this account already has a way of this kind with another subject.
 * usedNow: the way signs in at once (Add Google, the calendar match), so its last-used date is now.
 */
export async function addIdentity(
  userId: number,
  kind: IdentityKind,
  subject: string,
  address: string,
  opts: { usedNow?: boolean } = {},
): Promise<'added' | 'kept' | 'taken' | 'has-one'> {
  const holder = await prisma.signInIdentity.findUnique({ where: { kind_subject: { kind, subject } }, select: { userId: true } });
  if (holder) return holder.userId === userId ? 'kept' : 'taken';
  if (await hasIdentity(userId, kind)) return 'has-one';
  try {
    await prisma.signInIdentity.create({
      data: { userId, kind, subject, address, ...(opts.usedNow ? { lastUsedAt: new Date() } : {}) },
    });
  } catch (error) {
    if (!isUniqueViolation(error)) throw error;
    // Another request made one of the two in between: answer what is there now. Whoever made it sends its notice.
    console.warn(`[signin] user ${userId}: adding a ${kind} way met a unique constraint; answering what is stored now`);
    const now = await prisma.signInIdentity.findUnique({ where: { kind_subject: { kind, subject } }, select: { userId: true } });
    if (now) return now.userId === userId ? 'kept' : 'taken';
    return 'has-one';
  }
  console.log(`[signin] user ${userId}: a ${kind} sign-in way was added`);
  return 'added';
}

/**
 * Remove a way (spec §4, §2.13, §2.17). Any Google removal, the calendar's row included, turns googleCalendarSignIn off,
 * so the calendar match doesn't make it again (Add Google still works). Every removal ends every web session:
 * sessionsValidAfter is now (the route gives the device it came from a fresh cookie).
 */
export async function removeSignInMethod(userId: number, which: RemovableWay): Promise<void> {
  const now = new Date();
  await prisma.$transaction([
    ...(which === 'calendar-google' ? [] : [prisma.signInIdentity.deleteMany({ where: { userId, kind: which } })]),
    prisma.user.update({
      where: { id: userId },
      data: { sessionsValidAfter: now, ...(which === 'email' ? {} : { googleCalendarSignIn: false }) },
    }),
  ]);
  console.log(`[signin] user ${userId}: the ${which} way was removed; every web session ends`);
}
```

```ts
/**
 * The notice in the person's chat when a sign-in way is added (web sign-in spec §2.10), or when the Google account
 * their calendar is connected from is used for the first time (§2.17): so a stolen session can't add a way quietly.
 * It names the way with the address masked (maskEmail) and says where to remove it.
 *
 * It is the answer to the person's own action on the web, so the Shabbat pause doesn't hold it (CLAUDE.md;
 * scripts/smoke-pause.ts lists this file as NOT_PAUSED). The chat: Telegram when the account has it, else WhatsApp
 * (the phone, else the BSUID). On WhatsApp a free-form text outside the person's 24-hour window is accepted by Meta and
 * rejected later (131047), which the webhook's status handler logs; a refusal here is logged and captured. It never
 * throws: the way is made either way. No log line holds the address.
 */

import enMessages from '../../../messages/en.json';
import heMessages from '../../../messages/he.json';
import ruMessages from '../../../messages/ru.json';
import { captureError } from '../../lib/error-capture';
import { normalizeLocale, type Locale } from '../../utils/locale';
import { getWhatsAppChatId } from '../user-service';
import { getWhatsAppService } from '../messaging';
import type { UserConfig } from '../../types';
import { maskEmail } from './email-address';
import type { IdentityKind } from './identities';

export interface SignInNoticeEvent {
  kind: IdentityKind;
  /** The way's address, as stored; the notice shows it masked */
  address: string;
  /** added: from Settings; calendar: the first sign-in with the calendar's Google account */
  via: 'added' | 'calendar';
}

type NoticeCopy = typeof enMessages.signinNotice;
const WORDS: Record<Locale, NoticeCopy> = {
  en: enMessages.signinNotice,
  he: heMessages.signinNotice,
  ru: ruMessages.signinNotice,
};

export async function sendSignInNotice(user: UserConfig, event: SignInNoticeEvent): Promise<void> {
  const what = `${event.kind} (${event.via})`;
  try {
    const copy = WORDS[normalizeLocale(user.language)];
    const template = event.via === 'calendar' ? copy.calendarGoogle : event.kind === 'google' ? copy.addedGoogle : copy.addedEmail;
    const text = template.replace('{address}', maskEmail(event.address));

    if (user.telegramId) {
      // Loaded here, as google-connect.ts does: the bot module pulls in the whole Telegram client
      const { getMessagingService } = await import('../telegram/bot');
      await getMessagingService().sendMessage(user.telegramId, text);
      console.log(`[signin-notice] user ${user.id}: the ${what} notice was sent on Telegram`);
      return;
    }
    const chatId = getWhatsAppChatId(user);
    if (!chatId) {
      console.warn(`[signin-notice] user ${user.id}: no chat to send the ${what} notice to`);
      return;
    }
    await getWhatsAppService().sendMessage(chatId, text);
    console.log(`[signin-notice] user ${user.id}: the ${what} notice was sent on WhatsApp`);
  } catch (error) {
    console.error(`[signin-notice] user ${user.id}: the ${what} notice was not sent: ${error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error)}`);
    captureError(error, 'signin-notice', { user_id: user.id, kind: event.kind, via: event.via }, 'warning');
  }
}
```

- [ ] **Step 8: Write `src/services/web-signin/add-google.ts`**

```ts
/**
 * Settings' Add Google (web sign-in spec §2.9). Google refuses to sign in inside in-app browsers, so Add Google opens a
 * one-time famcal.bot link (5 minutes) in the person's browser: /{lang}/signin/add-google?token=<token> (English
 * unprefixed). That page names the account (peekAddGoogleToken, which never uses the link up) and offers Continue; only
 * Continue (POST /api/auth/google/add-start, Origin-checked) uses the link up (takeAddGoogleToken, GETDEL) and starts
 * Google with an 'add-google' flow bound to that browser. Google's callback then attaches the account
 * (finishAddGoogle), sends the notice and signs that browser in as the account that made the link.
 *
 * Redis keeps the token only as its sha256 (REDIS_KEYS.signinAddGoogle), and no log line holds it. The parameter is
 * `token` so the log and Sentry scrubber (part B) drops it from every URL it sees.
 */

import crypto from 'crypto';
import { NextResponse } from 'next/server';
import { redis } from '../../utils/redis';
import { REDIS_KEYS } from '../../config/redis-keys';
import { buildUrl } from '../../config/urls';
import { normalizeLocale } from '../../utils/locale';
import { localeHref } from '../../site/zmanim/links';
import { finishSignIn, signInPageUrl, signInRefusal } from '../../lib/web-session';
import { getUserById } from '../user-service';
import type { UserConfig } from '../../types';
import type { OidcFlow } from './flow';
import type { GoogleClaims } from './oidc';
import { addIdentity } from './identities';
import { sendSignInNotice } from './notice';

const ADD_GOOGLE_TTL_SECONDS = 5 * 60;
/** 24 random bytes as base64url */
const TOKEN = /^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{32}$/;

const keyOf = (token: string) => REDIS_KEYS.signinAddGoogle(crypto.createHash('sha256').update(token).digest('hex'));

/** Make the one-time link for a proved account: famcal.bot/{lang}/signin/add-google?token=<token>, 5 minutes. */
export async function createAddGoogleLink(user: UserConfig): Promise<string> {
  const token = crypto.randomBytes(24).toString('base64url');
  await redis.set(keyOf(token), JSON.stringify({ userId: user.id }), { ex: ADD_GOOGLE_TTL_SECONDS });
  return buildUrl(localeHref(normalizeLocale(user.language), `/signin/add-google?token=${token}`));
}

function readEntry(raw: unknown): { userId: number } | null {
  if (!raw) return null;
  const entry = (typeof raw === 'string' ? JSON.parse(raw) : raw) as { userId?: unknown };
  return typeof entry.userId === 'number' ? { userId: entry.userId } : null;
}

/** The account a link was made for, without using it up (the page that names it); null for a used, late or bad link. */
export async function peekAddGoogleToken(token: unknown): Promise<{ userId: number } | null> {
  if (typeof token !== 'string' || !TOKEN.test(token)) return null;
  return readEntry(await redis.get(keyOf(token)));
}

/** Use a link up (Continue): GETDEL, so it works once. */
export async function takeAddGoogleToken(token: unknown): Promise<{ userId: number } | null> {
  if (typeof token !== 'string' || !TOKEN.test(token)) return null;
  return readEntry(await redis.getdel(keyOf(token)));
}

/**
 * Google's callback for an 'add-google' flow (Task 4's handleOidcCallback has proved the token and cleared the flow
 * cookie): attach the Google account (sub, the verified address) to the account that made the link, send the notice,
 * and sign this browser in as that account. A sub another account holds is refused (status=taken), and so is a second
 * Google account (status=has-one). A suspended or banned account gets no way and no notice: signInRefusal answers
 * before anything is added, and finishSignIn shows the person its page. The same account adding the same Google account
 * again ('kept') is signed in without a second notice. The caller has checked the address is verified.
 */
export async function finishAddGoogle(flow: OidcFlow, claims: GoogleClaims): Promise<NextResponse> {
  const user = flow.userId ? await getUserById(flow.userId) : null;
  if (!user || !claims.email) {
    console.warn(`[signin] add-google: ${user ? `user ${user.id}: Google gave no address` : `the account that made the link is not there (${flow.userId ?? 'none'})`}`);
    return NextResponse.redirect(signInPageUrl(flow.locale, 'failed'));
  }
  const refusal = await signInRefusal(user);
  if (refusal) {
    console.warn(`[signin] user ${user.id}: add-google refused: the account is ${refusal}`);
    return finishSignIn(user, 'google');
  }
  const added = await addIdentity(user.id, 'google', claims.sub, claims.email, { usedNow: true });
  if (added === 'taken' || added === 'has-one') {
    console.warn(`[signin] user ${user.id}: add-google refused (${added})`);
    return NextResponse.redirect(signInPageUrl(flow.locale, added));
  }
  if (added === 'added') await sendSignInNotice(user, { kind: 'google', address: claims.email, via: 'added' });
  return finishSignIn(user, 'google');
}
```

```ts
/**
 * Who a Google sign-in is (web sign-in spec §3, §2.17): the account that added this Google account (google, sub).
 * The one call site for the Google callback's account lookup.
 */

import type { UserConfig } from '../../types';
import type { GoogleClaims } from './oidc';
import { findUserByIdentity } from './identities';

export type GoogleSignInResult = { user: UserConfig } | { status: 'no-account' | 'several' };

export async function resolveGoogleSignIn(claims: GoogleClaims): Promise<GoogleSignInResult> {
  const user = await findUserByIdentity('google', claims.sub);
  if (user) return { user };
  // No way added for this sub. Task 7 adds the Google account a calendar is connected from (spec §2.17) here.
  return { status: 'no-account' };
}
```
