`app/api/signin-methods/route.ts`:
```ts
// Settings → Sign in on the web (web sign-in spec §4): the ways this account signs in on the web.
//
// GET /api/signin-methods?user_id=…  → SignInMethodsView & { session }: Telegram (on for a Telegram account), the
//   Google and email ways with the addresses to show, whether the calendar's Google account would sign in (§2.17),
//   which ways this server has set up, and how this browser signed in (null inside Telegram).
//
// Security: verifyUserAuth proves the caller (Telegram initData, or the session cookie) with the general limiter; the
// answer is the proved user's own, never the id in the URL. A same-origin GET carries no Origin in most browsers, so
// the Origin guard is on the POSTs only; this route changes nothing.

import { NextRequest, NextResponse } from 'next/server';
import { verifyUserAuth } from '@/src/lib/api-auth';
import { requestInitData } from '@/src/lib/request-init-data';
import { generalRateLimiter } from '@/src/lib/rate-limit';
import { captureError } from '@/src/lib/error-capture';
import { listSignInMethods } from '@/src/services/web-signin/identities';

export const dynamic = 'force-dynamic';

export async function GET(request: NextRequest) {
  let userId: number | undefined;
  try {
    const auth = await verifyUserAuth(request, request.nextUrl.searchParams.get('user_id'), requestInitData(request), generalRateLimiter, 'signin-methods');
    if (!auth.success) return auth.response;
    userId = auth.user.id;
    const methods = await listSignInMethods(auth.user);
    return NextResponse.json({ ...methods, session: auth.via === 'session' ? auth.session.method : null });
  } catch (error) {
    captureError(error, 'signin-methods', { user_id: userId });
    return NextResponse.json({ error: 'failed' }, { status: 500 });
  }
}
```

`app/api/signin-methods/email/add/route.ts`:
```ts
// Settings → Sign in on the web → Add email (web sign-in spec §4, §5): mail a code to the address.
//
// POST /api/signin-methods/email/add?user_id=…  body { email }
//   → { ok: true }: the code is on its way (10 minutes), and the account waits for it (REDIS_KEYS.signinAddEmail).
//   → { ok: false, error }: invalid (400: not an ASCII address), has-one (409: the account has an email way),
//     unavailable (409: no email sender set up), limit (429: Add email codes per account, per address, per IP), failed (500).
// An address another account signs in with is mailed like any other and refused only once its code is right
// (email/confirm), so this answer never tells whose an address is.
//
// Security: Origin and JSON first (refuseCrossSite), then verifyUserAuth with the settings limiter; the route acts on
// the proved user only. No log line holds the address or the code.

import { NextRequest, NextResponse } from 'next/server';
import { verifyUserAuth } from '@/src/lib/api-auth';
import { requestInitData } from '@/src/lib/request-init-data';
import { settingsRateLimiter } from '@/src/lib/rate-limit';
import { captureError } from '@/src/lib/error-capture';
import { refuseCrossSite } from '@/src/lib/same-origin';
import { REDIS_KEYS } from '@/src/config/redis-keys';
import { redis } from '@/src/utils/redis';
import { normalizeLocale } from '@/src/utils/locale';
import { clientAddress } from '@/src/services/web-signin/client-address';
import { emailKey, normalizeEmail } from '@/src/services/web-signin/email-address';
import { allowCodeRequest } from '@/src/services/web-signin/limits';
import { emailConfigured } from '@/src/services/web-signin/email-send';
import { issueCode } from '@/src/services/web-signin/email-code';
import { hasIdentity } from '@/src/services/web-signin/identities';

export const dynamic = 'force-dynamic';

/** How long an Add email waits for its code: the code's own life */
const PENDING_TTL_SECONDS = 10 * 60;

const answer = (body: Record<string, unknown>, status = 200) => NextResponse.json(body, { status });

export async function POST(request: NextRequest) {
  const refused = refuseCrossSite(request);
  if (refused) return refused;
  let userId: number | undefined;
  try {
    // A body that is not JSON is read as no body; the fact is logged, never the parse message
    const body = await request.json().catch(() => {
      console.warn('[signin-methods] the body is not JSON');
      return null;
    });
    const auth = await verifyUserAuth(request, request.nextUrl.searchParams.get('user_id'), requestInitData(request, body), settingsRateLimiter, 'signin-methods-email-add');
    if (!auth.success) return auth.response;
    const user = auth.user;
    userId = user.id;

    if (!emailConfigured()) {
      console.warn(`[signin-methods] user ${user.id}: Add email asked with no email sender set up`);
      return answer({ ok: false, error: 'unavailable' }, 409);
    }
    const address = normalizeEmail(body?.email);
    if (!address) {
      console.warn(`[signin-methods] user ${user.id}: Add email refused an address that is not one`);
      return answer({ ok: false, error: 'invalid' }, 400);
    }
    if (await hasIdentity(user.id, 'email')) {
      console.warn(`[signin-methods] user ${user.id}: Add email refused: the account has an email way`);
      return answer({ ok: false, error: 'has-one' }, 409);
    }
    const key = emailKey(address);
    const allowed = await allowCodeRequest({ emailKey: key, ip: clientAddress(request), addForUserId: user.id });
    if (!allowed.ok) {
      console.warn(`[signin-methods] user ${user.id}: Add email code refused (${allowed.reason})`);
      return answer({ ok: false, error: 'limit' }, 429);
    }
    await redis.set(REDIS_KEYS.signinAddEmail(user.id), JSON.stringify({ emailKey: key }), { ex: PENDING_TTL_SECONDS });
    await issueCode({ purpose: 'add', emailKey: key, address, userId: user.id, locale: normalizeLocale(user.language) });
    console.log(`[signin-methods] user ${user.id}: an Add email code was issued`);
    return answer({ ok: true });
  } catch (error) {
    captureError(error, 'signin-methods-email-add', { user_id: userId });
    return answer({ ok: false, error: 'failed' }, 500);
  }
}
```

`app/api/signin-methods/email/confirm/route.ts`:
```ts
// Settings → Sign in on the web → Add email, the code (web sign-in spec §4, §5).
//
// POST /api/signin-methods/email/confirm?user_id=…  body { code }
//   → { ok: true, methods }: the email way is made, the chat gets the notice (§2.10).
//   → { ok: false, error }: wrong (400), limit (429: too many wrong codes for this address or from this IP),
//     restart (410: no Add email waiting, the code expired or was used), taken (409: another account signs in with this
//     address), has-one (409: the account got an email way meanwhile), failed (500).
// Tries are counted before the compare (checkCode), and every wrong one counts toward the address's and the IP's limits.
//
// Security: Origin and JSON first, then verifyUserAuth with the settings limiter. The code must have been issued for
// this same account. No log line holds the address or the code.

import { NextRequest, NextResponse } from 'next/server';
import { verifyUserAuth } from '@/src/lib/api-auth';
import { requestInitData } from '@/src/lib/request-init-data';
import { settingsRateLimiter } from '@/src/lib/rate-limit';
import { captureError } from '@/src/lib/error-capture';
import { refuseCrossSite } from '@/src/lib/same-origin';
import { REDIS_KEYS } from '@/src/config/redis-keys';
import { redis } from '@/src/utils/redis';
import { clientAddress } from '@/src/services/web-signin/client-address';
import { codeChecksBlocked, recordWrongCode } from '@/src/services/web-signin/limits';
import { checkCode } from '@/src/services/web-signin/email-code';
import { addIdentity, listSignInMethods } from '@/src/services/web-signin/identities';
import { sendSignInNotice } from '@/src/services/web-signin/notice';

export const dynamic = 'force-dynamic';

const answer = (body: Record<string, unknown>, status = 200) => NextResponse.json(body, { status });

/** The Add email waiting for this account's code: the hashed address, or null. */
async function pendingEmailKey(userId: number): Promise<string | null> {
  const raw = await redis.get<{ emailKey?: unknown } | string>(REDIS_KEYS.signinAddEmail(userId));
  if (!raw) return null;
  const entry = (typeof raw === 'string' ? JSON.parse(raw) : raw) as { emailKey?: unknown };
  return typeof entry.emailKey === 'string' ? entry.emailKey : null;
}

export async function POST(request: NextRequest) {
  const refused = refuseCrossSite(request);
  if (refused) return refused;
  let userId: number | undefined;
  try {
    // A body that is not JSON is read as no body; the fact is logged, never the parse message
    const body = await request.json().catch(() => {
      console.warn('[signin-methods] the body is not JSON');
      return null;
    });
    const auth = await verifyUserAuth(request, request.nextUrl.searchParams.get('user_id'), requestInitData(request, body), settingsRateLimiter, 'signin-methods-email-confirm');
    if (!auth.success) return auth.response;
    const user = auth.user;
    userId = user.id;

    const key = await pendingEmailKey(user.id);
    if (!key) {
      console.warn(`[signin-methods] user ${user.id}: an Add email code with no Add email waiting`);
      return answer({ ok: false, error: 'restart' }, 410);
    }
    const ip = clientAddress(request);
    if (await codeChecksBlocked({ emailKey: key, ip })) {
      console.warn(`[signin-methods] user ${user.id}: Add email codes paused (too many wrong ones)`);
      return answer({ ok: false, error: 'limit' }, 429);
    }
    const code = typeof body?.code === 'string' ? body.code.trim() : '';
    const result = await checkCode('add', key, code);
    if (!result.ok) {
      if (result.reason === 'expired') {
        await redis.del(REDIS_KEYS.signinAddEmail(user.id));
        console.warn(`[signin-methods] user ${user.id}: the Add email code expired or was used up`);
        return answer({ ok: false, error: 'restart' }, 410);
      }
      await recordWrongCode({ emailKey: key, ip });
      console.warn(`[signin-methods] user ${user.id}: a wrong Add email code`);
      return answer({ ok: false, error: 'wrong' }, 400);
    }
    await redis.del(REDIS_KEYS.signinAddEmail(user.id));
    if (result.userId !== user.id) {
      // The address's add code was issued to another account meanwhile (a code is per address)
      console.warn(`[signin-methods] user ${user.id}: the Add email code was issued to another account`);
      return answer({ ok: false, error: 'restart' }, 410);
    }
    const added = await addIdentity(user.id, 'email', result.address, result.address);
    if (added === 'taken' || added === 'has-one') {
      console.warn(`[signin-methods] user ${user.id}: Add email refused after the right code (${added})`);
      return answer({ ok: false, error: added }, 409);
    }
    // 'kept': this account already holds the address (a second tap on the same code), whose notice went out when the way was made
    if (added === 'added') await sendSignInNotice(user, { kind: 'email', address: result.address, via: 'added' });
    return answer({ ok: true, methods: await listSignInMethods(user) });
  } catch (error) {
    captureError(error, 'signin-methods-email-confirm', { user_id: userId });
    return answer({ ok: false, error: 'failed' }, 500);
  }
}
```

`app/api/signin-methods/remove/route.ts`:
```ts
// Settings → Sign in on the web → Remove (web sign-in spec §4, §2.13, §2.17).
//
// POST /api/signin-methods/remove?user_id=…  body { which: 'google' | 'email' | 'calendar-google' }
//   → { ok: true, methods }. Every web session of the account ends (sessionsValidAfter); the device this came from, when
//     it is a web session, gets a fresh cookie with the same method and a sign-in time of now, so it stays signed in.
//     A WhatsApp link's cookie keeps its own expiry (spec §2.4: never renewed); a web session gets a full new life.
//     Any Google removal turns the calendar's Google account off (googleCalendarSignIn).
//   → 400 invalid for anything else (Telegram and WhatsApp can't be removed here), 500 failed.
//
// Security: Origin and JSON first, then verifyUserAuth with the settings limiter; acts on the proved user only.

import { NextRequest, NextResponse } from 'next/server';
import { verifyUserAuth } from '@/src/lib/api-auth';
import { requestInitData } from '@/src/lib/request-init-data';
import { settingsRateLimiter } from '@/src/lib/rate-limit';
import { captureError } from '@/src/lib/error-capture';
import { refuseCrossSite } from '@/src/lib/same-origin';
import { createSessionToken, setSessionCookie } from '@/src/lib/session-auth';
import { getUserById } from '@/src/services/user-service';
import { listSignInMethods, removeSignInMethod, type RemovableWay } from '@/src/services/web-signin/identities';

export const dynamic = 'force-dynamic';

const WAYS: readonly RemovableWay[] = ['google', 'email', 'calendar-google'];
const isWay = (value: unknown): value is RemovableWay => typeof value === 'string' && (WAYS as readonly string[]).includes(value);

export async function POST(request: NextRequest) {
  const refused = refuseCrossSite(request);
  if (refused) return refused;
  let userId: number | undefined;
  try {
    // A body that is not JSON is read as no body; the fact is logged, never the parse message
    const body = await request.json().catch(() => {
      console.warn('[signin-methods] the body is not JSON');
      return null;
    });
    const auth = await verifyUserAuth(request, request.nextUrl.searchParams.get('user_id'), requestInitData(request, body), settingsRateLimiter, 'signin-methods-remove');
    if (!auth.success) return auth.response;
    userId = auth.user.id;
    const which: unknown = body?.which;
    if (!isWay(which)) {
      console.warn(`[signin-methods] user ${userId}: refused a removal of an unknown way`);
      return NextResponse.json({ ok: false, error: 'invalid' }, { status: 400 });
    }
    await removeSignInMethod(userId, which);
    const fresh = (await getUserById(userId)) ?? auth.user;
    const response = NextResponse.json({ ok: true, methods: await listSignInMethods(fresh) });
    if (auth.via === 'session') {
      // Signed in now, so after the new sessionsValidAfter: this device stays signed in, every other one is out. A
      // WhatsApp link is never renewed: its cookie keeps the link's own expiry and only the seconds left.
      const keep = auth.session.method === 'wa' ? auth.session.exp : null;
      const token = createSessionToken(userId, auth.session.method, Date.now(), keep === null ? undefined : { exp: keep });
      setSessionCookie(response, token, keep === null ? undefined : { maxAgeSec: Math.max(1, keep - Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000)) });
    }
    return response;
  } catch (error) {
    captureError(error, 'signin-methods-remove', { user_id: userId });
    return NextResponse.json({ ok: false, error: 'failed' }, { status: 500 });
  }
}
```

`app/api/auth/google/add-link/route.ts`:
```ts
// Settings → Sign in on the web → Add Google (web sign-in spec §2.9): the one-time link that opens in the browser.
//
// POST /api/auth/google/add-link?user_id=…  body {}
//   → { url }: famcal.bot/{lang}/signin/add-google?token=<token> (English unprefixed), 5 minutes, used up only by Continue on that page.
//   → 409 { error: 'unavailable' } with no Google sign-in client set up; 409 { error: 'has-one' } when the account has a
//     Google way already (remove it first); 500 { error: 'failed' }.
//
// Security: Origin and JSON first, then verifyUserAuth with the settings limiter; the link is for the proved user. No
// log line holds the token.

import { NextRequest, NextResponse } from 'next/server';
import { verifyUserAuth } from '@/src/lib/api-auth';
import { requestInitData } from '@/src/lib/request-init-data';
import { settingsRateLimiter } from '@/src/lib/rate-limit';
import { captureError } from '@/src/lib/error-capture';
import { refuseCrossSite } from '@/src/lib/same-origin';
import { providerConfigured } from '@/src/services/web-signin/oidc';
import { hasIdentity } from '@/src/services/web-signin/identities';
import { createAddGoogleLink } from '@/src/services/web-signin/add-google';

export const dynamic = 'force-dynamic';

export async function POST(request: NextRequest) {
  const refused = refuseCrossSite(request);
  if (refused) return refused;
  let userId: number | undefined;
  try {
    // A body that is not JSON is read as no body; the fact is logged, never the parse message
    const body = await request.json().catch(() => {
      console.warn('[signin-methods] the body is not JSON');
      return null;
    });
    const auth = await verifyUserAuth(request, request.nextUrl.searchParams.get('user_id'), requestInitData(request, body), settingsRateLimiter, 'signin-add-google-link');
    if (!auth.success) return auth.response;
    userId = auth.user.id;
    if (!providerConfigured('google')) {
      console.warn(`[signin] user ${userId}: Add Google asked with no Google sign-in client set up`);
      return NextResponse.json({ error: 'unavailable' }, { status: 409 });
    }
    if (await hasIdentity(userId, 'google')) {
      console.warn(`[signin] user ${userId}: Add Google refused: the account has a Google way`);
      return NextResponse.json({ error: 'has-one' }, { status: 409 });
    }
    const url = await createAddGoogleLink(auth.user);
    console.log(`[signin] user ${userId}: an Add Google link was made`);
    return NextResponse.json({ url });
  } catch (error) {
    captureError(error, 'signin-add-google-link', { user_id: userId });
    return NextResponse.json({ error: 'failed' }, { status: 500 });
  }
}
```

`app/api/auth/google/add-start/route.ts`:
```ts
// Continue on /signin/add-google (web sign-in spec §2.9): use the one-time link up and start Google.
//
// POST /api/auth/google/add-start  body { token }
//   → { url }: Google's sign-in URL, with an 'add-google' flow (state, nonce, PKCE) bound to this browser by the
//     famcal_signin cookie (Path=/api/auth, 10 minutes). Google's answer comes back to /api/auth/google/callback.
//   → 410 { error: 'expired' } for a used, late or bad link; 403 { error: 'suspended' }; 409 { error: 'unavailable' }
//     with no Google sign-in client; 500 { error: 'failed' }.
//
// Security: Origin and JSON first, so only the famcal.bot page can use a link up; looking at the page never does
// (peekAddGoogleToken). No log line holds the token or the state.

import { NextRequest, NextResponse } from 'next/server';
import { captureError } from '@/src/lib/error-capture';
import { refuseCrossSite } from '@/src/lib/same-origin';
import { normalizeLocale } from '@/src/utils/locale';
import { getUserById } from '@/src/services/user-service';
import { startFlow, type OidcFlow } from '@/src/services/web-signin/flow';
import { authorizationUrl, newOidcChecks, providerConfigured } from '@/src/services/web-signin/oidc';
import { takeAddGoogleToken } from '@/src/services/web-signin/add-google';

export const dynamic = 'force-dynamic';

export async function POST(request: NextRequest) {
  const refused = refuseCrossSite(request);
  if (refused) return refused;
  let userId: number | undefined;
  try {
    // A body that is not JSON is read as no body; the fact is logged, never the parse message
    const body = await request.json().catch(() => {
      console.warn('[signin] add-google: the body is not JSON');
      return null;
    });
    const link = await takeAddGoogleToken(body?.token);
    if (!link) {
      console.warn('[signin] add-google: Continue with a link that is used, late or not one');
      return NextResponse.json({ error: 'expired' }, { status: 410 });
    }
    userId = link.userId;
    const user = await getUserById(link.userId);
    if (!user) {
      console.warn(`[signin] add-google: the account ${link.userId} that made the link is not there`);
      return NextResponse.json({ error: 'expired' }, { status: 410 });
    }
    if (user.suspendedAt) {
      console.warn(`[signin] user ${user.id}: add-google refused: the account is suspended`);
      return NextResponse.json({ error: 'suspended' }, { status: 403 });
    }
    if (!providerConfigured('google')) {
      console.warn(`[signin] user ${user.id}: add-google with no Google sign-in client set up`);
      return NextResponse.json({ error: 'unavailable' }, { status: 409 });
    }
    const flow: OidcFlow = { kind: 'add-google', ...newOidcChecks(), locale: normalizeLocale(user.language), userId: user.id };
    const url = await authorizationUrl('google', flow);
    const response = NextResponse.json({ url: url.toString() });
    await startFlow(response, flow);
    console.log(`[signin] user ${user.id}: add-google went to Google`);
    return response;
  } catch (error) {
    captureError(error, 'signin-add-google-start', { user_id: userId });
    return NextResponse.json({ error: 'failed' }, { status: 500 });
  }
}
```

```ts
export async function GET(request: NextRequest) {
  return handleOidcCallback('google', request, ['google', 'add-google'], async (claims, flow) => {
    if (!claims.emailVerified || !claims.email) {
      console.warn(`[signin] google: the account's address is not verified (${flow.kind} flow)`);
      return NextResponse.redirect(signInPageUrl(flow.locale, 'failed'));
    }
    if (flow.kind === 'add-google') return finishAddGoogle(flow, claims);
    const found = await resolveGoogleSignIn(claims);
    if ('status' in found) return NextResponse.redirect(signInPageUrl(flow.locale, found.status));
    return finishSignIn(found.user, 'google');
  });
}
```

(`handleOidcCallback` clears the `famcal_signin` cookie on every answer, so the Add Google branch does not; the provider's `?error=` is answered there for both providers, with a check in `smoke-signin-oidc`, part C.)

    DB.user = [
      baseUser({ id: TAL, name: 'Tal', telegramId: BigInt(TAL_TG), googleRefreshToken: 'rt-tal', googleAccountKey: KEY_TAL }),
      baseUser({ id: NOA, name: 'Noa', telegramId: BigInt(222222222) }),
    ];
    DB.signInIdentity = [];
    world.accounts = { 'rt-tal': 'Tal@Gmail.com' };
  }
  const userRow = (id: number): Row => DB.user.find(u => u.id === id) as Row;
  const identitiesOf = (id: number): Row[] => (DB.signInIdentity ?? []).filter(i => i.userId === id);
  const claims = (o: Row = {}): Row => ({ sub: 'g-new', email: 'tal@gmail.com', emailVerified: true, ...o });
  const location = (res: Row): string => res.headers.get('location') ?? '';
  /** Where a redirect goes, path and query (English has no language prefix: i18n/routing.ts 'as-needed'). */
  const pathOf = (res: Row): string => {
    const url = new URL(location(res), 'https://famcal.bot');
    return `${url.pathname}${url.search}`;
  };
  let flows = 0;
  /** "Continue with Google" through the callback, with these claims: the response. */
  const signInWithGoogle = async (c: Row) => {
    const state = `st-${++flows}`;
    const cookie = await flowCookie({ kind: 'google', state, nonce: `n-${flows}`, codeVerifier: 'v'.repeat(43), locale: 'en' });
    world.claims = c;
    return callbackRoute.GET(request(`/api/auth/google/callback?code=c-${flows}&state=${state}`, { cookie }));
  };

  // ---- The key ----

  await check('#1 the key: the same for any case and spacing of the address, <key id>:<64 hex>, no address in it; another SESSION_SECRET gives another id and value; none without SESSION_SECRET', () => {
    const k = account.googleAccountKey('Tal@Gmail.com');
    assert(k === account.googleAccountKey('  tal@gmail.com ') && /^[0-9a-f]{8}:[0-9a-f]{64}$/.test(k) && k.startsWith(`${KEY_ID}:`), `key ${k}`);
    assert(account.googleAccountKey('other@gmail.com') !== k, 'two addresses, one key');
    assert(!k.includes('tal'), 'the key holds the address');
    const secret = process.env.SESSION_SECRET;
    try {
      process.env.SESSION_SECRET = 'another-secret';
      const other = account.googleAccountKey('tal@gmail.com');
      assert(other !== k && !other.startsWith(`${KEY_ID}:`) && account.googleAccountKeyId() !== KEY_ID, `another secret ${other}`);
      process.env.SESSION_SECRET = '';
      assert(account.googleAccountKey('tal@gmail.com') === null && account.googleAccountKeyId() === null, 'a key without SESSION_SECRET');
    } finally {
      process.env.SESSION_SECRET = secret;
    }
  });

  // ---- The match ----

  await check('#2 one account on that Google account, live check agreeing: "Continue with Google" signs it in, makes the Google way (used now) and sends the calendar notice, masked; Google asked once with its calendar token', async () => {
    seed();
    const res = await signInWithGoogle(claims());
    assert(pathOf(res) === '/dashboard?user_id=9', `location ${location(res)}; captured ${show(captured)}`);
    const session = validateSessionToken(res.cookies.get(SESSION_COOKIE_NAME)?.value ?? '');
    assert(session?.userId === TAL && session.method === 'google', `session ${show(session)}`);
    const [way] = identitiesOf(TAL);
    assert(way?.kind === 'google' && way.subject === 'g-new' && way.address === 'tal@gmail.com' && way.lastUsedAt instanceof Date, `way ${show(way)}`);
    assert(sent.length === 1 && sent[0].chatId === String(TAL_TG) && sent[0].text.includes('t•••@gmail.com') && sent[0].text.includes('the account your calendar is connected from'), `sent ${show(sent)}`);
    assert(show(world.googleAsks) === show(['rt-tal']), `asks ${show(world.googleAsks)}`);
  });

  await check('#3 the next sign-in finds the way it made: no Google call, no second notice', async () => {
    seed();
    await signin.resolveGoogleSignIn(claims());
    world.googleAsks.length = 0;
    sent.length = 0;
    const res = await signInWithGoogle(claims());
    assert(pathOf(res) === '/dashboard?user_id=9' && world.googleAsks.length === 0 && sent.length === 0, `location ${location(res)} asks ${show(world.googleAsks)} sent ${show(sent)}`);
  });

  await check('#4 a live check that disagrees (the calendar now on another account) is no-account: no way, no notice, and the callback lands on the no-account page', async () => {
    seed();
    world.accounts['rt-tal'] = 'other@gmail.com';
    const r = await signin.resolveGoogleSignIn(claims());
    assert(show(r) === show({ status: 'no-account' }), `result ${show(r)}`);
    assert(identitiesOf(TAL).length === 0 && sent.length === 0 && show(world.googleAsks) === show(['rt-tal']), `ways ${show(identitiesOf(TAL))} sent ${show(sent)}`);
    assert(location(await signInWithGoogle(claims())).includes('status=no-account'), 'callback');
  });

  await check('#5 a dead connection (Google refuses the token) is no-account, logged and captured with the user id', async () => {
    seed();
    world.accounts['rt-tal'] = Object.assign(new Error('invalid_grant'), { response: { status: 400, data: { error: 'invalid_grant' } } });
    const r = await signin.resolveGoogleSignIn(claims());
    assert(show(r) === show({ status: 'no-account' }) && identitiesOf(TAL).length === 0, `result ${show(r)}`);
    assert(captured.some(c => c.context === 'google-account-check' && c.extra.user_id === TAL), `captured ${show(captured)}`);
    assert(logs.some(l => l.includes('[google-account] user 9')), `logs ${show(logs)}`);
  });

  await check('#6 two FamCal accounts on one Google account (a shared family account) is several, with no Google call; an account whose calendar is disconnected does not count', async () => {
    seed();
    DB.user.push(baseUser({ id: 10, name: 'Family', telegramId: BigInt(333333333), googleRefreshToken: 'rt-family', googleAccountKey: KEY_TAL }));
    const r = await signin.resolveGoogleSignIn(claims());
    assert(show(r) === show({ status: 'several' }) && world.googleAsks.length === 0 && (DB.signInIdentity ?? []).length === 0, `result ${show(r)} asks ${show(world.googleAsks)}`);
    assert(location(await signInWithGoogle(claims())).includes('status=several'), 'callback');
    seed();
    DB.user.push(baseUser({ id: 10, name: 'Family', telegramId: BigInt(333333333), googleRefreshToken: '', googleAccountKey: KEY_TAL }));
    const one = await signin.resolveGoogleSignIn(claims());
    assert(one.user?.id === TAL, `result ${show(one)}`);
  });

  await check('#7 the switch off (googleCalendarSignIn) is no-account, with no Google call (the query asks only for accounts with it on)', async () => {
    seed();
    userRow(TAL).googleCalendarSignIn = false;
    const r = await signin.resolveGoogleSignIn(claims());
    assert(show(r) === show({ status: 'no-account' }) && world.googleAsks.length === 0, `result ${show(r)} asks ${show(world.googleAsks)}`);
  });

  await check('#8 an account that already has a Google way (another Google account) is no-account, with no Google call', async () => {
    seed();
    DB.signInIdentity.push(identityRow({ userId: TAL, kind: 'google', subject: 'g-old', address: 'old@gmail.com' }));
    const r = await signin.resolveGoogleSignIn(claims());
    assert(show(r) === show({ status: 'no-account' }) && world.googleAsks.length === 0 && identitiesOf(TAL).length === 1, `result ${show(r)}`);
  });

  await check('#9 no verified address (unverified, or none) is no-account before any account lookup', async () => {
    seed();
    for (const c of [claims({ emailVerified: false }), claims({ email: null })]) {
      prismaCalls.length = 0;
      const r = await account.matchCalendarAccount(c);
      assert(show(r) === show({ status: 'no-account' }) && !prismaCalls.includes('user.findMany'), `${show(c)}: ${show(r)} calls ${show(prismaCalls)}`);
    }
  });

  await check('#10 a row with no key yet, or a key made under another SESSION_SECRET, does not match', async () => {
    for (const key of [null, `${OLD_ID}:${'0'.repeat(64)}`]) {
      seed();
      userRow(TAL).googleAccountKey = key;
      const r = await signin.resolveGoogleSignIn(claims());
      assert(show(r) === show({ status: 'no-account' }) && world.googleAsks.length === 0, `key ${key}: ${show(r)}`);
    }
  });

  await check('#11 a suspended account is answered (finishSignIn shows its page), and nothing is attached or sent', async () => {
    seed();
    userRow(TAL).suspendedAt = new Date();
    const r = await signin.resolveGoogleSignIn(claims());
    assert(r.user?.id === TAL && identitiesOf(TAL).length === 0 && sent.length === 0, `result ${show(r)}`);
    assert(location(await signInWithGoogle(claims())).includes('status=suspended'), 'callback');
  });

  await check('#12 Settings shows the calendar row before its first use; removing the way it made, or the row itself, turns the switch off and the match stops', async () => {
    seed();
    const list = async () => body(await methodsRoute.GET(request(`/api/signin-methods?user_id=${TAL_TG}`, { initData: initDataFor(TAL_TG) })));
    assert((await list()).googleFromCalendar === true, 'before the first use');
    await signin.resolveGoogleSignIn(claims());
    const after = await list();
    assert(after.google?.address === 'tal@gmail.com' && after.googleFromCalendar === false, `after ${show(after)}`);
    await identities.removeSignInMethod(TAL, 'google');
    assert(identitiesOf(TAL).length === 0 && userRow(TAL).googleCalendarSignIn === false, `row ${show(userRow(TAL))}`);
    world.googleAsks.length = 0;
    const again = await signin.resolveGoogleSignIn(claims());
    assert(show(again) === show({ status: 'no-account' }) && world.googleAsks.length === 0, `again ${show(again)}`);
    seed();
    await identities.removeSignInMethod(TAL, 'calendar-google');
    assert(userRow(TAL).googleCalendarSignIn === false && show(await signin.resolveGoogleSignIn(claims())) === show({ status: 'no-account' }), 'calendar row removed');
  });

  // ---- The startup pass ----

  function seedFill(): void {
    resetWorld();
    DB.user = [
      baseUser({ id: 9, telegramId: BigInt(901), googleRefreshToken: 'rt-a', googleAccountKey: null }),
      baseUser({ id: 10, telegramId: BigInt(902), googleRefreshToken: 'rt-b', googleAccountKey: `${OLD_ID}:${'0'.repeat(64)}` }),
      baseUser({ id: 11, telegramId: BigInt(903), googleRefreshToken: 'rt-c', googleAccountKey: account.googleAccountKey('c@example.net') }),
      baseUser({ id: 12, telegramId: BigInt(904), googleRefreshToken: '', googleAccountKey: null }),
    ];
    world.accounts = { 'rt-a': 'A@Gmail.com', 'rt-b': 'b@example.org', 'rt-c': 'c@example.net' };
  }

  await check('#13 the startup pass makes one select and fills only the connected rows with no key or a key of another id; the others are untouched', async () => {
    seedFill();
    await account.fillGoogleAccountKeys();
    assert(prismaCalls[0] === 'user.findMany' && prismaCalls.filter(c => c === 'user.findMany').length === 1, `calls ${show(prismaCalls)}`);
    assert(show([...world.googleAsks].sort()) === show(['rt-a', 'rt-b']), `asks ${show(world.googleAsks)}`);
    assert(userRow(9).googleAccountKey === account.googleAccountKey('a@gmail.com') && userRow(10).googleAccountKey === account.googleAccountKey('b@example.org'), `filled ${show([userRow(9).googleAccountKey, userRow(10).googleAccountKey])}`);
    assert(userRow(11).googleAccountKey === account.googleAccountKey('c@example.net') && userRow(12).googleAccountKey === null, 'an untouched row changed');
  });

  await check('#14 a row Google fails for is logged and captured and left as it was; the next boot asks for it alone, and a boot after that makes its one select and nothing else', async () => {
    seedFill();
    world.accounts['rt-b'] = new Error('calendars.get(primary) answered HTTP 401');
    await account.fillGoogleAccountKeys();
    assert(userRow(9).googleAccountKey === account.googleAccountKey('a@gmail.com') && userRow(10).googleAccountKey === `${OLD_ID}:${'0'.repeat(64)}`, `rows ${show([userRow(9).googleAccountKey, userRow(10).googleAccountKey])}`);
    assert(captured.some(c => c.context === 'google-account-check' && c.extra.user_id === 10), `captured ${show(captured)}`);
    assert(logs.some(l => l.includes('[google-account] startup pass: 1 filled, 1 left')), `logs ${show(logs)}`);
    world.accounts['rt-b'] = 'b@example.org';
    world.googleAsks.length = 0;
    await account.fillGoogleAccountKeys();
    assert(show(world.googleAsks) === show(['rt-b']) && userRow(10).googleAccountKey === account.googleAccountKey('b@example.org'), `second boot ${show(world.googleAsks)}`);
    world.googleAsks.length = 0;
    prismaCalls.length = 0;
    await account.fillGoogleAccountKeys();
    assert(show(prismaCalls) === show(['user.findMany']) && world.googleAsks.length === 0, `all filled: calls ${show(prismaCalls)} asks ${show(world.googleAsks)}`);
  });

  await check('#15 a calendar reconnected while the pass asked Google keeps the key its own connect wrote (the pass writes only over the token it read)', async () => {
    seedFill();
    world.accounts['rt-a'] = () => {
      Object.assign(userRow(9), { googleRefreshToken: 'rt-a2', googleAccountKey: 'from-the-connect' });
      return 'a@gmail.com';
    };
    await account.fillGoogleAccountKeys();
    assert(userRow(9).googleAccountKey === 'from-the-connect', `key ${userRow(9).googleAccountKey}`);
  });

  await check('#16 without SESSION_SECRET the pass makes no query at all and says so in one line that does not name the variable (startup names it once: smoke-auth-leftovers #5 counts the lines that do)', async () => {
    seedFill();
    const secret = process.env.SESSION_SECRET;
    try {
      process.env.SESSION_SECRET = '';
      await account.fillGoogleAccountKeys();
      assert(prismaCalls.length === 0 && world.googleAsks.length === 0, `calls ${show(prismaCalls)}`);
      assert(logs.some(l => l.includes('[google-account] no sign-in key, so the calendar accounts are not keyed')), `logs ${show(logs)}`);
      assert(!logs.some(l => l.includes('SESSION_SECRET')), `a line names SESSION_SECRET: ${show(logs)}`);
    } finally {
      process.env.SESSION_SECRET = secret;
    }
  });

  await check('#17 [guard] instrumentation.ts starts the pass once, after the scheduler; the new modules make no raw fetch (every Google call is getGoogleAuth or googleFetch)', () => {
    const text = fs.readFileSync(path.join(ROOT, 'instrumentation.ts'), 'utf8');
    const at = text.indexOf('fillGoogleAccountKeys');
    assert(text.indexOf('startScheduler()') !== -1 && at > text.indexOf('startScheduler()'), 'the pass is not started after the scheduler');
    assert((text.match(/fillGoogleAccountKeys\(\)/g) ?? []).length === 1, 'the pass is started more than once');
    for (const file of ['src/services/web-signin/calendar-account.ts', 'src/services/web-signin/account-key.ts']) {
      const source = fs.readFileSync(path.join(ROOT, file), 'utf8');
      assert(!/\bfetch\(/.test(source) && !source.includes('googleapis.com'), `${file} calls Google on its own`);
    }
  });

  await check('#18 [R9] an account on the same Google account whose switch is off is not a second holder: the one with the switch on is matched (not "several"); with both off nobody is', async () => {
    seed();
    DB.user.push(baseUser({ id: 10, name: 'Family', telegramId: BigInt(333333333), googleRefreshToken: 'rt-family', googleAccountKey: KEY_TAL, googleCalendarSignIn: false }));
    const r = await signin.resolveGoogleSignIn(claims());
    assert(r.user?.id === TAL && show(world.googleAsks) === show(['rt-tal']), `result ${show(r)} asks ${show(world.googleAsks)}`);
    seed();
    DB.user.push(baseUser({ id: 10, name: 'Family', telegramId: BigInt(333333333), googleRefreshToken: 'rt-family', googleAccountKey: KEY_TAL, googleCalendarSignIn: false }));
    userRow(TAL).googleCalendarSignIn = false;
    const none = await signin.resolveGoogleSignIn(claims());
    assert(show(none) === show({ status: 'no-account' }) && world.googleAsks.length === 0 && (DB.signInIdentity ?? []).length === 0, `result ${show(none)} asks ${show(world.googleAsks)}`);
  });

  await check('#19 [R5] a banned account (its Telegram id is on the block list) is answered, not matched: no Google way, no notice, and the callback lands on status=blocked with no session', async () => {
    seed();
    DB.blockedIdentifier = [{ id: 1, telegramId: BigInt(TAL_TG), whatsappPhone: null, createdAt: new Date() }];
    const r = await signin.resolveGoogleSignIn(claims());
    assert(r.user?.id === TAL && identitiesOf(TAL).length === 0 && sent.length === 0, `result ${show(r)} ways ${show(identitiesOf(TAL))} sent ${show(sent)}`);
    const res = await signInWithGoogle(claims());
    assert(location(res).includes('status=blocked') && !res.cookies.get(SESSION_COOKIE_NAME)?.value && identitiesOf(TAL).length === 0, `callback ${location(res)}`);
  });

  await check('#20 [R3] [guard] the boot pass runs only when Google sign-in is set up: instrumentation.ts asks providerConfigured(\'google\') before fillGoogleAccountKeys(), and logs one line when it is off', () => {
    const text = fs.readFileSync(path.join(ROOT, 'instrumentation.ts'), 'utf8');
    const ask = text.indexOf("providerConfigured('google')");
    const run = text.indexOf('fillGoogleAccountKeys()');
    assert(ask !== -1 && run !== -1 && ask < run, 'the pass is not behind providerConfigured(\'google\')');
    assert(text.includes('[google-account] Google sign-in is off: the calendar accounts are not keyed yet'), 'no line when the pass is off');
  });

  await check('#21 no console line and no capture holds an address', () => {
    const text = [...everyLog, ...everyCapture.map(c => `${c.context} ${c.message} ${show(c.extra)}`)].join('\n').toLowerCase();
    const found = ['tal@gmail.com', 'other@gmail.com', 'old@gmail.com', 'a@gmail.com', 'b@example.org', 'c@example.net'].filter(a => text.includes(a));
    assert(found.length === 0, `leaked ${show(found)}`);
  });

  report();
}

main().catch(err => {
  process.stdout.write(`${err instanceof Error ? err.stack : String(err)}\n`);
  process.exit(1);
});

- [ ] **Step 3: Write `src/services/web-signin/account-key.ts`**

```ts
/**
 * The keyed hash of a Google account's address (web sign-in spec §2.17): what FamCal keeps of the account a calendar
 * is connected from, so that a Google sign-in with that account can find the person. Never the address itself. The key
 * is appKey('google-account') (HKDF from SESSION_SECRET with its own label); the value starts with the key's id, so the
 * startup pass (calendar-account.ts) can tell a key made under another SESSION_SECRET and make it again. Pure, with no
 * I/O, so the OAuth callback and google-connect.ts import it without the sign-in modules.
 */

import crypto from 'crypto';
import { appKey } from '../../lib/app-keys';

const idOf = (key: Buffer) => crypto.createHmac('sha256', key).update('key-id').digest('hex').slice(0, 8);

/** The id of the key in use: the first 8 hex of HMAC(key, 'key-id'); null when SESSION_SECRET is unset. */
export function googleAccountKeyId(): string | null {
  const key = appKey('google-account');
  return key ? idOf(key) : null;
}

/** `<key id>:<hex HMAC-SHA256 of the trimmed, lower-cased address>`; null when SESSION_SECRET is unset or the address is empty. */
export function googleAccountKey(address: string): string | null {
  const normalized = address.trim().toLowerCase();
  if (!normalized) return null;
  const key = appKey('google-account');
  if (!key) return null;
  return `${idOf(key)}:${crypto.createHmac('sha256', key).update(`address:${normalized}`).digest('hex')}`;
}

- [ ] **Step 4: Write `src/services/web-signin/calendar-account.ts`**

```ts
/**
 * The Google account a calendar is connected from also signs in (web sign-in spec §2.17; the owner's request: the
 * person proved that account is theirs when they connected it).
 *
 * What is kept: User.googleAccountKey, the keyed hash of the connected account's address (account-key.ts), written by
 * the connect's commit (google-connect.ts) and cleared by the disconnect; and User.googleCalendarSignIn (default on,
 * turned off by removing the calendar's row or any Google way in Settings). The calendar consent has no openid, so the
 * address is the account's primary calendar id (googleAccountOf, as the copy to Google reads it).
 *
 * At sign-in (matchCalendarAccount, when (google, sub) found nobody): the verified address's key is looked up. Exactly
 * one account holding it with a live connection, its switch on and no Google way yet → Google is asked again with that
 * account's calendar token (syncGoogle(token).account(): getGoogleAuth, then googleAccountOf through googleFetch), and
 * its primary calendar must be the verified address right now. Then a Google way is made for that sub, the chat gets
 * the notice, and the person is signed in. Several accounts on one Google account (a shared family account) → several;
 * anything else → no-account.
 *
 * Connections made before 6b, or keyed under another SESSION_SECRET, get their key from fillGoogleAccountKeys, run once
 * per boot from instrumentation.ts: one select, then one Google call per such connection; a failure is logged and left
 * for the next boot.
 *
 * No log line holds an address: the user id only.
 */

import { prisma } from '../../utils/prisma';
import { readStoredToken } from '../../utils/encryption';
import { captureError } from '../../lib/error-capture';
import { getUserById } from '../user-service';
import { signInRefusal } from '../../lib/web-session';
import { syncGoogle } from '../google-sync/client';
import type { UserConfig } from '../../types';
import type { GoogleClaims } from './oidc';
import { addIdentity, hasIdentity } from './identities';
import { sendSignInNotice } from './notice';
import { googleAccountKey, googleAccountKeyId } from './account-key';

export { googleAccountKey, googleAccountKeyId } from './account-key';

export type CalendarMatch = { user: UserConfig } | { status: 'no-account' | 'several' };

const sameAddress = (a: string, b: string) => a.trim().toLowerCase() === b.trim().toLowerCase();

/** The account a stored calendar token belongs to now, or null (no token, or Google didn't tell: logged and captured). */
async function liveAccountOf(userId: number, storedToken: string): Promise<string | null> {
  const token = readStoredToken(storedToken, { userId, column: 'googleRefreshToken' });
  if (!token) {
    console.warn(`[google-account] user ${userId}: no usable calendar token to ask Google with`);
    return null;
  }
  try {
    return await syncGoogle(token).account();
  } catch (error) {
    console.warn(`[google-account] user ${userId}: Google did not tell the calendar's account: ${error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error)}`);
    captureError(error, 'google-account-check', { user_id: userId }, 'warning');
    return null;
  }
}

export async function matchCalendarAccount(claims: GoogleClaims): Promise<CalendarMatch> {
  if (!claims.emailVerified || !claims.email) return { status: 'no-account' };
  const key = googleAccountKey(claims.email);
  if (!key) {
    console.warn('[signin] google: no account key (SESSION_SECRET is unset), so no calendar match');
    return { status: 'no-account' };
  }
  // Spec §2.17: exactly one account with the switch on, a live connection and no Google way. Only accounts with the
  // switch on and a connection are holders, so an account that turned it off (or disconnected) is not a second one.
  const holders = await prisma.user.findMany({
    where: { googleAccountKey: key, googleCalendarSignIn: true, NOT: { googleRefreshToken: '' } },
    select: { id: true, googleRefreshToken: true },
    orderBy: { id: 'asc' },
    take: 2,
  });
  if (holders.length === 0) return { status: 'no-account' };
  if (holders.length > 1) {
    console.warn(`[signin] google: the calendar account is connected on several FamCal accounts (${holders.map(h => h.id).join(', ')}): no match`);
    return { status: 'several' };
  }
  const [holder] = holders;
  if (await hasIdentity(holder.id, 'google')) {
    console.log(`[signin] user ${holder.id}: has another Google way, so the calendar's account does not sign in`);
    return { status: 'no-account' };
  }
  const live = await liveAccountOf(holder.id, holder.googleRefreshToken);
  if (live === null || !sameAddress(live, claims.email)) {
    console.warn(`[signin] user ${holder.id}: the live check of the calendar's Google account did not agree`);
    return { status: 'no-account' };
  }
  const user = await getUserById(holder.id);
  if (!user) return { status: 'no-account' };
  // A suspended or banned account is answered, and finishSignIn refuses it with its page (signInRefusal is the one rule
  // it uses): nothing is attached or sent.
  if (await signInRefusal(user)) return { user };
  const added = await addIdentity(user.id, 'google', claims.sub, claims.email, { usedNow: true });
  if (added === 'taken' || added === 'has-one') {
    console.warn(`[signin] user ${user.id}: the calendar match could not make the Google way (${added})`);
    return { status: 'no-account' };
  }
  // 'kept' (a request made the same way a moment ago) sends no second notice: the one that made it did
  if (added === 'added') await sendSignInNotice(user, { kind: 'google', address: claims.email, via: 'calendar' });
  console.log(`[signin] user ${user.id}: signed in with the Google account their calendar is connected from`);
  return { user };
}

/**
 * The startup pass: give every connected calendar with no key, or a key of another key id, its account key. One select,
 * then for each such row one Google call and one write; the write is made only over the token the select read, so a
 * reconnect in between keeps its own. Never throws.
 */
export async function fillGoogleAccountKeys(): Promise<void> {
  const keyId = googleAccountKeyId();
  if (!keyId) {
    // Startup names the missing variable once (smoke-auth-leftovers #5 counts the lines that do), so this line does not
    console.warn('[google-account] no sign-in key, so the calendar accounts are not keyed');
    return;
  }
  let rows: { id: number; googleRefreshToken: string }[];
  try {
    rows = await prisma.user.findMany({
      where: {
        NOT: { googleRefreshToken: '' },
        OR: [{ googleAccountKey: null }, { NOT: { googleAccountKey: { startsWith: `${keyId}:` } } }],
      },
      select: { id: true, googleRefreshToken: true },
      orderBy: { id: 'asc' },
    });
  } catch (error) {
    captureError(error, 'google-account-fill');
    return;
  }
  if (rows.length === 0) {
    console.log('[google-account] startup pass: every connected calendar has its account key');
    return;
  }
  let filled = 0;
  for (const row of rows) {
    const live = await liveAccountOf(row.id, row.googleRefreshToken);
    const key = live ? googleAccountKey(live) : null;
    if (!key) continue;
    try {
      const { count } = await prisma.user.updateMany({
        where: { id: row.id, googleRefreshToken: row.googleRefreshToken },
        data: { googleAccountKey: key },
      });
      if (count === 1) filled++;
      else console.log(`[google-account] user ${row.id}: the calendar changed while the pass asked; its connect keeps its own key`);
    } catch (error) {
      captureError(error, 'google-account-fill', { user_id: row.id }, 'warning');
    }
  }
  console.log(`[google-account] startup pass: ${filled} filled, ${rows.length - filled} left`);
}
```

- [ ] **Step 10: Start the pass at boot, only once Google sign-in is set up** (`instrumentation.ts:17-21`; ruling R3)

Until the owner sets the `GOOGLE_SIGNIN_CLIENT_*` variables the way is hidden, so the pass would ask Google about every connected calendar for nothing. A redeploy after the owner sets them (Railway redeploys on a variable change) runs it, so every connected account is keyed on that first boot.

```ts

    startScheduler();

    const { captureError } = await import('./src/lib/error-capture');
```
After:

    // Start in-process cron scheduler (replaces QStash)
    const { startScheduler } = await import('./src/cron/scheduler');
    startScheduler();

    const { captureError } = await import('./src/lib/error-capture');

    // The Google account a calendar is connected from signs in on the web (web sign-in spec §2.17): give connections made
    // before it, or keyed under another SESSION_SECRET, their account key. Only once Google sign-in is set up (until then
    // the way is hidden and the pass would ask Google about every connected calendar for nothing; the deploy that sets
    // the GOOGLE_SIGNIN_CLIENT_* variables runs it). One select per boot, one Google call per connection still without a
    // key; never awaited, never throws (a failure is logged and left for the next boot).
    Promise.all([import('./src/services/web-signin/oidc'), import('./src/services/web-signin/calendar-account')])
      .then(([{ providerConfigured }, { fillGoogleAccountKeys }]) =>
        providerConfigured('google')
          ? fillGoogleAccountKeys()
          : console.log('[google-account] Google sign-in is off: the calendar accounts are not keyed yet'))
      .catch(err => captureError(err, 'google-account-fill'));

To limit the match to Gmail and Workspace (`hd`) addresses, `GoogleClaims` needs `hd`, plus one line in `matchCalendarAccount`. This is an owner call, since spec §2.17 is approved as written.

## Part F: Tasks 8 and 9 (the sign-in pages and Settings → Sign in on the web)

Spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-02-web-sign-in-design.md` §2.7, §2.9, §2.11, §2.13, §2.17, §3, §4. Contract: `plan/contract.md`.
Code facts below were read at main 2b38fc4c (file:line refer to that tree).

### Contract notes (corrections and additions; names otherwise exactly as the contract)

1. **The add-Google page reads its token with Task 6's `peekAddGoogleToken`** (crosscheck item 3). The one module for the
   one-time Add Google link is `src/services/web-signin/add-google.ts` (part E Task 6 Step 8): the token is 24 random
   bytes as base64url (32 characters, `/^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{32}$/`), Redis keeps only its sha256 under `signin:add-google:<hex>`,
   and `peekAddGoogleToken(token: unknown): Promise<{ userId: number } | null>` reads it with a `GET` (never `GETDEL`;
   only `takeAddGoogleToken`, called by `add-start`, uses the link up). `peekAddGoogleToken` itself refuses anything that
   is not a 32-character base64url string before any Redis read, so the page does not repeat the regex: one code path.
   The link's query parameter is **`token`** (`/signin/add-google?token=<token>`), the name Task 3's scrubber already
   drops from Sentry and logs; this part has no module of its own for the link.
2. **`POST /api/auth/google/add-start` failure shape:** a used, late or unknown token answers **410
   `{ error: 'expired' }`**; anything else is a 4xx/5xx with `{ error }`. The add-Google page says "start again from
   Settings" on 410 (and 404), and "couldn't open Google" on the rest.
3. **`POST /api/signin-methods/email/add` failure shapes** (the contract only names `{ ok: true }`): an address
   `normalizeEmail` refuses answers **400 `{ ok: false, error: 'invalid' }`**, and `allowCodeRequest` refusing (any
   `LimitReason`) answers **429 `{ ok: false, error: 'limit' }`**. `verifyUserAuth`'s own 429 (the route's rate limiter)
   stays `{ error: 'Too many requests…' }`; the UI words that one as "too many tries". The account is signed in, so
   these honest answers enumerate nothing (the generic answer is only for `/api/auth/email/request`).
4. **`methods` in the confirm and remove answers is `SignInMethodsView` without `session`.** The Settings group keeps
   the `session` it read from `GET /api/signin-methods` (a remove gives this device a fresh cookie with the same method,
   so the value doesn't change).
5. **How Settings calls the routes** (crosscheck item 2): `POST` with `Content-Type: application/json`,
   `credentials: 'same-origin'`, **`user_id` in the query string** (`/api/signin-methods/email/add?user_id=7`, as every
   user route in the repo reads it: `app/api/google-disconnect/route.ts:24-26`; part E note 2), the body only the
   route's own fields (`{ email }`, `{ code }`, `{ which }`, `{}`), and the initData in the `X-Telegram-Init-Data` header
   (`initDataHeaders()`), never the body or the URL. The routes read it with `requestInitData(request, body)`
   (`src/lib/request-init-data.ts:9`). `GET /api/signin-methods?user_id=` carries the header the same way, and so does
   `POST /api/auth/signout-all?user_id=`.
6. **The add-link URL** is absolute (E's `createAddGoogleLink` returns `buildUrl(localeHref(lang, '/signin/add-google?token=' +
   token))`, `localeHref` from `src/site/zmanim/links.ts:21`, so English is the unprefixed `/signin/add-google?token=` the
   site serves without a locale redirect hop); the UI still resolves it with `new URL(url, window.location.origin)`,
   which leaves an absolute URL as it is.
7. **One sign-in path builder, created by Task 2** (ruling R2). Part A Task 2 creates `src/site/signin.ts` with
   `signInHref(locale, status?)` (unknown locales fall back to English: `xx` becomes `/signin`) and
   `signInPageUrl` in `web-session.ts` is `new URL(signInHref(locale, status), getBaseUrl()).toString()`. **Task 8
   MODIFIES that file** (it adds `SIGNIN_STATUSES`, `OutcomeStatus`, `STATUS_KEY`, `readSignInStatus`, `isOutcome`) and
   keeps Task 2's `signInHref` exactly as it is: this part has no builder of its own and no step that replaces
   `signInPageUrl`. The file must stay importable by client components (no Prisma, no Redis, no server-only module); it
   imports `localeHref` (`src/site/zmanim/links.ts`), `normalizeLocale` (`src/utils/locale.ts`) and, type only, `SignInStatus` (part G's smoke-web-fixes #8 fails on any other value import).
8. **`providerConfigured` and `emailConfigured` read the env on every call** (the page is per request; the smoke flips
   the env between renders). Checked against parts C and D: `providerConfigured` reads the two variables through `credentials()` on every call, and `emailConfigured` is `Boolean(process.env.RESEND_API_KEY)`; only the discovered OIDC configuration is cached. The smoke's P1 pins it.
9. **The Settings group's title** (ruling R1, binding for E, F and H alike) is he "כניסה מהדפדפן", ru "Вход через
   браузер", en "Sign in on the web"; its remove button he "הסרה", ru "Убрать", en "Remove". Task 6's chat notices (`signinNotice.*`) should name the path with these

    (`kind`, `tone`, `valueDir`) added to `CODE_PROPS`.

11. **Two more outcomes: `taken` and `has-one`** (crosscheck item 4). Part A Task 2 widens `SignInStatus` with
    `'taken'` (this Google account already signs in to another FamCal account) and `'has-one'` (this account already has

### Design (frontend-design pass)

The brief pins the visual direction: the site's and the app kit's own tokens, so nothing new is invented.

- **Colour:** the site's tokens (`--ch-bg`, `--ch-card`, `--ch-surface`, `--ch-text`, `--ch-muted`, `--ch-accent`,
  `--ch-button`), Telegram's existing brand shade (`--site-telegram`, 5.4:1 under white), and Google's own button
  colours as three new tokens (light `#ffffff` / `#1f1f1f` / `#747775` border; dark `#131314` / `#e3e3e3` / `#8e918f`).
- **Type:** the site's system stack; the page title is the site's `.site-h1 .site-page-title`; the ways at 17 px 600.
- **Layout:** one narrow start-aligned column (560 px), like the zmanim index: the title, one line, then a single
  panel (`--ch-card`, 20 px radius, as Near me's) that holds the three ways stacked full width. Choosing email turns
  the panel into the address form, then the code form; "Other ways to sign in" turns it back. An outcome (no account,
  several, suspended, blocked) replaces the panel with its own words and actions.

  ```
  Sign in to FamCal
  Open your family calendar in any browser…
  ┌──────────────────────────────────────┐
  │ [ ✈ Continue with Telegram        ] │
  │   Telegram asks you to approve…      │
  │ [ G Continue with Google          ] │
  │ [ ✉ Email me a code               ] │
  └──────────────────────────────────────┘
  Signing in works for FamCal accounts…
  ```
- **Review against the generic sign-in page** (centred card, "Welcome back", social buttons, an "or" divider, an
  email field always shown): no "Welcome back" (the title says what the page does), start-aligned like every site page,
  no divider and no always-open field (the spec names three equal ways, and the field would push Google below the fold
  on a phone), no logo inside the card (the header has it). The one memorable thing is restraint: three ways that read
  as one family, Google's in Google's own colours as its rules require.
- **Settings:** the kit only (SectionLabel, FormCard, FormRow, ButtonRow, action rows, BottomSheet, TextField, Notice),
  mirroring the Google Calendar section (a card of rows, a danger confirm in a sheet).
- Quality floor: 44 px targets (ways 52 px), 16 px inputs, visible focus (`.site :focus-visible`), logical properties
  for RTL, no hover, reduced motion stops the one spinner, loading states that clear on failure with words.

Create `scripts/lib/jsx-copy.ts` (the block of `scripts/smoke-site-truth.ts:60-105`, moved as it is, exported, with the
code props the sign-in forms and the app kit use added):

```ts
// The copy scanner the smokes share: the user-facing strings written in a TSX source, read with TypeScript's parser
// (smoke-site-truth T3 over the site, smoke-signin-ui U10 over Settings' sign-in group). JSX text, and a string with
// letters shown as a child or through a prop that renders text, is copy; a code prop's value (a class list, a path, an
// id, an input's autofill or keyboard hint) is not, unless it reads like a sentence.
// scripts/lib/ is not a smoke (ci-smokes.sh runs scripts/smoke-*.ts only).

import ts from 'typescript';

/** JSX props whose value is code, never shown: a string with letters in any other prop is copy. */
export const CODE_PROPS = new Set([
  'className', 'id', 'key', 'href', 'src', 'rel', 'type', 'role', 'dir', 'lang', 'scope', 'target', 'variant', 'level', 'path', 'doc', 'focusable',
  'aria-hidden', 'aria-current', 'aria-haspopup', 'aria-expanded', 'aria-live', 'aria-modal', 'aria-labelledby', 'aria-describedby', 'aria-controls',
  // An input's autofill, keyboard and label wiring (the sign-in forms), and the app kit's own code props
  'autoComplete', 'autoCapitalize', 'inputMode', 'enterKeyHint', 'htmlFor', 'name', 'kind', 'tone', 'valueDir',
]);
const BRAND = new Set(['FamCal']);
const hasWords = (text: string) => {
  const t = text.replace(/&[a-z]+;/g, '').trim();
  return t !== '' && /\p{L}/u.test(t) && !BRAND.has(t);
};

/** The strings an expression shows as its value: a literal, or one a ?:, || or ?? (or the right of &&) gives back. */
function shownLiterals(e: ts.Expression): string[] {
  if (ts.isParenthesizedExpression(e)) return shownLiterals(e.expression);
  if (ts.isStringLiteral(e) || ts.isNoSubstitutionTemplateLiteral(e)) return [e.text];
  if (ts.isTemplateExpression(e)) return [e.head.text, ...e.templateSpans.map((span) => span.literal.text)];
  if (ts.isConditionalExpression(e)) return [...shownLiterals(e.whenTrue), ...shownLiterals(e.whenFalse)];
  if (ts.isBinaryExpression(e)) {
    const op = e.operatorToken.kind;
    if (op === ts.SyntaxKind.BarBarToken || op === ts.SyntaxKind.QuestionQuestionToken) return [...shownLiterals(e.left), ...shownLiterals(e.right)];
    if (op === ts.SyntaxKind.AmpersandAmpersandToken) return shownLiterals(e.right);
  }
  return [];
}

/** The copy written in a TSX source: JSX text, and strings shown as a child or through a prop that renders text. */
export function jsxCopy(file: string, source: string): string[] {
  const sf = ts.createSourceFile(file, source, ts.ScriptTarget.Latest, true, ts.ScriptKind.TSX);
  const found: string[] = [];
  const visit = (node: ts.Node) => {
    if (ts.isJsxText(node) && hasWords(node.text)) found.push(`${file}: "${node.text.trim()}"`);
    if (ts.isJsxExpression(node) && node.expression && !ts.isJsxAttribute(node.parent)) {
      for (const text of shownLiterals(node.expression)) if (hasWords(text)) found.push(`${file}: {"${text}"}`);
    }
    if (ts.isJsxAttribute(node) && node.initializer) {
      const name = node.name.getText(sf);
      const code = CODE_PROPS.has(name) || /^data-/.test(name);
      const values = ts.isStringLiteral(node.initializer) ? [node.initializer.text] : ts.isJsxExpression(node.initializer) && node.initializer.expression ? shownLiterals(node.initializer.expression) : [];
      for (const text of values) {
        // A code prop's value is a code word (a class list, a path, an id); one with spaces and capitals is copy
        if (code && !/[A-Z][a-z]+ [a-z]/.test(text)) continue;
        if (hasWords(text)) found.push(`${file}: ${name}="${text}"`);
      }
    }
    ts.forEachChild(node, visit);
  };
  visit(sf);
  return found;
}
```
