`src/lib/command-target.ts` becomes (whole file; `resolveCommandTarget` keeps its old behaviour for every old call):

```ts
/**
 * Where a command started from the web app answers: the chat that belongs to the
 * proved user, and how they signed in. A DB id is never used as a chat id (for a
 * WhatsApp-only user it used to become Telegram chat <DB id>, which is someone else's
 * chat or nobody's).
 */

import type { UserConfig } from '../types';
import { MessagingPlatform } from '../services/messaging/types';
import { getWhatsAppChatId } from '../services/user-service';
import type { AuthVia } from './api-auth';
import type { SignInMethod } from './session-auth';

export interface CommandTarget {
  platform: MessagingPlatform;
  chatId: number | string;
}

/**
 * Why there is no chat: 'wa_link_needed' is a WhatsApp-only account signed in another way
 * (Telegram, Google or email). WhatsApp refuses a free reply once 24 hours have passed
 * since the person's last message, so only a session opened from WhatsApp's own link
 * (which means they just wrote) may answer there. 'no_channel' is an account with neither chat.
 */
export type CommandTargetRefusal = 'wa_link_needed' | 'no_channel';

export type CommandTargetResult = { ok: true; target: CommandTarget } | { ok: false; reason: CommandTargetRefusal };

/**
 * - A 'wa' session (the WhatsApp link, and any cookie from before web sign-in) with a WhatsApp
 *   chat id answers on WhatsApp (phone, else BSUID).
 * - Otherwise, a user with a telegramId answers on Telegram: Telegram initData, an operator
 *   call, and a tg, google or email session.
 * - A tg, google or email session of a WhatsApp-only account: refused, 'wa_link_needed'.
 * - Otherwise there is no channel.
 *
 * `via` is how the request was proved ('server' is the operator, CRON_SECRET); `method` is
 * the session's sign-in method, read only for a session (absent counts as 'wa').
 */
export function resolveCommandTargetOrReason(
  user: UserConfig,
  via: AuthVia | 'server',
  method?: SignInMethod | null,
): CommandTargetResult {
  const whatsappChatId = getWhatsAppChatId(user);
  const sessionMethod = via === 'session' ? (method ?? 'wa') : null;
  if (sessionMethod === 'wa' && whatsappChatId) {
    return { ok: true, target: { platform: MessagingPlatform.WHATSAPP, chatId: whatsappChatId } };
  }
  if (user.telegramId) {
    return { ok: true, target: { platform: MessagingPlatform.TELEGRAM, chatId: Number(user.telegramId) } };
  }
  if (sessionMethod !== null && sessionMethod !== 'wa' && whatsappChatId) {
    return { ok: false, reason: 'wa_link_needed' };
  }
  return { ok: false, reason: 'no_channel' };
}

/** The chat, or null when there is none (the reason: resolveCommandTargetOrReason). */
export function resolveCommandTarget(user: UserConfig, via: AuthVia | 'server', method?: SignInMethod | null): CommandTarget | null {
  const resolved = resolveCommandTargetOrReason(user, via, method);
  return resolved.ok ? resolved.target : null;
}
```

## Part H: Task 11 (legal texts, docs, startup checks, the owner's list)

Repo `/Users/razielgershoni/development/famcalbot`, branch `feat/web-sign-in`. The repo files below were read at `2b38fc4c`. Line numbers are as of that commit; Tasks 1–10 shift some of them, so every edit is anchored on its text. Task 11 runs last, after Tasks 1–10.

The relayed question ("shouldn't anyone with Google connected already have a Google login?"): yes, and the texts here say so. The Policy's "What we keep", "Google user data" and the Terms' account security all name "the Google account your calendar is connected from" (spec §2.17). Task 1's `googleCalendarSignIn DEFAULT true` and Task 7's startup pass make it true for every account connected before 6b.

### Contract notes (corrections and additions against the real code and the other parts)

1. **The `RESEND_API_KEY` README row is Task 5's** (part D, Step 13, before the `CRON_SECRET` row). Task 11b adds the other four rows, adds "production startup logs a warning" to that row, and leaves the rest of it as Task 5 wrote it.
2. **`SignInIdentity` is touched in two files.** `identities.ts` (Task 4) is the one home of the Google and email ways, and Task 5 puts the email way's lookups (`findEmailSignIn`, `emailSignInAccount`, `touchEmailSignIn`) there too, imported from `identities.ts` by the two email routes (crosscheck item 10); `email-code.ts` reads no `SignInIdentity` row. The other file is Task 1's merge, which moves rows in `account-linking.ts`. The CLAUDE.md rule (Task 11b) names exactly those two files, and `smoke-signin-setup` S2 fails on any other file that uses `.signInIdentity`, `email-code.ts` included.
3. **The truth list forbids "sign in with Google" in every public string, legal texts included** (`scripts/lib/site-harness.ts:63`, the "Google as a step" entry). After 6b that sentence is true, and spec §7's Policy text uses it twice, so `smoke-site-truth` T1 and `smoke-site-pages` would fail. Task 11a drops only that alternative. The old-copy sample keeps tripping the entry through "Connect your Google Calendars", so T1's self-check still holds. Tasks 8–10 may then use the words too.
4. **The startup check is a new pure function, not new `StartupProblem`s.** `startupSecretProblems` feeds Sentry (`startup-secret`) and the deploy message's `missing:` line, which `smoke-fail-closed` #10 pins exactly. So `src/lib/startup-checks.ts` gains `SIGN_IN_ENV` and `signInSetupWarnings(env): string[]`. `instrumentation.ts`'s production block prints each line with `console.warn('[startup] …')`: no capture, not in the deploy message, never fatal. It also warns when `GOOGLE_SIGNIN_CLIENT_ID` equals `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID`, the same rule as Task 4's `credentials()` (part C, note 8).
5. **The `SESSION_SECRET` startup line changes** from "WhatsApp sign-in and share-story image links are refused" to "web sign-in and share-story image links are refused", because after 6b every web sign-in needs it. `smoke-fail-closed` (`PROBLEM.session`, `:203`) and `smoke-auth-leftovers` (#5, `:204`) pin the line and change with it.
6. **The counters sentence goes after "Visiting the site creates no account or profile."**, not inside the IP sentence that §7's "…" suggests. `smoke-site-pages` P7 pins the 6a sentence whole (`:302-330`), and the meaning is the same.
7. **`famcal_signin` is its own cookie line.** Spec §7 nests it under the session cookie, but it is a different cookie, so it gets its own list item. The text is unchanged.
8. **`LEGAL_UPDATED` is the day the text ships:** `'2026-11-03'`, or the push day (Israel) if that is later. `smoke-signin-legal` L3 accepts any day from 2026-11-03.
9. **`smoke-site-pages.ts:170` pins the old cookie name** (part A, note 10). Task 11a changes it to `__Host-famcal_session`.
10. **`smoke-auth-leftovers` #5 asserts exactly one startup line containing `SESSION_SECRET`.** Task 7's pass (part E) no longer names the variable (`[google-account] no sign-in key, so the calendar accounts are not keyed`, crosscheck item 12), and Task 7 Step 11 stubs the pass in `smoke-auth-leftovers` and `smoke-fail-closed`, so #5 keeps passing with this task's new `SESSION_SECRET` wording (note 5).

```ts
/** What no language may still say: the cookie's old name, the WhatsApp-only cookie line, the one account to keep safe. */
const GONE: Record<Locale, [Doc, RegExp][]> = {
  en: [['privacy', /(?<!__Host-)famcal_session/], ['privacy', /after you open it from WhatsApp/], ['terms', /Keep that account safe/]],
  he: [['privacy', /(?<!__Host-)famcal_session/], ['privacy', /אחרי שפותחים אותה מוואטסאפ/], ['terms', /שמרו היטב על החשבון הזה/]],
  ru: [['privacy', /(?<!__Host-)famcal_session/], ['privacy', /после того, как вы открыли его из WhatsApp/], ['terms', /Берегите этот аккаунт/]],
};

async function main() {
  await check('L1 the Privacy Policy and the Terms hold the same legal.* leaves (every key and list position) in en, he and ru', () => {
    const paths = (l: Locale) => leaves(messages[l].legal, 'legal').map(([at]) => at);
    const en = new Set(paths('en'));
    for (const locale of ['he', 'ru'] as const) {
      const other = new Set(paths(locale));
      const missing = [...en].filter((p) => !other.has(p));
      const extra = [...other].filter((p) => !en.has(p));
      assert(missing.length === 0 && extra.length === 0, `${locale}: missing ${show(missing.slice(0, 8))}, extra ${show(extra.slice(0, 8))}`);
    }
  });

  await check('L2 each language says what spec §7 adds (who, what we keep, the counters, Google sign-in, the providers, Resend bound and in the US, the cookies, retention, the cookie check, removing and deleting the ways, the Terms\' account security), and none still says the old cookie line or "keep that account safe"', () => {
    const problems: string[] = [];
    for (const locale of LOCALES) {
      for (const [doc, sentence] of SAYS[locale]) if (!text(locale, doc).includes(sentence)) problems.push(`${locale} ${doc}: no "${sentence}"`);
      for (const [doc, old] of GONE[locale]) if (old.test(text(locale, doc))) problems.push(`${locale} ${doc}: still ${old}`);
    }
    assert(problems.length === 0, problems.join('\n'));
  });

  await check('L3 LEGAL_UPDATED moved for both pages to the day the text changed (2026-11-03 or later)', async () => {
    const { LEGAL_UPDATED } = (await import(path.join(ROOT, 'src/site/legal.ts'))) as Row;
    assert(LEGAL_UPDATED.privacy >= '2026-11-03' && LEGAL_UPDATED.terms >= '2026-11-03', `LEGAL_UPDATED ${show(LEGAL_UPDATED)}`);
  });

  await check('L4 the cookies the Policy names are the code\'s, with its lengths (the session 30 days on famcal.bot and 24 hours from a WhatsApp link, the sign-in check 10 minutes), in en, he and ru', () => {
    const session = read('src/lib/session-auth.ts');
    const flow = read('src/services/web-signin/flow.ts');
    const product = (s: string) => s.split('*').reduce((n, f) => n * Number(f.trim()), 1);
    const sessionName = /export const SESSION_COOKIE_NAME = '([^']+)'/.exec(session)?.[1];
    const ttl = /export const SESSION_TTL_SEC = \{ wa: ([\d\s*]+), web: ([\d\s*]+) \}/.exec(session);
    const signinName = /export const SIGNIN_COOKIE_NAME = '([^']+)'/.exec(flow)?.[1];
    const flowTtl = /const FLOW_TTL_SEC = ([\d\s*]+);/.exec(flow)?.[1];
    assert(sessionName && ttl && signinName && flowTtl, `not found: ${show({ sessionName, ttl: ttl?.[0], signinName, flowTtl })}`);
    assert(product(ttl[1]) === 24 * 60 * 60 && product(ttl[2]) === 30 * 24 * 60 * 60, `SESSION_TTL_SEC is ${ttl[0]}: the Policy says 24 hours and 30 days`);
    assert(product(flowTtl) === 10 * 60, `FLOW_TTL_SEC is ${flowTtl}: the Policy says 10 minutes`);
    for (const locale of LOCALES) {
      const policy = text(locale, 'privacy');
      for (const name of [sessionName, signinName]) assert(policy.includes(`\`${name}\``), `${locale}: the Policy does not name \`${name}\``);
    }
  });

  let failed = 0;
  for (const r of results) {
    console.log(`${r.ok ? 'OK' : 'FAIL'}  ${r.name}${r.ok ? '' : ` — ${r.reason}`}`);
    if (!r.ok) failed++;
  }
  console.log(`\n${results.length - failed}/${results.length} passed`);
  process.exit(failed ? 1 : 0);
}

main().catch((err) => {
  console.error(err);
  process.exit(1);
});
```

```js
// Applies web sign-in's changes to the Privacy Policy and the Terms (spec 2026-11-02-web-sign-in §7) to
// messages/{en,he,ru}.json. Only the `legal` subtree is rewritten, in the files' own format (2-space JSON); the rest of
// each file is kept byte for byte. Every change names the text it replaces and stops when that text isn't there exactly
// once, so a second run, or a run on text that moved, changes nothing. Russian new text gets its no-break spaces by the
// rule smoke-site-truth T6 holds (a one-letter word and the word after it, a space before an em dash).
//
// Usage: node legal-edit.mjs <dir that holds messages/>   (scratch tool, never committed)

import fs from 'node:fs';
import path from 'node:path';

const root = process.argv[2];
if (!root) throw new Error('usage: node legal-edit.mjs <dir that holds messages/>');

const NB = ' ';
const norm = (s) => s.replace(/ /g, ' ');
const ruTypo = (s) => s.replace(/(?<![^\s«(„"—*])([вскоуиая]) /giu, `$1${NB}`).replace(/ —/g, `${NB}—`);
const deep = (v, fn) =>
  typeof v === 'string' ? fn(v) : Array.isArray(v) ? v.map((x) => deep(x, fn)) : v && typeof v === 'object' ? Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(v).map(([k, x]) => [k, deep(x, fn)])) : v;
const textOf = (item) => (typeof item === 'string' ? item : item && typeof item === 'object' && !Array.isArray(item) ? item.text ?? '' : '');
const key = (k) => (/^\d+$/.test(k) ? Number(k) : k);

function at(obj, dotted) {
  return dotted.split('.').reduce((node, k) => {
    if (node == null || node[key(k)] === undefined) throw new Error(`no ${dotted} (at ${k})`);
    return node[key(k)];
  }, obj);
}

function apply(locale, legal, ops) {
  const fix = locale === 'ru' ? (v) => deep(v, ruTypo) : (v) => v;
  for (const op of ops) {
    if (op.edit) {
      const parts = op.edit.split('.');
      const parent = at(legal, parts.slice(0, -1).join('.'));
      const k = key(parts.at(-1));
      const old = parent[k];
      if (typeof old !== 'string') throw new Error(`${locale} ${op.edit}: not a string`);
      const plain = norm(old);
      const count = plain.split(op.from).length - 1;
      if (count !== 1) throw new Error(`${locale} ${op.edit}: "${op.from}" is there ${count} times, not once:\n${old}`);
      if (locale === 'ru' && ruTypo(plain) !== old) throw new Error(`${locale} ${op.edit}: its no-break spaces aren't T6's rule, so rewriting would move them`);
      parent[k] = fix(plain.replace(op.from, op.to));
    } else if (op.after) {
      const list = at(legal, op.after);
      const hits = list.map((x, i) => [i, norm(textOf(x))]).filter(([, t]) => t.startsWith(op.anchor));
      if (hits.length !== 1) throw new Error(`${locale} ${op.after}: ${hits.length} items start with "${op.anchor}"`);
      const next = list[hits[0][0] + 1];
      if (next !== undefined && norm(JSON.stringify(next)) === norm(JSON.stringify(fix(op.values[0])))) throw new Error(`${locale} ${op.after}: already applied`);
      list.splice(hits[0][0] + 1, 0, ...op.values.map(fix));
    } else if (op.swap) {
      const list = at(legal, op.swap);
      const hits = list.map((x, i) => [i, typeof x === 'string' ? norm(x) : null]).filter(([, t]) => t === op.old);
      if (hits.length !== 1) throw new Error(`${locale} ${op.swap}: ${hits.length} items are "${op.old}"`);
      list.splice(hits[0][0], 1, ...op.values.map(fix));
    } else {
      throw new Error(`unknown op ${JSON.stringify(op)}`);
    }
  }
}

const region = (legal) => `  "legal": ${JSON.stringify(legal, null, 2).replace(/\n/g, '\n  ')}`;

// All three are read and changed before any is written, so a failure leaves every file as it was.
const out = {};
for (const locale of ['en', 'he', 'ru']) {
  const file = path.join(root, 'messages', `${locale}.json`);
  const text = fs.readFileSync(file, 'utf8');
  const messages = JSON.parse(text);
  const start = text.indexOf('\n  "legal": {\n') + 1;
  const before = region(messages.legal);
  if (start === 0 || text.slice(start, start + before.length) !== before) throw new Error(`${locale}: legal is not where or how this script expects it`);
  apply(locale, messages.legal, OPS[locale]);
  const next = text.slice(0, start) + region(messages.legal) + text.slice(start + before.length);
  JSON.parse(next);
  out[file] = next;
}
for (const [file, text] of Object.entries(out)) fs.writeFileSync(file, text);
console.log(`legal texts updated: ${Object.keys(out).map((f) => path.basename(f)).join(', ')}`);
```

```ts
//    CLAUDE.md has the sign-in rule; and only the files that rule names touch SignInIdentity rows.
//
// Real: src/lib/startup-checks.ts and the files read as text. No network, no DB.
//
// Run with the fake env (never the real one), from the repo root:
//   bash <scratchpad>/6b/run-smoke.sh smoke-signin-setup

import fs from 'node:fs';
import path from 'node:path';

type Row = Record<string, any>; // eslint-disable-line @typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any
const ROOT = path.resolve(__dirname, '..');
const read = (rel: string) => fs.readFileSync(path.join(ROOT, rel), 'utf8');

type Result = { name: string; ok: boolean; reason?: string };
const results: Result[] = [];
async function check(name: string, fn: () => void | Promise<void>) {
  try {
    await fn();
    results.push({ name, ok: true });
  } catch (err) {
    results.push({ name, ok: false, reason: err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err) });
  }
}
function assert(cond: unknown, message: string): asserts cond {
  if (!cond) throw new Error(message);
}
const show = (v: unknown) => JSON.stringify(v);

const FIVE = ['TELEGRAM_LOGIN_CLIENT_ID', 'TELEGRAM_LOGIN_CLIENT_SECRET', 'GOOGLE_SIGNIN_CLIENT_ID', 'GOOGLE_SIGNIN_CLIENT_SECRET', 'RESEND_API_KEY'];
const ALL_OFF = [
  'web sign-in with Telegram is off: TELEGRAM_LOGIN_CLIENT_ID and TELEGRAM_LOGIN_CLIENT_SECRET are not set',
  'web sign-in with Google is off: GOOGLE_SIGNIN_CLIENT_ID and GOOGLE_SIGNIN_CLIENT_SECRET are not set',
  'web sign-in with an email code is off: RESEND_API_KEY is not set',
];

/** The files the CLAUDE.md rule lets read or write SignInIdentity rows. */
const SIGNIN_IDENTITY_FILES = ['src/services/web-signin/identities.ts', 'src/services/account-linking.ts'];

async function main() {
  await check('S1 signInSetupWarnings names each way that is off by its variables, and a Google sign-in client that is the calendar\'s; never a value; SIGN_IN_ENV is the five variables the sign-in code reads, and its secrets match the console scrubber', async () => {
    const mod = (await import(path.join(ROOT, 'src/lib/startup-checks.ts'))) as Row;
    assert(typeof mod.signInSetupWarnings === 'function', 'startup-checks exports no signInSetupWarnings');
    const names = (mod.SIGN_IN_ENV as { way: string; names: string[] }[]).flatMap((w) => w.names);
    assert(show(names) === show(FIVE), `SIGN_IN_ENV names ${show(names)}`);
    const all = { TELEGRAM_LOGIN_CLIENT_ID: '8000000001', TELEGRAM_LOGIN_CLIENT_SECRET: 'VALUE-TGL-1', GOOGLE_SIGNIN_CLIENT_ID: 'VALUE-GSI-id', GOOGLE_SIGNIN_CLIENT_SECRET: 'VALUE-GSI-2', RESEND_API_KEY: 'VALUE-RES-3', GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID: 'VALUE-CAL-id' };
    const cases: [string, Record<string, string | undefined>, string[]][] = [
      ['all set', all, []],
      ['none set', {}, ALL_OFF],
      ['all empty', Object.fromEntries(FIVE.map((n) => [n, ''])), ALL_OFF],
      ['only the Telegram secret missing', { ...all, TELEGRAM_LOGIN_CLIENT_SECRET: undefined }, ['web sign-in with Telegram is off: TELEGRAM_LOGIN_CLIENT_SECRET is not set']],
      ['Google sign-in on the calendar client', { ...all, GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID: 'VALUE-GSI-id' }, ['web sign-in with Google is off: GOOGLE_SIGNIN_CLIENT_ID is the calendar client GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID; give sign-in its own Web client']],
    ];
    const problems: string[] = [];
    for (const [label, env, want] of cases) {
      const got = mod.signInSetupWarnings(env);
      if (show(got) !== show(want)) problems.push(`${label}: ${show(got)}`);
      if (/VALUE-|8000000001/.test(show(got))) problems.push(`${label}: a value in ${show(got)}`);
    }
    // The names the sign-in code reads: a renamed variable here would warn about one nobody reads
    const code = read('src/services/web-signin/oidc.ts') + read('src/services/web-signin/email-send.ts');
    for (const name of FIVE) if (!code.includes(`process.env.${name}`)) problems.push(`the sign-in code never reads process.env.${name}`);
    const pattern = /const SECRET_NAME = \/(.+)\/i;/.exec(read('src/lib/console-scrub.ts'))?.[1];
    assert(pattern, 'no SECRET_NAME in src/lib/console-scrub.ts');
    for (const name of FIVE.filter((n) => !n.endsWith('_CLIENT_ID'))) if (!new RegExp(pattern, 'i').test(name)) problems.push(`${name} does not match the console scrubber's SECRET_NAME`);
    assert(problems.length === 0, problems.join('; '));
  });

  await check('S2 the README\'s env table has a row for each of the five and a Web sign-in section with both callbacks; .env.example a commented placeholder for each; CLAUDE.md the sign-in rule; only the files the rule names touch SignInIdentity', () => {
    const readme = read('README.md');
    const example = read('.env.example').split('\n');
    const problems: string[] = [];
    for (const name of FIVE) {
      if (!new RegExp(`^\\|[^\\n]*\`${name}\``, 'm').test(readme)) problems.push(`README's table has no ${name} row`);
      const line = example.find((l) => l.startsWith(`# ${name}=`));
      if (!line || !/^# [A-Z_]+=your_[a-z_]+_here$/.test(line)) problems.push(`.env.example has no commented placeholder for ${name}`);
      if (example.some((l) => l.startsWith(`${name}=`))) problems.push(`.env.example sets ${name} uncommented`);
    }
    if (!/^### Web sign-in$/m.test(readme)) problems.push('README has no "### Web sign-in" section');
    for (const url of ['https://famcal.bot/api/auth/telegram/callback', 'https://famcal.bot/api/auth/google/callback']) if (!readme.includes(url)) problems.push(`README does not name ${url}`);
    const rule = read('CLAUDE.md').split('\n').find((l) => l.startsWith('- Every web sign-in'));
    if (!rule) problems.push('CLAUDE.md has no "- Every web sign-in" rule');
    else for (const word of ['`finishSignIn`', ...SIGNIN_IDENTITY_FILES.map((f) => path.basename(f)), 'sessionsValidAfter', '`matchCalendarAccount`', '(never `sub`)']) if (!rule.includes(word)) problems.push(`the CLAUDE.md rule does not name ${word}`);
    // The rule's file list, held: no other file reads or writes SignInIdentity rows
    const walk = (dir: string): string[] =>
      fs.readdirSync(path.join(ROOT, dir), { withFileTypes: true }).flatMap((e) => {
        const rel = `${dir}/${e.name}`;
        if (e.isDirectory()) return e.name === 'node_modules' ? [] : walk(rel);
        return /\.tsx?$/.test(e.name) ? [rel] : [];
      });
    const touching = ['src', 'app', 'components'].flatMap(walk).filter((rel) => /\.signInIdentity\b/.test(read(rel)));
    const stray = touching.filter((rel) => !SIGNIN_IDENTITY_FILES.includes(rel));
    if (stray.length > 0) problems.push(`SignInIdentity rows touched outside the rule's files: ${show(stray)}`);
    if (!touching.includes(SIGNIN_IDENTITY_FILES[0])) problems.push(`identities.ts touches no SignInIdentity row (the walk found ${show(touching)})`);
    assert(problems.length === 0, problems.join('; '));
  });

  let failed = 0;
  for (const r of results) {
    console.log(`${r.ok ? 'OK' : 'FAIL'}  ${r.name}${r.ok ? '' : ` — ${r.reason}`}`);
    if (!r.ok) failed++;
  }
  console.log(`\n${results.length - failed}/${results.length} passed`);
  process.exit(failed ? 1 : 0);
}

main().catch((err) => {
  console.error(err);
  process.exit(1);
});
```

```ts
/**
 * The web sign-in ways and the variables each one needs (web sign-in spec §6). The owner sets them after the deploy,
 * and a way stays hidden until its own are set (oidc.ts's providerConfigured, email-send.ts's emailConfigured), so an
 * unset one is a warning (signInSetupWarnings), never a StartupProblem: no Sentry capture, not "missing" in the deploy
 * message.
 */
export const SIGN_IN_ENV: readonly { way: string; names: readonly string[] }[] = [
  { way: 'Telegram', names: ['TELEGRAM_LOGIN_CLIENT_ID', 'TELEGRAM_LOGIN_CLIENT_SECRET'] },
  { way: 'Google', names: ['GOOGLE_SIGNIN_CLIENT_ID', 'GOOGLE_SIGNIN_CLIENT_SECRET'] },
  { way: 'an email code', names: ['RESEND_API_KEY'] },
];

/**
 * One line per web sign-in way that is off, naming its unset variables (never a value), and one for a Google sign-in
 * client that is the calendar client (oidc.ts keeps that way off: a calendar-client token must never sign anyone in).
 * Pure: env in, lines out.
 */
export function signInSetupWarnings(env: Record<string, string | undefined>): string[] {
  const warnings: string[] = [];
  for (const { way, names } of SIGN_IN_ENV) {
    const unset = names.filter((name) => !env[name]);
    if (unset.length > 0) warnings.push(`web sign-in with ${way} is off: ${unset.join(' and ')} ${unset.length > 1 ? 'are' : 'is'} not set`);
  }
  if (env.GOOGLE_SIGNIN_CLIENT_ID && env.GOOGLE_SIGNIN_CLIENT_SECRET && env.GOOGLE_SIGNIN_CLIENT_ID === env.GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID) {
    warnings.push('web sign-in with Google is off: GOOGLE_SIGNIN_CLIENT_ID is the calendar client GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID; give sign-in its own Web client');
  }
  return warnings;
}
```

Before `### Install & run` (`:113-115`). Before:
```md
To roll back, swap the two values: the sweep converts back. The sweep stops reading the database until the next deploy once SAFE is logged, or, with no `ENCRYPTION_KEY_PREVIOUS`, once nothing is left to encrypt. That way Neon can still scale to zero.
```

After:
````md
To roll back, swap the two values: the sweep converts back. The sweep stops reading the database until the next deploy once SAFE is logged, or, with no `ENCRYPTION_KEY_PREVIOUS`, once nothing is left to encrypt. That way Neon can still scale to zero.

### Web sign-in

An existing account signs in on famcal.bot at `/signin` with Telegram, Google or a 6-digit email code, and gets the same web app as the Mini App (spec `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-02-web-sign-in-design.md`). The web makes no accounts: a person starts FamCal in Telegram or WhatsApp, then adds Google or an email address under Settings → Sign in on the web. The Google account a person's Google Calendar is connected from signs in without being added: FamCal keeps a keyed hash of its address (never the address) and confirms it live with Google at sign-in.

- **Telegram:** OpenID Connect through `openid-client`; the account is found by the token's Telegram `id`, never its `sub`.
- **Google:** a Web client of its own (`openid email`); the account is found by Google's `sub`, never by the address.
- **Email:** a code mailed through Resend from `FamCal <signin@famcal.bot>` to the address stored on the account, with limits per address, per IP and per day in Upstash.

Every way, the WhatsApp link too, ends in `finishSignIn` (`src/lib/web-session.ts`), which refuses a suspended or banned account and sets `__Host-famcal_session`: 30 days, renewed by `/api/page-data` while the web app is used; a WhatsApp link's session lasts 24 hours and is never renewed. Sign out on all devices, removing a way, a suspension and a ban end every session by moving `User.sessionsValidAfter`. Each way stays hidden until its variables are set, and production startup logs `[startup] web sign-in with … is off` for each one that isn't.

One-time setup:

1. **Telegram:** @BotFather → the bot → Login Widget → Switch to OpenID Connect Login; redirect URI `https://famcal.bot/api/auth/telegram/callback`, trusted origin `https://famcal.bot`. Its Client ID and Client Secret go in `TELEGRAM_LOGIN_CLIENT_ID` and `TELEGRAM_LOGIN_CLIENT_SECRET`.
2. **Google:** Google Auth Platform (the Calendar's project) → Clients → Create client → Web application "FamCal sign-in", redirect URI `https://famcal.bot/api/auth/google/callback`. Its ID and secret go in `GOOGLE_SIGNIN_CLIENT_ID` and `GOOGLE_SIGNIN_CLIENT_SECRET`; never the Calendar client's.
3. **Resend:** add the domain `famcal.bot` in region eu-west-1 and let it write its records to Cloudflare (`send.famcal.bot` MX and SPF, `resend._domainkey` DKIM). The apex MX and SPF stay Cloudflare Email Routing's, so mail to privacy@famcal.bot keeps arriving, and Resend's Receiving stays off. An API key with sending access to famcal.bot goes in `RESEND_API_KEY`.

### Install & run
````

- [ ] **Step 3: The `x-real-ip` check (spec §5), run by Claude when the owner says "set"**

Spec §5 says one real request must confirm that Railway sets `x-real-ip` and overwrites a value the client sends, because every sign-in limit counts per `x-real-ip` (`clientAddress`, part B). It needs `RESEND_API_KEY` to be set (the request route answers 503 before), so it runs after the owner's "set" and before the owner is told to try the email way. It sends 25 code requests, each with a different client-supplied `x-real-ip` and a different address that has no account (so nothing is mailed and no per-email limit can interfere); the per-IP limit is 20 code requests an hour.

```bash
for n in $(seq 1 25); do
  curl -s -o /dev/null -w "$n %{http_code}\n" \
    -H 'Origin: https://famcal.bot' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -H "x-real-ip: 203.0.113.$((n + 10))" \
    -d "{\"email\":\"probe${n}@example.com\",\"locale\":\"en\"}" \
    https://famcal.bot/api/auth/email/request
done
```

Expected: all 25 lines end in `200` (the route answers `{ ok: true }` for every address, held back or not). Then read the Railway log for the last two minutes (`railway logs` from the repo, if the CLI is linked; otherwise ask the owner to paste the lines containing `[signin-limits]` from Railway > Deployments > View logs) and count the lines `[signin-limits] code request refused: ip-hour`:

- **5 lines (requests 21 to 25), and no `a request came with no x-real-ip` line:** Railway overwrites the header with the real client address, so all 25 counted as one address. The limits work. Tell the owner to try the email way, and to wait an hour first if they will try it from this network (this machine's address is now at its hourly limit).
- **0 lines:** Railway passes the client's `x-real-ip` through, so anyone could dodge every limit by changing the header. Do not tell the owner the email way is safe. Move `clientAddress` (`src/services/web-signin/client-address.ts`) to the header Railway does set, in a fix of its own, before anything else.
- **A `a request came with no x-real-ip` line:** Railway drops the header, so all requests share one count (20 an hour for everyone). That fails closed. Tell the owner, and decide with them whether to read another header.
